# 牛津习语词典


6957 条习语。例句 4749 条用原书原文，其余原书那句被 OCR 毁了，退回自拟并标「（自拟）」。


常用 / 口语：★ 一颗，☆ 半颗，五颗为满。常用 = 在当代英语里有多常见；口语 = 多大程度上属于口头表达。


<table>
<thead><tr><th>习语</th><th>中文解释</th><th>常用 / 口语</th><th>例句</th></tr></thead>
<tr class="sec"><td colspan="4">A</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from A to ˈB</b></td><td>从一处到另一处</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I don't care what kind of car it is as long as it gets me from A to B.<br>我倒不在乎是什么样的车，只要能把我从一处载到另一处就可以了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from A to ˈZ</b></td><td>从头至尾；详尽彻底地</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We need an expert who knows the subject from A to Z.<br>我们需要一位精通这门学科的专家。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be taken aˈback (by sb/sth)</b></td><td>大吃一惊；被吓一跳</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She completely was taken aback by his anger.<br>他勃然大怒，把她吓了一大跳。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be about to do sth</b></td><td>正要做某事；即将做某事</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I was about to phone him when he walked into the room.<br>我正要给他打电话，他进屋了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>how/what about...?</b></td><td>（询问情况或提出建议）怎么样</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>How about Ruth? Have you heard from her?<br>露丝怎么样了？你有她的消息吗？。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>how/what about ˈthat (, then)? (informal)</b></td><td>（表示惊讶或赞叹）是吗；太妙了</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>She got the scholarship on her first try — how about that, then!<br>她第一次申请就拿到奖学金了，你说妙不妙！（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not be about to do sth</b></td><td>不愿做某事；无意做某事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I've never done any cooking and I'm not about to start now.<br>我从没做过饭，现在也不打算做。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>that's about ˈall/it</b></td><td>就这些；没别的要说了</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Milk, bread, a bag of rice — that's about it for the shopping list.<br>牛奶、面包、一袋米，购物清单就这些了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>above ˈall (ˈelse)</b></td><td>尤其是；最重要的是</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Don't spend too much, don't forget to write, but above all, have a good time!<br>别花太多钱，别忘了写信，最重要的是，要玩得开心!。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>aˌbove and beˈyond sth (formal)</b></td><td>超越（职责等）；不止于</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>They showed commitment to the job above and beyond what was expected of them.<br>他们的敬业精神超乎人们对他们的期望。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/get aˈbove yourself (disapproving)</b></td><td>自命不凡；狂妄自大</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She's getting a bit above herself. She's only been working for me for two weeks and already she's telling me what to do!<br>她也有点太自负了， 才为我工作了两个星期，就开始对我指手画脚!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep aˈbreast of sth</b></td><td>了解…的最新情况；跟上…的发展</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>It is almost impossible to keep abreast of all the latest developments in computing.<br>要跟上计算机领域所有最新的发展几乎是不可能的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌabsence makes the heart grow ˈfonder (saying)</b></td><td>离别情更浓；小别胜新婚</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>They text all day now he's abroad — absence makes the heart grow fonder.<br>他出国后两人整天发消息，真是小别胜新婚。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leave of ˈabsence (formal)</b></td><td>准假；休假</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>He asked for three months' leave of absence to look after his sick father.<br>他申请了三个月假期去照顾生病的父亲。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>by ˈaccident</b></td><td>偶然；意外地</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We met by accident at the airport.<br>我</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(whether) by ˌaccident or deˈsign</b></td><td>不论是偶然还是有意</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Whether by accident or design, his email went to the whole company.<br>不管是无心还是有意，他那封邮件发给了全公司。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>acciˌdentally on ˈpurpose (informal, ironic)</b></td><td>故作意外地；假装无意地</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She accidentally on purpose left her number on his desk.<br>她故作无意地把电话号码留在了他桌上。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>accidents will ˈhappen (saying)</b></td><td>意外总是难免的</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Don't cry over the broken vase, sweetheart — accidents will happen.<br>别为打碎的花瓶哭了，宝贝，意外总是难免的。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>of your own acˈcord</b></td><td>自愿地；主动地</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I didn' need to tell her to apologize; she did it of her own accord.<br>不需要我告诉她，她主动道歉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>of little/no acˈcount (formal)</b></td><td>无关紧要；无足轻重</td><td>★★<br>★</td><td>His past achievements were of no account when it came to competing with the younger men.<br>要说跟较年轻的人竞争，他过去的成绩就不值一提了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on ˈno account •not on ˈany account</b></td><td>决不；无论如何都不</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>On no account should you open that door while the machine is running.<br>机器运转时你决不能打开那扇门。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on your own acˈcount</b></td><td>为自己；自行负责地</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>She quit the agency and started trading on her own account last spring.<br>去年春天她离开中介，开始自己单干做买卖。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put/turn sth to good acˈcount (formal)</b></td><td>充分利用（金钱、才能等）</td><td>★<br>★</td><td>He put his years in the kitchen to good account when he wrote the book.<br>写这本书时，他把多年的厨房经验用了个够。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take sth into acˈcount •take account of sth</b></td><td>考虑到；把…考虑在内</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We must take rising prices into account when we plan next year's budget.<br>做明年预算时我们一定要把物价上涨考虑进去。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>there's no accounting for ˈtaste(s) (saying)</b></td><td>人各有所好；好恶无从解释</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He put ketchup on his noodles — well, there's no accounting for taste.<br>他往面条上浇番茄酱，唉，人各有所好吧。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>by/from ˈall accounts</b></td><td>据大家所说；据说</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Tve never seen any of her moves, but she's a brilliant director, by all accounts.<br>我从未看过她的电影，不过大冢都说她是个才华横溢的导演。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>play your ˈace</b></td><td>打出王牌；使出绝招</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>I think it's time we played our ace, which is the fact that without us they wouldn't be able to run this place.<br>我认为该是打出我们王牌的时候了:没有我们他们管理不了这里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>within an ace of sth/of doing sth (BrE)</b></td><td>差一点儿；几乎</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>We came within an ace of victory.<br>我们距胜利只有一步之遥。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have/hold (all) the ˈaces (also hold all the ˈcards)</b></td><td>握有王牌；占绝对优势</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The Labour Party candidate holds all the aces — he's local and well liked.<br>工觉候选人占尽优势:他是本地人，而且深受公众喜爱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>an/sb's Achilles' ˈheel</b></td><td>致命弱点；阿喀琉斯之踵</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Hus pride proved to be his Achilles' heel.<br>狂妄自大成了他的致命弱点。 ③</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˌacid ˈtest (of sth) (also the ˈlitmus test especially in AmE)</b></td><td>决定性的考验；试金石</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Theyve always been good frends, but the acid test will come when they have to share a flat.<br>他们一直是好朋友，可是两个人必须合住一套公寓，真正的考验快要到了。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make sb's acˈquaintance •make the acˈquaintance of sb</b></td><td>结识某人；与某人初次相见</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Iam delighted to make your acquaintance, Mrs Baker.<br>贝克夫人，很高兴认识您。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>an acquired ˈtaste</b></td><td>逐渐培养出来的爱好</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Whisky is an acquired taste.<br>威士忌酒要喝惯了才会喜欢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>an ˌact of ˈGod (law)</b></td><td>天灾；不可抗力</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The insurance covers Your house against ail types of damage, excluding those caused by acts of God.<br>这份保险单承保房屋可能受到的各种损坏，但不包括自然灾害造成的损害。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈbalancing/juggling act</b></td><td>搞平衡；两头兼顾</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The UN must perform a delicate balancing act between the different sides involved in the conflict.<br>联合国必须在冲突各方之间寻求微妙的平衡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/get in on the ˈact (informal)</b></td><td>（在他人成功后）插一手；参与分羹</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Once the café took off, every landlord wanted to get in on the act.<br>咖啡馆一火，每个房东都想来插一脚。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈvanishing act (informal)</b></td><td>（需要时）消失不见；找不到人</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He pulled his usual vanishing act the moment the bill arrived.<br>账单一送来，他又照例玩起了人间蒸发。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get your ˈact together •get sth/it toˈgether (informal) (also get/have your ˈshit together, ◆ slang)</b></td><td>振作起来；把事情安排妥当</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You need to get your act together before the exams start next month.<br>下个月考试前你得好好振作起来。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a hard/tough act to ˈfollow</b></td><td>难以超越的人（或事）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The last head teacher achieved a lot - shell be a hard act to follow.<br>前任校长成就卓著，接替者将难以望其项背。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈaction stations (spoken, especially BrE)</b></td><td>（下令准备行动）各就各位</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Action stations, everyone — the inspectors will be here in ten minutes!<br>各就各位，各位，检查员十分钟后就到！（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in ˈaction</b></td><td>在工作；在运转；活动中</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>John's a great cook - you should see him in action.<br>约翰的厨艺了不起，你应该看看他做饭的样子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>out of ˈaction</b></td><td>（因伤病）不能工作；（因损坏）失灵</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Jane's broken leg will put her out of action for a while.<br>简的腿骨折了，她这一段时间将不能工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a piece/slice of the ˈaction (informal)</b></td><td>（利益的）一份；一杯羹</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Foreign firms will all want a piece of the action if the new airport goes ahead.<br>新机场倘若能开建，外国公司都会想分得一杯羹。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>where the ˈaction is</b></td><td>热闹之处；活动中心</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I'd hate to live out in the country —Ilike to be where the action is.<br>我不愿意住在乡下，我喜欢热闹的地方。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ad ˈhoc (from Latin)</b></td><td>临时的；特设的；专门的</td><td>★★★★<br>★★</td><td>They set up an ad hoc committee to deal with the parking complaints.<br>他们成立了一个临时委员会处理停车投诉。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ad infiˈnitum (from Latin)</b></td><td>无休止地；反复不停地</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>You cannot stay here ad infinitum without paying any rent.<br>你不能一分钱房租也不付一直住在这里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ad ˈnauseam (from Latin)</b></td><td>（因重复而）令人厌烦地</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The coach discussed our defensive mistakes ad nauseam after the match.<br>赛后教练把我们的防守失误说得人耳朵起茧。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>add ˌfuel to the ˈfire/ˈflames</b></td><td>火上浇油</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She was already furious and his apologies and excuses only added fuel to the flames.<br>她本来就怒不可遏，他的道歉和解释只能是火上浇油。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pour oil on troubled ˈwater(s)</b></td><td>平息争端；调解纠纷</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Grandma poured oil on troubled waters by changing the subject quickly.<br>奶奶赶紧换了话题，把这场争吵平息了下去。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>add ˌinsult to ˈinjury</b></td><td>雪上加霜；伤害之外又加侮辱</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She forgot to send me an invitation to her party and then added insult to injury by asking to borrow my jacket!<br>她忘了邀请我参加她的聚会，更气人的是，还要向我借夹克衫!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>without further/more aˈdo (old-fashioned)</b></td><td>立即；干脆地；不再耽搁</td><td>★★<br>★</td><td>Without further ado, let me introduce tonight's very special guest.<br>闲话少说，我来介绍今晚这位特别嘉宾。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in adˈvance (of sth)</b></td><td>预先；事先</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>You have to book the tickets at least two weeks in advance.<br>票必须至少提前两周订。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take adˈvantage of sth/sb</b></td><td>利用某机会；占某人便宜</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We made sure that we took full advantage of the hotel facilities.<br>我们确保已充分享用了酒店的设施。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to sb's adˈvantage</b></td><td>对某人有利</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The rise in the value of the pound will work to the advantage of those planning a trip abroad this summer.<br>英镑升值对计划今年夏天出国的人有利。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to (good, better, etc.) adˈvantage</b></td><td>有效地；更出色地</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>You would be spending your time to better advantage if you did what I suggested.<br>你要是按我的建议去做，你的时间会得到更有效的利用。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turn sth to your (own) adˈvantage</b></td><td>转害为利；为己所用</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>She had three rooms in the house after her children left home, so she decided to turn this to her advantage and rent them out to students.<br>她的几个孩子长大离家以后，房子里空出来三个房间，所以她打算充分利用，把它们租给学生。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>far/farther/further aˈfield</b></td><td>在远处；到远方</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>You can hire a car if you want to explore further afield.<br>你要是还想游览更远的地方，可以租辆车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I'm afraid (that)... (spoken)</b></td><td>（礼貌地表歉意）恐怕；很遗憾</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I'm afraid I can't come to your party.<br>很遗憾，我不能参加你们的聚会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>after ˈall</b></td><td>毕竟；终究；还是</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I think I will have something to eat after all.<br>我想我还是吃点东西吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>aˌgain and aˈgain</b></td><td>一再；反复地；屡次</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Tve told him again and again to shut the door but he always leaves it open.<br>我三番五次告诉他要把门关上，可是他总是不关。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>then/there aˈgain (informal)</b></td><td>另一方面；话说回来</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Ithought he liked me, but then again maybe he didn'.<br>我觉得他喜欢我，但也许他并不喜欢我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌact/ˌbe your ˈage (informal)</b></td><td>别孩子气；举止要与年龄相称</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You're behaving like a couple of kids.Act your age!<br>你俩表现得像小孩一样，要懂事点!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌcome of ˈage</b></td><td>成年；达到法定年龄；发展成熟</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He will inherit his father's money when he comes of age.<br>他成年后将会继承父亲的财产。 2 (</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌlook your ˈage</b></td><td>看上去与年龄相称</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I was surprised when I last saw her — she's really starting to look her age now.<br>最近一次看到她时我很吃惊，她现在真的开始显老了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌunderˈage</b></td><td>未成年；未到法定年龄</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We don't serve alcohol to teenagers who are under age/to under-age teenagers.<br>我们不卖酒给未成年人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on ˈaggregate (BrE, sport)</b></td><td>按（比赛）总比分</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>They won 4-2 on aggregare.<br>他们以 4:2 的总分获胜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>aˌgree to ˈdiffer</b></td><td>各自保留意见；同意存异</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Our views on this matter are so different that we ll just have to agree to difer.<br>我们在这一问题上的看法分歧很大，看来大家只能保留各自的意见了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I ˌcouldn't agree (with you) ˈmore</b></td><td>我完全同意</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I couldn't agree with you more about the need to hire extra staff.<br>在需要雇用更多员工的问题上，我与你的意见完全一致。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in aid of sb/sth (BrE)</b></td><td>为支援（或帮助）某人（某事）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The children spent the day collecting money in aid of charity.<br>孩子们一整天都在为慈善事业募捐。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>what's (all) ˈthis, etc. in aid of? (BrE, spoken)</b></td><td>这究竟是为什么；这有什么用</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>What's all this crying in aid of?<br>这样号啕大哭到底是怎么了？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take ˈaim at sb/sth (AmE)</b></td><td>把矛头指向；集中批评</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The unions are taking aim at the government.<br>工会组织正把矛头指向政府。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>anything ˈgoes</b></td><td>怎么都行；没有任何规矩</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>John always has to wear a suit and tie to the office, but where I work anygoes.<br>约翰上班必须穿西装打领带，而我上</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>(as) easy, clear, quick, etc. as ˈanything</b></td><td>极其容易（或清楚、迅速等）</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It was only a small gift but Phil was as pleased as anything with it.<br>只是一件小礼物，可是菲尔高兴得跟什么似的。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>not for ˈanything (informal)</b></td><td>决不；无论如何也不</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I wouldn't give it up for anything.<br>我决不放弃。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>make no aˈpology/aˈpologies for sth</b></td><td>不为某事道歉；问心无愧</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Having grown up in the north of the country, Imake no apologies for saying that people there are more friendly than people in the south.<br>我在北方长大，我打心底里觉得北方人比南方人友好。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>in apple-pie ˈorder</b></td><td>井井有条；整整齐齐</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She keeps the accounts in apple-pie order.<br>她</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>the best of ˈluck (to sb) (old-fashioned, informal, often ironic)</b></td><td>祝你好运（多含反语，暗指难成）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The four of you are going to live in that tiny apartment? The best of luck to you!<br>你们四个人打算住在那样一个小公寓里吗？祝你们好运!</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>a ˌbird of ˈpassage</b></td><td>漂泊不定的人；过客</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>He's a bird of passage who never stays in one city long.<br>他是个漂泊不定的人，从不在一个城市久留。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flip/give/shoot sb the ˈbird (AmE, slang)</b></td><td>冲某人竖中指（表示侮辱）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>The driver gave me the bird when I honked at the traffic lights.<br>我在红灯处按喇叭，那司机冲我竖了中指。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the birds and the ˈbees (old-fashioned or humorous)</b></td><td>基本的性知识</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Now that Jamie is eleven, isn't it time you told him about the birds and the bees?<br>杰米已经十一岁了，现在是不是该给他讲讲基本的性知识了？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>birds of a ˈfeather (flock toˈgether) (saying)</b></td><td>物以类聚，人以群分</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Those two are always plotting together — birds of a feather, I suppose.<br>那俩人总凑一块儿谋划，真是物以类聚。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give ˈbirth (to sb/sth)</b></td><td>生孩子；产生（新事物）</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She gave birth to twin boys in the back of a taxi.<br>她在出租车后座生下了一对双胞胎男孩。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr class="sec"><td colspan="4">B</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the (whole) ... ˈbit (informal, disapproving)</b></td><td>一整套典型做派（或说辞）</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He gave us the whole struggling-artist bit again over dinner.<br>晚饭时他又把那套穷困艺术家的说辞搬了出来。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>a bit of ˈrough (BrE, slang)</b></td><td>（社会地位低的）粗野情人</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>She told her friends she rather fancied a bit of rough.<br>她跟朋友说，她还挺喜欢粗野型的男人。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not a ˈbit • not one (little) ˈbit</b></td><td>一点也不；毫不</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I'm not a bit surprised that he forgot to call again.<br>他又忘了打电话，我一点都不意外。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not a ˈbit of it! (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>根本不是那样；压根儿没有</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You'd think he'd be tired after the journey but not a bit of it!<br>你可能以为他旅行之后会疲劳，但根本不是那样!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a bite at/of the ˈcherry (BrE)</b></td><td>做某事的机会</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Everyone deserves a bite at the cherry before the jobs are filled.<br>职位定下来之前，每个人都该有一次机会。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a second/another bite at/of the ˈcherry (BrE)</b></td><td>第二次机会；再来一次的机会</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>They all wanted a bite of the cherry.<br>他们都想得到这个机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bite the ˈbig one (AmE, slang)</b></td><td>糟透了；失败</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>This place really bites the big one!<br>这个地方糟糕透了! 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bite the ˈbullet (informal)</b></td><td>咬紧牙关应付；硬着头皮做</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Getting your car repaired is often an expensive business, but all you can do is bite the bullet and pay up.<br>修车往往是一件很花钱的事，可是你只能咬紧牙关付账单。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bite the ˈdust (informal)</b></td><td>失败；完蛋；被摧毁</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Thousands of small businesses bite the dust every year.<br>每年有数以千计的小企业倒闭。 2 (</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bite the hand that ˈfeeds you</b></td><td>恩将仇报；以怨报德</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>When you say such nasty things about the organization, you're biting the hand that feeds you.<br>你这样恶语中伤组织是忘恩负义。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bite your ˈlip</b></td><td>咬住嘴唇忍住不说（或不哭）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She bit her lip and said nothing when he took all the credit.<br>他把功劳全揽走时，她咬着嘴唇一句话没说。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bite your ˈnails/fingernails</b></td><td>焦虑不安地咬指甲</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>What an exciting movie that was — real nail-biting stuff!<br>那部电影真刺激，着实令人神经紧张!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bite off ˌmore than you can ˈchew (informal)</b></td><td>不自量力；贪多嚼不烂</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He's promised to get all this work finished by the weekend but I've got a feeling he's bitten off more than he can chew.<br>他保证周末前完成所有的活儿，可是我觉得他有点不自量力。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bite your ˈtongue</b></td><td>忍住不说；把话咽回去</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I didn't believe her explanation but I bit my tongue.<br>我不相信她的解释，可是我忍住没有说出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I, etc. won't ˈbite (you) (humorous)</b></td><td>我又不会吃了你</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You should tell your teacher that you don't understand — she won't bite you!<br>你应该告诉老师你不懂，她又不会吃了你!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the biter ˈbit</b></td><td>害人反害己；作法自毙</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>The biter bit: his own prank ended up soaking him instead.<br>作法自毙，他自己的恶作剧最后把他淋了个透。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bits and ˈpieces (also ˌbits and ˈbobs BrE)</b></td><td>零星物品；零七八碎</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I keep bits and pieces of old jewellery in this biscuit tin.<br>我把零星的旧首饰都放在这个饼干盒里。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a bitter ˈpill (for sb) (to swallow)</b></td><td>难以接受的苦果</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Losing the final at home was a bitter pill for the fans to swallow.<br>在主场输掉决赛，对球迷来说是难以下咽的苦果。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to the bitter ˈend</b></td><td>坚持到底；一直到最后</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Now that we have begun this project, we must see it through to the bitter end.<br>既然我们已经开始了这个项目，就一定要奋战到底。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>black and ˈblue</b></td><td>青一块紫一块；遍体鳞伤</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He fell off his bike and his knees were black and blue.<br>他从自行车上摔下来，膝盖青一块紫一块。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(in) black and ˈwhite</b></td><td>非黑即白；看问题绝对化</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She sees every issue in black and white, with no middle ground.<br>她看什么问题都非黑即白，没有中间地带。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a black ˈday (for sb)</b></td><td>倒霉的一天；黑暗的日子</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>It was a black day for the town when the factory closed.<br>工厂关闭那天，对这个镇子来说是黑暗的一天。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the black ˈmarket</b></td><td>黑市</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Tickets for the final were selling on the black market for hundreds.<br>决赛的门票在黑市上炒到了好几百。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈblack spot</b></td><td>事故多发地段；问题严重的地方</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>This junction is a notorious black spot for cyclists in winter.<br>这个路口是冬天骑车人出事的著名黑点。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the ˈblack (business)</b></td><td>有盈余；账面不亏损</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The café has finally been in the black for three months running.<br>这家咖啡馆终于连续三个月有盈余了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>he, it, etc. is not as black as he, it, etc. is ˈpainted</b></td><td>不像传闻中那样糟糕</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>The boss is not as black as she's painted; in fact, I find her quite helpful and friendly.<br>女老板并不像人们说的那么坏；实际上，我发现她很热心也很友善。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>look ˈblack</b></td><td>前景暗淡；希望渺茫</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>I know things look black at the moment but I'm sure youll get a job soon.<br>我知道目前看起来希望渺茫，但我敢肯定你会很快找到工作的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be to ˈblame (for sth)</b></td><td>对（坏事）负有责任</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>If anyone's to blame, it's me.<br>如果有人该承担责任，那就是我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>don't blame ˈme (spoken)</b></td><td>别怪我（用于劝阻他人）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Call her, if you like, but don't blame me if she's angry.<br>你想给她打电话就打吧，不过要是她生气可别怪我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I don't ˈblame you/her, etc. (for doing sth)</b></td><td>我不怪你（或她等）；情有可原</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You walked out of the meeting? I don't blame you one bit.<br>你退出了会议？我一点也不怪你。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a blank ˈcheque (BrE) (AmE a blank ˈcheck)</b></td><td>自由处理权；全权委托</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Just because I asked you to speak on my behalf, that didn't mean you had a blank cheque to promise anything you liked.<br>我要你为我代言并不意味着你可以信口开河随意许诺。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌblast from the ˈpast (informal)</b></td><td>勾起回忆的旧人旧事旧物</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>This song is real blast from the past.<br>这绝对是一首经典老歌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blaze a/the ˈtrail</b></td><td>开辟道路；作先驱</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>As the first female Member of Parliament, she blazed a trail for others to follow.<br>作为下院第一位女议员，她为后来者树立了榜样。•'</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>like ˈblazes (old-fashioned, spoken)</b></td><td>猛烈地；飞快地</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>By the time they reached the hotel it was raining like blazes.<br>他们到达酒店时，正下着倾盆大雨。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>bleed sb ˈdry/ˈwhite (disapproving)</b></td><td>榨干某人的钱财</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>He used to be quite wealthy, but his children have bled him dry.<br>他从前很富有，可是都被他的孩子们给榨干了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bless (BrE, spoken, approving)</b></td><td>真可爱；真难为他（表示喜爱）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He made me a birthday card all by himself — bless!<br>他自己给我做了张生日卡，真可爱！（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌbless his, her, etc. (little) cotton ˈsocks (BrE, humorous)</b></td><td>真难为他（她）；太可爱了</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He waited two hours in the rain for me, bless his cotton socks.<br>他在雨里等了我两个小时，真是难为他了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈbless you</b></td><td>上帝保佑你（他人打喷嚏时说）</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>"Atishoo!" "Bless you — there's a box of tissues on the table."<br>“阿嚏！”“上帝保佑你，桌上有纸巾。”（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a blessing in disˈguise</b></td><td>因祸得福；看似祸实是福</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Missing that flight turned out to be a blessing in disguise.<br>没赶上那班飞机，结果是因祸得福。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>a ˌblind ˈdate</b></td><td>相亲；与陌生人的约会</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>My sister set me up on a blind date with her colleague.<br>我姐姐给我安排了和她同事的相亲。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blind ˈdrunk (informal)</b></td><td>烂醉如泥</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He came home blind drunk and fell asleep on the stairs.<br>他烂醉如泥地回到家，睡在了楼梯上。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blind sb with ˈscience</b></td><td>用专业术语把人唬住</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>The salesman tried to blind us with science instead of quoting a price.<br>推销员净拿专业术语唬人，就是不肯报价。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>in the blink of an ˈeye</b></td><td>一眨眼的工夫；转眼间</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He was gone in the blink of an eye.<br>他一眨眼就不见了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the ˈblink (informal)</b></td><td>（机器）失灵，出毛病</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Can I watch the film at your house? Our TV's on the blink again.<br>我能在你家看那部电影吗？我家的电视又出毛病了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have been around the ˈblock (a few times)</b></td><td>经验丰富；见多识广</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She's been around the block a few tumes and can't be fooled that easily.<br>她见多识广，不是那么容易上当受骗的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put/lay your head/neck on the ˈblock</b></td><td>甘冒风险；把自己置于受责难之地</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The government laid its head on the block and said that if it loses this vote in Parliament tonight it will call an election.<br>政府冒风险称，如果在议会今晚的投票中失利的话将要求举行选举。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bad ˈblood (between A and B) (old-fashioned)</b></td><td>积怨；仇恨</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>There has always been bad blood between the two families.<br>这两家人之间有宿仇。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be after/out for sb's ˈblood (informal, often humorous)</b></td><td>想报复某人；找某人算账</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>They have been after my blood ever since I accidentally damaged their car.<br>自从我无意间弄坏了他们的车，他们一直想报复我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blood and ˈguts (informal)</b></td><td>血腥暴力场面</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Audiences seem to prefer movles with romance and humour rather than the blood and guts stuf.<br>观众似乎更喜欢浪漫和搞笑的电影，而不是那些血腥暴力的镜头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blood and ˈthunder (informal)</b></td><td>耸人听闻的煽情场面</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Idon't like blood-and-thunder novels.<br>我不喜欢充满刺激恐怖情节的小说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blood is thicker than ˈwater (saying)</b></td><td>血浓于水；家人总比外人亲</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Tony was angry with his brother for a while, but blood is thicker than water, and in the end he forgave him.<br>托尼一时很生哥哥的气，不过毕竟血浓于水，最后他还是原谅了哥哥。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>your/sb's ˌblood is ˈup (BrE)</b></td><td>怒火中烧；血气上涌</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Normally, he's a quiet man, but when his blood is up he can be very violent.<br>他平时寡言少语，但发起火来可是够厉害的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌblood, sweat and ˈtears</b></td><td>血汗；艰苦付出</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The only way to succeed is through old-fashioned blood, sweat and tears.<br>成功的唯一途径还是老办法:艰苦奋斗。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fresh/new/young ˈblood</b></td><td>新生力量；新鲜血液</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>What this committee really needs is some new blood.<br>该委员会真正需要的是一些新生力量。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have (sb's) ˈblood on your hands</b></td><td>对某人的死负有罪责</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He's a tyrant with the blood of millions of innocent people on his hands.<br>他是一个暴君，双手沾满了千百万无辜者的鲜血。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the/sb's ˈblood/genes</b></td><td>与生俱来；天生如此</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Both his father and his mother were writers, so literature runs in his blood.<br>他的父母都是作家， 所以他骨子里流着文学的血。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>like getting ˌblood out of/from a ˈstone</b></td><td>极难办到；难于登天</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Getting an apology from him was like getting blood out of a stone.<br>让他道歉比登天还难。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make sb's ˈblood boil</b></td><td>使某人怒火中烧</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Seeing him beating that little dog made my blood boil.<br>看到他打那条小狗，我怒不可遏。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make sb's ˈblood run cold • make sb's ˈblood freeze</b></td><td>使人不寒而栗</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>His calm description of the crime made my blood freeze completely.<br>他平静地描述那桩罪行，让我浑身发冷。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>your (own) flesh and ˈblood</b></td><td>亲骨肉；至亲</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You can't turn your back on her; she's your own flesh and blood.<br>你不能不管她，她是你的亲骨肉。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a blot on the ˈlandscape</b></td><td>煞风景的东西（尤指丑陋建筑）</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>That power station is rather a blot on the landscape.<br>那座发电)相当影响景观。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>ˈmind-blowing (adj.)</b></td><td>令人震撼的；极其惊人的</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We were stunned by the mind-blowing scenery on the drive north.<br>北上路上那令人震撼的景色让我们都看呆了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blow sb/sth out of the ˈwater (informal)</b></td><td>彻底击败；证明毫无价值</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Their new phone blows the competition out of the water on price.<br>他们的新手机在价格上把对手打得落花流水。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blow your own ˈtrumpet (especially BrE) (informal)</b></td><td>自吹自擂</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He never stops blowing his own trumpet about that one big sale.<br>他没完没了地吹嘘那一笔大单。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blow/toot your own ˈhorn (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>自吹自擂；自我吹嘘</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I don't like to blow my own trumpet, but the office was much better run when I was in charge.<br>我不喜欢自吹自擂，可是我负责的时候把办公室管理得高效得多。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blow sb/sth ˌsky-ˈhigh (informal)</b></td><td>炸飞；彻底摧毁</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The explosives factory was blown sky-high when one of the workers lit a match.<br>一名工人点了根火柴，炸药厂就全炸毁了。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>blow your ˈtop (BrE) (AmE blow your ˈstack)</b></td><td>大发雷霆；火冒三丈</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>She blew her top when she found the kitchen in that state.<br>她看到厨房那副样子，气得暴跳如雷。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blow up in sb's ˈface</b></td><td>（计划等）突然砸锅、失败</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Starting up the business was difficult, and it all nearly blew up in his face when his partner fell sick at the last minute.<br>创办公司真不容易，而在最后关头他的合伙人病倒了，他差点儿眼睁睁看着一切化为泡影。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blow the ˈwhistle (on sb/sth) (informal)</b></td><td>检举揭发（某人某事）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>One of the police officers blew the whistle on his colleagues when he found out they were taking bribes.<br>一名警察发现自己的同事受贿后检举了他们。 •'</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cushion/soften the ˈblow</b></td><td>缓和打击；减轻冲击</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>When he lost his job he was offered a cash payment to soften the blow.<br>他丢掉工作的时候得到一笔现金作为安慰。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌblow-by-ˌblow acˈcount, deˈscription, etc.</b></td><td>按事情发生顺序的细致描述</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He gave blow-by-blow account of everything he had done that day.<br>他把他那天所干的事情一五一十地告诉了我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>come to ˈblows (over sth)</b></td><td>动武；打起来</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>They were shouting at each other so much that I thought they would come to blows.<br>他们互相大吵，我以为他们会打起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>out of the ˈblue</b></td><td>突然；出乎意料地</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She called me out of the blue after twenty years of silence.<br>沉寂二十年后，她突然给我打来电话。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(do sth) till you're ˌblue in the ˈface</b></td><td>说到口干舌燥（也无济于事）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You can explain till you're blue in the face; he won't listen.<br>你说到口干舌燥也没用，他根本不听。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>your, sb's, etc. ˌblue-eyed ˈboy (informal, disapproving)</b></td><td>红人；宠儿</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Bob is certain to be promoted: he's the manager's blue-eyed boy.<br>鲍勃肯定会得到提拔，他是经理的红人。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>above ˈboard</b></td><td>光明正大；公开合法</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>All my dealings with the company have been completely above board.<br>我和那家公司的所有交易都是光明磊落的。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>(and) Bob's your ˈuncle (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>这就成了；大功告成</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Add the eggs, stir for a minute, and Bob's your uncle.<br>加进鸡蛋，搅一分钟，就大功告成了。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>body and ˈsoul</b></td><td>全身心地；完完全全</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She devoted herself body and soul to this political cause.<br>她全身心地投入到这项政治事业中。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>bolt ˈupright</b></td><td>笔直地（坐起）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The noise woke her suddenly and she sat bolt upright in bed.<br>吵闹声把她突然惊醒，她直挺挺地从床上坐了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make a ˈbolt/ˈdash for it/sth (informal)</b></td><td>拔腿就跑；夺路而逃</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The prisoners made a bolt for it through an open window.<br>那些囚犯从一扇敞开的窗户逃跑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be the ˈbomb (AmE)</b></td><td>特别棒；顶呱呱</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Check out the new website. It's the bomb!<br>看看这个新网站，真是太棒了!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go down a ˈbomb • go (like) a ˈbomb (BrE)</b></td><td>大获成功；十分轰动</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Our performance went down a bomb.<br>我们的演出引起了轰动。></td></tr>
<tr><td><b>your word is your ˈbond</b></td><td>说话算数；一诺千金</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>With him a handshake is enough; his word is his bond.<br>跟他握个手就行了，他说话向来算数。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bone ˈidle (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>懒到极点</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>The family consists of Vera, her intensely irritating husband and her two bone idle sons.<br>这一家子分别是薇拉、她招人烦的老公以及她的两个懒儿子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a bone of conˈtention</b></td><td>争议的焦点</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The interpretation of this painting has long been a bone of contention among art historians.<br>对这幅画的解释长久以来一直是艺术史学家争论不休的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>close to/near the ˈbone (informal)</b></td><td>过于直露；容易伤人</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Some of the things she said to him about his failure to find work were a bit close to the bone.<br>关于他找不到工作的事情，她对他说的有些话太直白了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cut, pare, etc. sth to the ˈbone</b></td><td>削减到最低限度</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The council has cut library funding to the bone this year.<br>今年市政厅把图书馆经费砍到了最低。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a ˈbone to pick with sb (informal)</b></td><td>要跟某人理论；有账要算</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Here, Tve got a bone to pick with you: why did you tell David I wasn't at home when he phoned?<br>听着，我要跟你讲讲理:戴维打电话的时候你为什么告诉他我不在家？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not have a ... ˈbone in your body</b></td><td>全无某种品性</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She was honest and hard-working, and didn't have an unkind bone in her body.<br>她诚实又肯干，为人非常善良。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>throw sb a ˈbone</b></td><td>施以小惠；给点好处</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The boss threw me a bone and let me leave early on Friday.<br>老板给了点甜头，让我周五早走。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make no ˈbones about sth/about doing sth</b></td><td>直言不讳；毫不掩饰</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She made no bones about telling him she wanted a Pay rise.<br>她毫不隐讳地告诉他，她想加新。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bring sb to ˈbook (for sth) (formal, especially BrE)</b></td><td>追究责任；使受惩罚</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>This is just another of the many crimes for which nobody was ever brought to book.<br>许多罪行无人受到惩罚，这是又一案例。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>by the ˈbook</b></td><td>照章办事；循规蹈矩</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He insists on doing everything by the book.<br>他坚持任何事情都要照章行事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in sb's ˈbook (spoken)</b></td><td>依某人看；照某人的观点</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>They took the car away without asking me, and in my book that's theft.<br>他们没有问我一声就把车开走了，依我看这就是盗窃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>throw the ˈbook at sb (informal)</b></td><td>严厉惩处某人；从重发落</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The police stopped me for speeding and threw the book at me for everything - faulty lights, dangerous tyres, no insurance..<br>因为超速警察把我拦了下来，然后给我挑了一大堆毛病: 车灯已坏，轮胎不安全，没上保险…</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>close the ˈbook on sth</b></td><td>结束某事；不再过问</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Police have closed the book on the case after thirty long years.<br>三十年后，警方给这个案子画上了句号。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a closed ˈbook (to sb)</b></td><td>一窍不通的事物；完全陌生的领域</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Quantum physics is a closed book to me; I never got past high school science.<br>量子物理对我来说完全是天书，高中理科我就没学明白。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be in/get into sb's ˈgood/ˈbad books (informal)</b></td><td>得（或失）某人欢心</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Washing his car got me back into my father's good books.<br>给我爸洗了车，我又讨他喜欢了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on/off the/sb's ˈbooks (business)</b></td><td>记（或不记）在正式账目上</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The company falsified its accounts and kept billions of dollars in debt off the books.<br>这家公司做假账，数十亿美元的债务未入账。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>one for the ˈbooks (especially AmE)</b></td><td>值得记上一笔的稀奇事</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Well here's one for the books — a microwave that plays music.<br>哟， 这东西可非同寻常—能播放音乐的微波炉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the boot is on the other ˈfoot (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>情况反过来了；此一时彼一时</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Now that she's the manager, the boot is on the other foot.<br>现在她当了经理，情况可反过来了。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>give sb/get the ˈboot (informal)</b></td><td>解雇；被炒鱿鱼</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He got the boot for stealing money from the firm.<br>他因偷公司的钱被解雇了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put/stick the ˈboot in (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>落井下石；猛踢倒地者</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>She was upset about losing her job and then her sister started putting the boot in, telling her she was lazy.<br>她丢了工作很心烦，这时她姐姐又在伤口上撒盐，说她太懒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to ˈboot (old-fashioned or humorous)</b></td><td>此外；而且还</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She has a big house, an expensive car, and a noliday villa in to boot.<br>她有一座大房子、一辆豪华车，另</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>drag/pull yourself up by your (own) ˈbootstraps (informal)</b></td><td>自力更生；白手起家</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Nobody helped her get where she is today — she pulled herself up by her own bootstraps.<br>她取得今天的成就没有靠他人帮忙，而是全靠自己的努力。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bore sb to ˈtears • bore sb ˈstiff (informal)</b></td><td>使某人厌烦透顶</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>His holiday photos bored us to tears for a solid hour.<br>他的度假照片让我们整整烦了一个小时。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>not have a cat in ˈhell's chance (also not have a ˈdog's chance) (informal)</b></td><td>毫无机会；一点希望也没有</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You haven't got a cat in hell's chance of buying a decent car for that amount.<br>那点钱根本就不可能买到一辆像样的车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>when the cat's aˈway the mice will ˈplay (saying)</b></td><td>猫儿不在，鼠儿造反</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The teacher stepped out and chaos erupted: when the cat's away the mice will play.<br>老师一出门就乱成一锅粥，真是猫儿不在鼠儿造反。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch your ˈdeath (of cold) (old-fashioned, informal)</b></td><td>得重感冒</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Don't go out without your coat - you'll catch your death.<br>别不穿外套就出门，你会感冒的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch sb's ˈeye</b></td><td>引起某人注意；吸引某人目光</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>A red dress in the window caught my eye as we walked past.<br>路过时，橱窗里一条红裙子吸引了我的目光。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch sb in the ˈact (of doing sth)</b></td><td>当场抓住；抓个正着</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She turned round to catch him in the act of trying to run upstairs.<br>她转过身来正好看到</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈcatch it (BrE) (AmE catch ˈhell, ˈget it) (spoken)</b></td><td>挨骂；受罚</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>If your dad finds out youll really catch it!<br>要是你老爸知道了，你肯定要挨罚!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch sb ˈnapping (informal)</b></td><td>使人措手不及；趁人不备</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Chelsea's defence was caught napping in the final moments of the game when Jones scored his second goal for Liverpool.<br>比赛的最后时刻，琼斯趁切尔西队防守松懈，为利物浦队攻入了第二个球。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch sb off (their) guard</b></td><td>趁某人不备；使措手不及</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The question caught him off his guard and he couldn't answer.<br>他对这个问题毫无准备。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch sb on the ˈhop (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>使某人措手不及；出其不意</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The early inspection caught the whole kitchen staff on the hop.<br>提前到来的检查让整个后厨措手不及。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch some ˈrays (especially AmE, slang)</b></td><td>晒太阳</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>We're heading to the roof to catch some rays before the clouds roll in.<br>云还没上来，我们去屋顶晒会儿太阳。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch the ˈsun</b></td><td>晒黑；晒伤</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You've caught the sun on your shoulders—they're already bright pink.<br>你肩膀晒着了，都红得发亮了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch sb with their ˈpants down (informal)</b></td><td>使人措手不及；当场撞破</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The surprise audit caught the whole department with their pants down.<br>突击审计打了整个部门一个措手不及。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>catch sb with their ˈtrousers down (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>出其不意抓个正着；冷不防</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The reporters caught the minister with his trousers down over the missing files.<br>记者就失踪文件一事把部长打了个措手不及。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>play ˈcatch-up</b></td><td>奋起直追；拼命赶超</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The oil company has spent the last couple of years playing catch-up.<br>这家石油公司最近几年一直在拼命赶超。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be caught in the ˈcrossfire</b></td><td>殃及池鱼；卷入争斗受害</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>When two industrial giants clash, small companies can get caught in the crossfire.<br>若两大工业巨头发生争斗，小公司往往会遭受池鱼之殃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wouldn't be seen/caught ˈdead (in/with/at sth) (informal)</b></td><td>打死也不会（穿、去等）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He wouldn't be caught dead in a suit, not even at his own wedding.<br>他打死也不肯穿西装，连自己婚礼上都不穿。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be (all) for/in a good ˈcause</b></td><td>是为做好事；有意义</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Most motorists seem to accept that the speed cameras are all in a good cause (= they help to keep people safe on the roads by stopping people driving too fast).<br>大多数机动车驾驶员似乎都认为有测速摄像机是件好事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a lost ˈcause</b></td><td>注定失败的事；没指望的人</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Persuading Dad to use a smartphone is a lost cause at this point.<br>到这份上，劝我爸用智能手机已经没戏了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>throw caution to the ˈwind(s) (often humorous)</b></td><td>不顾一切；放胆行事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I decided to throw caution to the winds and buy myself a really expensive pair of shoes.<br>我决定不再顾忌什么，给自己花大价钱买一双鞋。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be the ˌcentre of atˈtention (BrE) (AmE be the ˌcenter of atˈtention)</b></td><td>成为众人瞩目的焦点</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>At every party my little brother has to be the centre of attention.<br>每次聚会我弟弟都非得当全场焦点。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˌturn of the ˈcentury/ˈyear</b></td><td>世纪之交；年头岁尾</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>He was born around the turn of the century.<br>他出生在世纪之交。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stand on ˈceremony (BrE)</b></td><td>讲究礼节；拘礼</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Come on - don't stand on ceremony! Start eating or the food will get cold!<br>来吧，别客气!快吃吧，不然饭菜要凉了!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>without ˈceremony</b></td><td>不拘礼节地；随随便便地</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>He dropped the box on my desk without ceremony and walked straight out.<br>他随手把箱子往我桌上一放就走了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>for ˈcertain</b></td><td>确切地；肯定地</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Nobody knows for certain why the factory closed so suddenly last winter.<br>去年冬天工厂为何突然关门，谁也说不准。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make ˈcertain (that...)</b></td><td>弄清楚；查明</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Make certain that the windows are shut before you set the alarm.<br>设警报前先确认窗户都关好了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make certain of sth/of doing sth</b></td><td>确保（某事发生）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>You'll have to leave succeed) soon to make certain of getting there on time.<br>你碰碰运气:</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>by ˈany chance</b></td><td>（询问时用）或许；有没有可能</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Do you have a spare charger by any chance? Mine died this morning.<br>你身上碰巧有多余的充电器吗？我的今早没电了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr class="sec"><td colspan="4">C</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(the) chances ˈare (that) (informal)</b></td><td>很可能</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The chances are that he'll come if he can finish work on time.<br>如果他能按时完工的话可能会来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take ˈchances</b></td><td>冒险；碰运气</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Take no chances: don't lend money to people you don't know.<br>别冒险，不要借钱给你不认识的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take your ˈchances (informal)</b></td><td>抓住机会；碰碰运气</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>When the offer of a job in Singapore came, I accepted it. After all, you have to take your chances in life.<br>当新加坡有工作机会时，我接受了。不管怎么说， 人生的机遇定要抓住。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>change ˈhands</b></td><td>易主；转手</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The house has changed hands several times.<br>这房子已几易其主。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>change your ˈmind</b></td><td>改变主意</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He was intending to go to the party but now he's changed his mind and decided to stay in.<br>他本想去参加聚会，不过现在改变主意了，决定在家里呆着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌchange of ˈheart</b></td><td>态度转变；改变看法</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The Government has had a change of heart over the proposed tax reforms and is now prepared to listen to public opinion.<br>政府对税收改革的提议改变了态度，现在准备听取公众的意见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>change the ˈsubject</b></td><td>转换话题</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Every time I mention money, he changes the subject to the weather.<br>我一提钱，他就把话题扯到天气上。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>change your ˈtune (informal)</b></td><td>改变态度；改口</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Tom used to say that parents worry too much about their children, but he soon changed his tune when he became a parent himself!<br>汤姆过去总说父母为孩子操心过多，可他自己当上父亲之后口气很快就变了!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>change your ˈways</b></td><td>改变生活方式；改过</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Tve learned my lesson and I'm going to try to change my ways.<br>我接受了教训，打算换个活法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>for a ˈchange</b></td><td>换换花样；改变一下</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We usually 80 to Cyprus on holiday but this year we've decided to stay at home for a change.<br>通常我们会去塞浦路斯度假，今年我们决定换个花样，在家里呆着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get no ˈchange out of sb (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>从某人处得不到帮助（或消息）</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>If you need any help, ask Manuel. Youll get more change out of him than the others.<br>如果你需要帮助，就找曼纽尔吧，你在他那儿能得到更多帮助。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a wind/the winds of ˈchange</b></td><td>变革之风；变化的征兆</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>There's a wind of change in the attitude of voters.<br>选民的态度有改变的迹象。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌchapter and ˈverse</b></td><td>详细出处；确切依据</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>I can't give you chapter and verse, but I can tell you that the lines she quoted come from a Brecht play.<br>我</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌchapter of ˈaccidents</b></td><td>接二连三的不幸；祸不单行</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>The trip was a chapter of accidents: lost bags, food poisoning and a strike.<br>这趟旅行祸不单行：丢行李、食物中毒，还赶上罢工。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌin/ˌout of ˈcharacter</b></td><td>符合（或不符合）某人性格</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Shouting at a waiter is completely out of character for my gentle uncle.<br>冲服务员大喊大叫，完全不像我那温和的叔叔。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get a ˈcharge out of sth (AmE)</b></td><td>从…中获得乐趣</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>My grandmother gets a real charge out of beating us all at cards.<br>我奶奶打牌赢我们所有人，觉得特别过瘾。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take ˈcharge (of sth)</b></td><td>接管；开始负责</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>When the manager fell ill, Priya took charge of the whole project.<br>经理病倒后，普里娅接管了整个项目。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>charity begins at ˈhome (saying)</b></td><td>仁爱始于家庭；先顾自家人</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Before donating abroad, remember that charity begins at home.<br>往国外捐款前，别忘了行善要先从家里做起。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>work like a ˈcharm (informal)</b></td><td>非常奏效；很灵验</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Idon't know what begin to run after sb/sth in order to catch them she said to him, but it worked like a charm - he's much more cooperative now.<br>我不知道她</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lead/have a charmed ˈlife</b></td><td>总是好运；如有神助</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>He's walked away from two crashes, so the man leads a charmed life.<br>两次车祸他都毫发无伤，这人真是命大。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>off the ˈcharts</b></td><td>高得离谱；超出正常范围</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ticket demand for the reunion tour has been off the charts all week.<br>重组巡演的票务需求这一周高得离谱。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chase your (own) ˈtail</b></td><td>瞎忙活；徒劳无功</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I spent all morning chasing my own tail between three different offices.<br>我一上午在三个办公室之间瞎跑，一无所获。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈtail-chasing</b></td><td>瞎忙；徒劳的奔忙</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>After a week of pure tail-chasing, we finally got a straight answer.<br>瞎折腾了一星期，我们总算得到一个明确答复。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be going ˈcheap (informal)</b></td><td>廉价出售；降价卖</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>These shirts were going cheap, so I bought two.<br>这些衬衫降价出售，于是我买了两件。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cheap and ˈcheerful (informal)</b></td><td>物美价廉；便宜实惠</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It's a cheap and cheerful little diner, but the breakfasts are excellent.<br>这是家便宜实惠的小餐馆，早餐特别棒。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cheap and ˈnasty (informal)</b></td><td>质劣价廉；便宜没好货</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The furniture cheap and nasty.<br>这家具是质量低劣的便</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cheap at ˈtwice the price</b></td><td>非常划算；再贵一倍也值</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>I know E6 000 is a lot of money, but a great car like this is cheap at the price.<br>我知道6000英镑不是个小数目，但是买一辆这么好的车还是物有所值的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not come ˈcheap</b></td><td>价格不菲；不便宜</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Violins like this don't come cheap.<br>像这样的小提琴不会便宜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the ˈcheap (informal)</b></td><td>廉价地；花小钱</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He got it on the cheap so I wasn't surprised when it broke after a couple of months.<br>他买的是廉价货，所以几个月后就坏了，我一点也不惊讶。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep/hold sb/sth in ˈcheck</b></td><td>控制；抑制</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The disease is kept in check with drugs.<br>疾病被药物控制着。0</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>checks and ˈbalances</b></td><td>制约与平衡；权力制衡</td><td>★★★★<br>★★</td><td>These are the proposals for introducing a new system of checks and balances into the boardrooms of UK companies.<br>这些提案试图为英国公司的董事会引进一套新的权力制衡制度。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cheek by ˈjowl (with sb/sth)</b></td><td>紧挨着；密集相邻</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>If he'd known that he was to find himself seated cheek by jowl with his old enemy he wouldn't have attended the dinner.<br>要是他知道会跟仇家并肩坐在一起共进晚餐的话， 他根本就不会来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turn the other ˈcheek</b></td><td>逆来顺受；不予还击</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>It's hard to just turn the other cheek when people are criticizing you unfairly.<br>当一个人受到不公平的指责时，是很难保持平静逆来顺受的。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get sth off your ˈchest (informal)</b></td><td>倾诉心事；一吐为快</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>If something is worrying you,get it off your chest.<br>心里有什么烦恼，就说出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌchew the ˈfat (BrE) (AmE ˌchew the ˈrag)</b></td><td>闲聊；唠嗑</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We sat on the porch chewing the fat until it got completely dark.<br>我们坐在门廊上闲聊，一直聊到天全黑。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈchicken feed (informal)</b></td><td>小钱；微不足道的钱</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>My salary is chicken feed compared with hers.<br>与她相比，我的工资少得可怜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(your/the) chickens come home to ˈroost</b></td><td>自食其果；恶有恶报</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>His chickens came home to roost when the inspectors found the faulty wiring.<br>检查员查出线路有问题，他终于自食其果。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>don't count your ˈchickens (before they're hatched) (saying)</b></td><td>别过早乐观；勿盲目自信</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Don't count your chickens—the buyer hasn't actually signed anything yet.<br>别高兴太早，买家其实还没签任何字。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>too many ˌchiefs and not enough ˈIndians (saying)</b></td><td>指挥的多，干活的少</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Nothing gets finished here: too many chiefs and not enough Indians.<br>这儿什么都做不完，指挥的多，干活的少。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈchild's play</b></td><td>极容易的事；小菜一碟</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>After climbing that mountain, a five-mile walk feels like child's play.<br>爬过那座山之后，走五英里简直是小菜一碟。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈchill runs/goes down sb's spine</b></td><td>令人毛骨悚然；不寒而栗</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>A chill ran down my spine when I heard footsteps in the empty house.<br>空房子里传来脚步声，我不寒而栗。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>send a ˈchill up/down sb's spine</b></td><td>使人不寒而栗</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The recording of that phone call sent a chill down my spine.<br>那通电话的录音让我脊背发凉。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>chill sb to the ˈbone/ˈmarrow</b></td><td>使人透心凉；使极为恐惧</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The wind off the sea chilled us to the bone within five minutes.<br>海风吹了不到五分钟就把我们冻透了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(keep your) ˈchin up (informal)</b></td><td>振作起来；别灰心</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Chin up! Things will get better soon.<br>别灰心!事情很快就会有转机的。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>have the market ˈcornered (in sth)</b></td><td>垄断某一市场</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Bestsave has the market cornered in cheap groceries across the whole region.<br>倍省超市垄断了整个地区的廉价杂货生意。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>be around the ˈcorner</b></td><td>近在眼前；即将发生</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Success is around the corner, so the work must not be stopped now.<br>成功就在眼前，现在决不能停下来。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>out of the corner of your ˈeye</b></td><td>用眼角余光</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Out of the corner of my eye I saw him slip the envelope into his bag.<br>我用余光瞥见他把信封塞进了包里。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turn the ˈcorner</b></td><td>度过难关；出现转机</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The patient turned the corner on Tuesday and is now sitting up eating.<br>病人周二挺过了危险期，现在能坐起来吃饭了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cut ˈcorners (disapproving)</b></td><td>走捷径；偷工减料</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Don't be tempted to cut corners when doing a home decorating job.<br>居室装修不要图省事贪便宜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the four corners of the ˈearth/ˈworld</b></td><td>天涯海角；世界各地</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Fans came from the four corners of the earth for the band's final concert.<br>歌迷从世界各地赶来看乐队的告别演唱会。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the corridors of ˈpower</b></td><td>权力中枢；政府高层</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>She spent thirty years in the corridors of power advising four different ministers.<br>她在权力中枢待了三十年，先后为四位大臣出谋划策。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at ˈany cost</b></td><td>不惜任何代价</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He is determined to win at any cost.<br>他决心无</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it will ˈcost you (spoken)</b></td><td>那可得花大价钱</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I can get you tickets for tonight, but it will cost you.<br>今晚的票我能弄到，不过你得出血。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to your ˈcost</b></td><td>吃了亏才知道；付出代价后才明白</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>As I know to my cost, that garage never finishes a job on time.<br>我是吃过亏才知道，那家修车行从不按时完工。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at ˈall costs</b></td><td>不惜一切代价</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We must avoid a strike at all costs before the holiday season starts.<br>假期旺季开始前，我们必须不惜一切代价避免罢工。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈcouch potato (informal, disapproving)</b></td><td>终日窝在沙发看电视的懒人</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>His mother warns him he'll turn into a couch potato over the long summer.<br>他妈妈警告说，这个长假他会变成沙发土豆。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be able to count sb/sth on (the fingers of) one ˈhand</b></td><td>屈指可数；寥寥无几</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>You can count the good restaurants in this town on one hand.<br>这镇上好餐馆一只手就数得过来。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>count sth on the fingers of one ˈhand</b></td><td>少得可数；寥寥可数</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She could count on the fingers of one hand the people she actually enjoyed being with.<br>她真正喜欢与之交往的人屈指可数。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>count your ˈblessings</b></td><td>知足；想想还有什么值得庆幸</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Stop looking and count your blessings! At least youve still got a job and somewhere to live.<br>别再愁眉苦脸的，知足吧!至少你有工作可做，有地方可住。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>count the ˈcost</b></td><td>考虑代价（或风险）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The job was attractive financially, but when I counted the cost in terms of separation from my family and friends, I decided not to take it.<br>这份工作收入很高，可想到要以同家人和朋友分开为代价，我决定不接受。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>count ˈsheep</b></td><td>数羊（以求入睡）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Doug closed his eyes and tried counting sheep, but he still couldn't get to sleep.<br>道格闭上眼睛开始数羊以便入睡，可是怎么也睡不着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep (a) ˈcount (of sth)</b></td><td>记住数目；数得清</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Make sure you keep count of all the phone calls you make so you can claim the money back later.<br>把你打电话的次数记下来，以后可以报销。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lose ˈcount (of sth)</b></td><td>记不清数目；数不过来</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He's had so many different jobs that Tve lost count (of them all).<br>他做过很多份工作， 我都记不清多少了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not count your ˈchickens (before they're hatched)</b></td><td>别过早乐观；勿盲目自信</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She said she was certain to be offered a part in the play, but I told her not to count her chickens, as a lot of other people wanted the same part.<br>她说她一定能在剧中得到一个角色，可是我告诉她不要高兴得过早，因为很多人也都想演那个角色。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>out for the ˈcount (BrE) (AmE ˌdown for the ˈcount)</b></td><td>不省人事；累得酣睡</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>After a whole day of walking around the ciry, I was out for the count!<br>在城里走了一整天之后，我累得倒头大睡!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stand up and be ˈcounted</b></td><td>公开表明立场；挺身表态</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>I think that people who disagree with the policy should stand up and be counted.<br>我认为不同意这一政策的人应该站出来公开表明立场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>over the ˈcounter</b></td><td>（买药）不需处方</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>These tablets are available over the counter.<br>这些药片不用处方就可买到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>under the ˈcounter</b></td><td>私下地；偷偷地；非法地</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Before the revolution, such luxuries were only sold under the counter.<br>革命前，这样的奢侈品只能私下交易。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>who's ˈcounting? (informal)</b></td><td>谁在乎呢；谁数着呢</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Tve been late for school three times this week - but who's counting?<br>这周内我上学迟到了三次，不过管它呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a country ˈbumpkin/ˈcousin (informal, usually disapproving)</b></td><td>乡巴佬；没见过世面的人</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He felt like a country bumpkin during his first week in London.<br>在伦敦的头一周，他觉得自己像个乡巴佬。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go to the ˈcountry (BrE)</b></td><td>举行大选</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>The Prime 1 (also course informal) used to emphasize Minister may decide to go to the country in the that what you are saying is true or correct next few weeks.<br>首相可能决定在数周内举行大选。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have/lack the courage of your conˈvictions</b></td><td>有（或没有）勇气坚持信念</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>She had the courage of her convictions and voted against her own party.<br>她坚持自己的信念，投票反对本党。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pluck up (the) ˈcourage (to do sth)</b></td><td>鼓起勇气（做某事）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It took him a month to pluck up the courage to ask her out.<br>他花了一个月才鼓起勇气约她出去。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take your ˌcourage in both ˈhands</b></td><td>鼓起勇气；壮起胆子</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She took her courage in both hands and told the boss she was leaving.<br>她鼓起勇气告诉老板自己要走。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a course of ˈaction</b></td><td>行动方针；处事办法</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The safest course of action is to postpone the trip until early spring.<br>最稳妥的做法是把行程推迟到早春。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the ˌnormal/ˌordinary course of eˈvents</b></td><td>在通常情况下；照常规</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>In the normal course of events, the results arrive within about ten days.<br>通常情况下，结果十天左右就会寄到。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>of ˈcourse</b></td><td>当然；自然</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Of course you can borrow the car, just fill the tank afterwards.<br>你当然可以借车，用完加满油就行。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>of ˈcourse (spoken)</b></td><td>（礼貌应允）当然可以</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Can I use your phone? Of course—help yourself, it's on the table.<br>我能用下你的电话吗？当然，请便，就在桌上。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>of ˈcourse not (also ˈcourse not informal)</b></td><td>当然不；才不呢</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Of course not! I'd never tell your sister about the surprise trip.<br>当然不会！我绝不会把这次惊喜旅行告诉你姐姐。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hold ˈcourt (often ironic)</b></td><td>成为众人焦点；高谈阔论</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>There was Professor Johnson, holding court as usual in the students' coffee bar.<br>看，约翰逊教授又在学生咖啡厅里大出风头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>rule/throw sth out of ˈcourt</b></td><td>断然拒绝；不予考虑</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The committee ruled any further discussion out of court.<br>委员会拒绝进一步讨论此事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ball is in your/sb's ˈcourt</b></td><td>该你（或某人）作决定了</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I've made my offer, so now the ball is in their court.<br>我已经开出条件，现在轮到他们决定了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>courtesy of sb/sth</b></td><td>蒙…好意；由…提供</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The pictures have been reproduced by courtesy of the British Museum.<br>承蒙大英博物馆惠允，才得以复制了这些画。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do sb the courtesy of doing sth</b></td><td>出于礼貌为某人做某事</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Please do me the courtesy of listening to what I'm saying.<br>请耐心听我讲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have the courtesy to do sth</b></td><td>有礼貌地做某事；懂规矩</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>You think he'd at least have the courtesy to call to say he'd be late.<br>按常理他至少应该懂得打个电话，说一下他要晚来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cover all the/your ˈbases (especially AmE)</b></td><td>考虑周全；面面俱到</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Are you sure we covered all our bases on this?<br>你确信我们在这个问题上考虑周全了吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cover your ˈback (informal) (AmE also cover your ˈass, slang)</b></td><td>预防日后被追责；留一手</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Copy me into that email just to cover your back if things go wrong.<br>那封邮件抄送我一份，万一出事你也有个交代。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cover your ˈtracks</b></td><td>掩盖行踪；不留痕迹</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He didn't want his wife to know he'd met an old girlfriend so he invented a story to cover his tracks.<br>他不想让妻子知道自己与从前的女友见面，就编了个谎话来遮掩。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from ˌcover to ˈcover</b></td><td>从头至尾（读完）</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Tve read the newspaper from cover to cover, but I can't find any mention of yesterday's accident.<br>我把报纸从头到尾都看完了，怎么也找不到关于昨天事故的消息。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>under ˈcover</b></td><td>秘密地；伪装身份地</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Two officers worked under cover in the warehouse for almost six months.<br>两名警官在仓库卧底了将近半年。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>under cover of sth</b></td><td>在…的掩护下</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>They hoped to get into the enemy fortress under cover of darkness.<br>他们希望在夜幕的掩护下进入敌人的要塞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a ˈcow (AmE, slang)</b></td><td>大发雷霆；急得跳脚</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>My dad spent $500 on a new coat and my mom had a cow.<br>我爸爸花了500美元买了一件新外套，妈妈顿时气不打一处来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>till/until the ˈcows come home (informal)</b></td><td>很久很久；无限期地</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You can talk till the cows come home, but youll never persuade me togo with you!<br>随你怎么说，休想让我跟你一起去!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crack a ˈjoke</b></td><td>讲笑话；开玩笑</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He's always cracking jokes in class.<br>他总是在课上讲笑话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the crack of ˈdawn (informal)</b></td><td>黎明；破晓时分</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We left at the crack of dawn to beat the holiday traffic.<br>我们天一亮就出发，好避开假日车流。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>crack the ˈwhip</b></td><td>严加督促；施压逼人干活</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>What you need to do used to tell sb in an impolite way to stop is crack the whip and make sure that they do talking about unimportant things or talking the job properly.<br>你需要采取铁腕政策，让他们好</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not be all it's cracked ˈup to be (informal)</b></td><td>并不像人们说的那么好</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The food in this restaurant is not all it's cracked up to be.<br>这</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get ˈcracking (informal)</b></td><td>赶紧开始；抓紧干</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Let's get cracking on the packing or we'll miss the morning ferry.<br>赶紧收拾行李吧，不然赶不上早班渡轮。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from the ˌcradle to the ˈgrave</b></td><td>从生到死；一辈子</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The system was meant to care for citizens from the cradle to the grave.<br>这套制度本意是从生到死照顾国民。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cramp sb's ˈstyle</b></td><td>妨碍某人自由发挥；碍手碍脚</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Having my little brother along really cramped my style at the party.<br>带着弟弟去派对，实在让我放不开。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do sb ˈcredit ◆ do ˈcredit to sb</b></td><td>为某人增光；值得称许</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Her calm handling of the whole crisis really does her credit.<br>她冷静应对整场危机，实在令人称许。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be to sb's ˈcredit</b></td><td>值得赞扬；给某人长脸</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The event was arranged with a speed and efficiency that does you credit.<br>这项活动组织得快捷高效，给你加了分。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have sth to your ˈcredit</b></td><td>取得（成就）；名下有</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>At the age of twenty he already has several major victories to his credit.<br>他在二十岁时已经数次取得重大的胜利。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the ˈcredit side</b></td><td>就好的方面而言；从有利一面看</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>If you work for yourself you may not make much money. On the credit side, you will be completely independent.<br>如果你自己干的话可能挣不到太多钱，但从好的方面看，可以不受他人管束。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>up the ˈcreek (informal) (also up shit ˈcreek (without a ˈpaddle), slang)</b></td><td>陷入困境；麻烦大了</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>If the generator fails tonight, we are really up the creek.<br>今晚发电机要是罢工，我们就麻烦大了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˌcreme de la ˈcreme (from French, formal or humorous)</b></td><td>精华；最优秀的人</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>This university takes only the creme de la creme of school leavers.<br>这所大学只招收最优秀的中学毕业生。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(on) the crest of a ˈwave</b></td><td>处于鼎盛时期；春风得意</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>He was fortunate to arrive in Hollywood when the film industry was on the crest of a wave.<br>他很幸运，在电影业的鼎盛时期来到好莱坞。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a skeleton ˈcrew/ˈstaff/ˈservice</b></td><td>最低限度的人员；基本运作的班子（或服务）</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Over Christmas the hospital runs with a skeleton staff and only urgent cases.<br>圣诞期间医院只留最少人手，仅处理急诊。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's (just) not ˈcricket (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</b></td><td>不公平；不光明正大</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>Reading someone else's emails is just not cricket, even if you're the boss.<br>偷看别人的邮件太不地道了，就算你是老板也一样。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put a ˈcrimp in/on sth (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>妨碍；对…有负面影响</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>I'm sorry to put a crimp in your The plans.<br>影响了你的计划，真不好意思。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put a ˈcrimp on sth (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>使…受影响；给…添麻烦</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>The extra expense of moving can put a crimp on your monthly budget.<br>搬家多出来的花销会把你每月的预算压得很紧。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌcrock of ˈshit (taboo, slang, especially AmE)</b></td><td>屁话；胡说八道</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Honestly, that excuse about traffic is a crock of shit and everyone knows it.<br>说什么堵车，全是屁话，谁都看得出来。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈcrocodile tears</b></td><td>鳄鱼的眼泪；假慈悲</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>They never visited her when she was ill, but they came to her funeral and shed (= cried) a few crocodile tears.<br>她生病时他们从不去看她，但是她的葬礼他们都参加了，还挤出了几滴鳄鱼的眼泪。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>come a ˈcropper (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>摔跟头；遭惨败</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>Pete came a cropper on his motorbike and ended up in hospital.<br>皮特从摩托车上摔下米，结果进了医院。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/talk at cross ˈpurposes</b></td><td>各说各话；互相误解</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>We talked for ten minutes at cross purposes before realizing we meant different people.<br>我们各说各话聊了十分钟，才发现说的不是同一个人。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cross a ˈbridge when you ˈcome to it</b></td><td>问题出现时再解决；船到桥头自然直</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Let's cross that bridge when we come to it instead of worrying about it now.<br>等真出了问题再说吧，现在别瞎操心。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cross your ˈbridges when you ˈcome to them</b></td><td>待问题出现时再设法解决；到时再说</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She always crosses her bridges when she comes to them and never plans ahead.<br>她总是遇到问题再解决，从不提前打算。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cross sb's ˈmind</b></td><td>掠过某人心头；某人想到</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>It suddenly crossed my mind that I hadn't seen her for months.<br>我突然想起，好几个月没见到她了。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>cross my ˈheart (and hope to ˈdie) (spoken)</b></td><td>我发誓；千真万确</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I didn't touch your chocolate, cross my heart and hope to die.<br>我真没动你的巧克力，我发誓。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cross sb's ˈpath • our/their paths ˈcross</b></td><td>与某人不期而遇；偶然相遇</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He never crossed my path, thank goodness.<br>于关键时刻；在紧要关头；处于十字路口:</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>bear/carry your ˈcross</b></td><td>背负自己的十字架；默默承受苦难</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>We all dot → dot the/your i's and cross the/your t's have our crosses to be ⑦ ORIGIN This refers to the punishments used in the time of Jesus and described in the Bible.<br>这个， 习语原指《圣经》中耶稣时代所用的惩罚。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>have crossed ˈlines/ˈwires (informal)</b></td><td>话说岔了；沟通有误</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Somewhere along the way we had crossed wires about who was booking the hotel.<br>中间不知哪里说岔了，谁订酒店都没弄清。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>if/when it comes to the ˈcrunch (informal)</b></td><td>到了紧要关头；关键时刻</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>When it comes to the crunch, she always backs her team without hesitation.<br>到了关键时刻，她总会毫不犹豫地力挺自己的团队。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>cry ˈwolf</b></td><td>谎报险情；发假警报</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Is the economic future really so bad? Or are the economists just crying wolf?<br>未来的经济真的有那么糟糕吗？还是经济学家们在谎报险情？ ②</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>ˌcrystal ˈclear</b></td><td>一清二楚；极易理解</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>After Anne was late for the third time in a week, her boss made it crystal clear that it must not happen again.<br>安妮一周内</td></tr>
