<tr><td><b>don't you ˈdare (do sth)! (spoken)</b></td><td>你敢！；不许你…</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Don't you dare tell my mother about the parking ticket!<br>你敢跟我妈说罚单的事试试！（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>how ˈdare you, etc. (spoken)</b></td><td>你（他等）怎么敢；岂有此理</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>How dare you speak to me like that!<br>你竟敢这样对我说话!。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I dare ˈsay (spoken)</b></td><td>我想；大概；很可能</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I dare say she's forgotten all about it by now, honestly.<br>说真的，我想她这会儿早忘干净了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a dark ˈhorse (BrE)</b></td><td>深藏不露的人；黑马</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>You're a dark horse — you never told us you could sing!<br>你可真深藏不露，从没说过你会唱歌！（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the ˈdark (about sth)</b></td><td>蒙在鼓里；对…一无所知</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Workers were kept in the dark about the plans to sell the company.<br>对于出售公司的计划!.人们还被篆在鼓里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a shot/stab in the ˈdark</b></td><td>瞎猜；胡乱一试</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It was a shot in the dark, but my guess turned out right.<br>纯属瞎猜，可我居然蒙对了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>darn it! (spoken, especially AmE)</b></td><td>见鬼；真讨厌（表示恼火）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Darn it! Tve lost my keys!<br>真见鬼，我的钥匙天广!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I'll be ˈdarned! (spoken, especially AmE)</b></td><td>真没想到；真让人意外</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Well, I'll be darned, they actually let him back on the team.<br>嘿，真没想到，他们居然让他回队里了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cut a ˈdash (BrE)</b></td><td>风度翩翩；引人注目</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>She cuts quite a dash with her designer clothes and expensive car.<br>她穿石名牌服装，开有蒙华轿车，很”派。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>out of date</b></td><td>过时的；过期的</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Half the information on that website is completely out of date.<br>那个网站上一半的信息都过时了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to ˈdate</b></td><td>迄今为止；到目前为止</td><td>★★★★<br>★★</td><td>To date we've had over three hundred applications for the single post.<br>到目前为止，这一个职位已收到三百多份申请。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌup to date</b></td><td>最新的；包含最新信息的</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Please keep the sales figures up to date so I can check them.<br>请把销售数据随时更新，方便我核对。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nothing ˈdaunted (BrE, formal)</b></td><td>毫不气馁；无所畏惧</td><td>★<br>★</td><td>Nothing daunted, she climbed back on the horse and rode off.<br>她毫不气馁，重新翻身上马跑了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>all day and ˈevery day</b></td><td>天天如此；成天不变</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I have to be active. I couldn't just sit around all day and every day now Tve retired.<br>我要积极生活，现作我退休了，总不能老这么天大闲坐石</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>all in a day's ˈwork</b></td><td>家常便饭；分内之事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Dealing with angry passengers is all in a day's work for her.<br>应付发火的乘客对她来说是家常便饭。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>any day (now) (spoken)</b></td><td>就这一两天；很快</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>The letter should arrive any day now.<br>信应该很快就到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈany day (of the week)</b></td><td>无论何时都；怎么都（表示更喜欢）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I'd rather have him than his brother any day of the week.<br>不管怎么说，我宁可要他也不想要他的弟弟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>carry/win the ˈday (formal)</b></td><td>获胜；占上风</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>I was a difficult match, but the New Zealand team finally carried the day.<br>这是场艰苦的比赛，不过新西兰队最终取得了胜利。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>day after ˈday</b></td><td>日复一日；一天又一天</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Day after day, she came and waited fifty-five if she's a day!<br>她可不止四十岁!至少有</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>day by ˈday</b></td><td>一天天地；逐日</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Day by day she grew more confident about the job.<br>天天过去了，她对工作更有信心了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>day ˌin, day ˈout</b></td><td>天天如此；日复一日不间断</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I drive to work day in, day out, and I'm getting tired of spending so much time travelling.<br>我天天开车上班，已经厌倦了花这么多时间在路上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the day of ˈreckoning (formal)</b></td><td>算账的日子；遭报应之时</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Tomorrow is the day of reckoning; the accountant will tell me what my profits were and how much tax Tll have to pay.<br>明天就是算总账的日子，会计师会告诉我有多少盈利，该交多</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>don't give up the ˈday job (informal, humorous)</b></td><td>别丢了老本行（讽刺水平不行）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>So you want to be a writer? Well my advice is, don't give up the day job.<br>这么说你想当作家？得了吧，我劝你还是不要放弃老本行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from day ˈone (spoken)</b></td><td>从第一天起；从一开始</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>This arrangement has never worked from day one.<br>这个安排从一开始就行不通。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from day to ˈday</b></td><td>过一天算一天；日复一日地</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>They both live from day to day, looking after their sick daughter.<br>他们俩都在熬日子，日复一日地照顾生病的女儿。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from ˌone day to the ˈnext</b></td><td>一天一个样；变化无常</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>In this job, I never know what to expect from one day to the next.<br>做这份工作，我每天都不知道第二天会出现什么情况。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have had your/its ˈday</b></td><td>风光不再；已过全盛期</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He used to be one of the world's top soccer players but now, I'm afraid, he's had his day.<br>他曾经是世界最顶尖的足球运动员之一，不过现在，恐怕他已风光不再。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌif he's, she's, etc. a ˈday (informal)</b></td><td>（说年龄）少说也有；至少</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>She's seventy if she's a day, though she still runs marathons.<br>她少说也有七十了，可还在跑马拉松。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in sb's day/time</b></td><td>在某人的年代；在某人的鼎盛时期</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>In my grandfather's day you could buy a house for a few thousand pounds.<br>在我爷爷那年头，几千英镑就能买套房。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in ˈthis day and age</b></td><td>在当今这个时代</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It's surprising, in this day and age, to discover that there are still many homes which do not have telephones.<br>在今天这个时代，居然还有很多家庭没有电话，这真让人奇怪。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make sb's ˈday (informal)</b></td><td>让某人高兴一整天</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Your postcard from Lisbon absolutely made my day.<br>你从里斯本寄来的明信片让我高兴了一整天。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make a ˈday of it (spoken)</b></td><td>好好玩上一整天</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Instead of going home when we've done our shopping, why don't we make a day of it and stay in town for lunch?<br>买完东西干吗急着回家？干脆在城里吃午饭，痛痛快快过上一整天。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not be sb's ˈday (spoken)</b></td><td>是某人倒霉的一天</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>First I tore my jacket, then my car broke down. This is definitely not my day!<br>先是夹克衫撕破了，然后车又坏了，我今天真够倒霉的!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈone day</b></td><td>有朝一日；（过去的）某一天</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>One day r'd like to go to o one day we China.<br>总有一天我要去中国。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈsome day</b></td><td>将来有一天；总有一天</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Some day youll realize what good parents you have.<br>总有一天你会明白你的父母有多好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take it/things one ˌday at a ˈtime (spoken)</b></td><td>一天天慢慢来；不去多想以后</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I don't know if hell get better. We're just taking things one day at a time.<br>我不知道他还能不能好起来，我们只有过一天算一天。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈthat'll be the day (spoken, ironic)</b></td><td>那才怪呢；根本不可能</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Him cooking dinner for everyone? That'll be the day.<br>他给大家做饭？那才怪呢。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to the ˈday</b></td><td>恰好；一天不差</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>It's ten years to the day since I first came to this town.<br>今天距我第一次来这个小镇已整整十年了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to this ˈday</b></td><td>直到今天；至今</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>To this day I have not been able to find out anything about who my real parents were.<br>直到今天我也没能搞清楚谁是我的亲生父母。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌdaylight ˈrobbery (informal, especially BrE)</b></td><td>漫天要价；明抢</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Five pounds for a small coffee is absolute daylight robbery.<br>一小杯咖啡卖五镑，简直是明抢。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>see ˈdaylight</b></td><td>恍然大悟；看到希望</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>It was a long stand time before he finally saw daylight and realized what was going on.<br>过了好长时间他才终于明白过来，意识到发生了什么事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beat/scare the (living) ˈdaylights out of sb</b></td><td>把某人痛打一顿；把某人吓个半死</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He said ifi did it again he'd beat the living daylights out of me!<br>他说要是我再</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>your, its, etc. days are ˈnumbered</b></td><td>时日无多；撑不了多久了</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Now that we're no longer getting any government support, the theatre's days are numbered.<br>如今我们得不到政府的任何支持，剧院撑不了多久了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈone of these days</b></td><td>总有一天；改天</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>It's been nice talking to you. We must meet up again one of these days.<br>很高兴跟你交谈，我们一定要找个时间再聚一聚。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(just) one of those ˈdays</b></td><td>诸事不顺的一天</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>It's been one of those days. I lost my keys and then I fell over running for the bus.<br>真是个倒霉的日子，我丢了钥匙，赶公共汽车的时候又摔了一跤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈthese days</b></td><td>如今；现在（与过去相比）</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>These days hardly anyone writes letters by hand any more.<br>如今几乎没人再手写信了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈthose were the days</b></td><td>那才是好时光；那才叫好年头</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>We played football until dark every evening — those were the days!<br>我们每天踢球踢到天黑，那才叫好日子！（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cut sb ˈdead</b></td><td>故意不理睬某人；装作没看见</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She cut me dead in the corridor as if we'd never met.<br>她在走廊里当没看见我，好像从不认识。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dead and ˈburied/gone</b></td><td>早已过去；不复存在</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>That argument is dead and buried, so let's not bring it up.<br>那场争执早就翻篇了，别再提。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(as) dead as a/the ˈdodo (informal)</b></td><td>彻底过时；早已绝迹</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Old business practices are as dead as a dodo in the computer age.<br>在计算机时</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(as) ˌdead as a ˈdoornail (informal)</b></td><td>死透了；彻底不动了</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I tried the engine again, but the battery was as dead as a doornail.<br>我又试了一次，可电瓶彻底没电了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a dead ˈcert (informal)</b></td><td>十拿九稳的事；必胜者</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>With that lineup, they're a dead cert for the semi-finals.<br>凭这个阵容，他们进半决赛十拿九稳。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a dead ˈduck (informal)</b></td><td>注定失败的计划；没戏的想法</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The new supermarket is going to be a dead duck; there's no demand for one in this area.<br>这家新超市注定会倒闭，因为这一地区不需要这么一个店。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a dead ˈend (informal)</b></td><td>死胡同；僵局</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Lack of further clues meant that the murder investigation came to a dead end.<br>没有进一步的线索，谋杀案的调查陷入僵局。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be dead in the ˈwater</b></td><td>（人或计划）已失败；毫无进展</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The merger talks have been dead in the water since last month.<br>合并谈判从上个月起就彻底停摆了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a dead ˈletter</b></td><td>形同虚设的规定；无人理会的建议</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>That old parking rule is a dead letter now; nobody enforces it.<br>那条老停车规定形同虚设，没人执行。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a dead ˈloss</b></td><td>一无是处的人（或物）</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>As a plumber he's a dead loss; the leak is worse now.<br>他当水管工一无是处，现在漏得更厉害了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dead ˈmeat (informal)</b></td><td>死定了；要倒大霉</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>If Mum finds out we broke the vase, we're dead meat.<br>要是妈发现花瓶是我们打碎的，我们就死定了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(in) the ˌdead of (the) ˈnight</b></td><td>深夜；夜深人静时</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>They loaded the van in the dead of night so nobody would notice.<br>他们趁夜深人静装车，免得被人看见。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at ˌdead of ˈnight</b></td><td>在深夜；夜半时分</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She crept in at dead of night, while they were asleep.<br>深夜在他们熟睡</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a dead ˈringer for sb (informal)</b></td><td>酷似某人的人</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She's a dead ringer for her mother.<br>她活像她的母亲。 ②</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dead to the ˈworld (informal)</b></td><td>睡得很沉；不省人事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Within two minutes of getting into bed, I was dead to the world.<br>上床不到两分钟我就睡得死去一般。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dead ˈwood (informal)</b></td><td>冗员；无用的人（或物）</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The new manager wants to cut out the dead wood in our department.<br>新经理想清掉我们部门的冗员。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sb wouldn't be seen/caught ˈdead… (spoken)</b></td><td>打死也不会做（某事）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I wouldn't be seen dead in a hat like that.<br>我不愿意戴那样的帽子出洋相。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(as) deaf as a ˈpost (informal)</b></td><td>聋得什么也听不见</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You'll have to shout if you want her to hear you. She's as deaf as a post.<br>你想让她听见就得大声喊，她耳朵聋得厉害。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fall on deaf ˈears</b></td><td>被置若罔闻；没人理会</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Our request for money fell on deaf ears.<br>没人搭理我们要钱的请求。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turn a deaf ˈear (to sth)</b></td><td>充耳不闻；不予理会</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She turned a deaf ear to her husband's advice and took the job anyway.<br>她不听丈夫的劝告，还是接受了这份工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cut a ˈdeal (with sb) • cut (sb) a ˈdeal (business)</b></td><td>（与某人）达成交易</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She cut a deal with the boss who allowed her to work on the project if she raised half the funds.<br>她和老板达成了协议:只要她能筹集到一半的资金，她就可以继续做这个项目。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>deal sb/sth a ˈblow • deal a blow to sb/sth</b></td><td>给…以打击；使…受挫</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The death of her father dealt her a terrible blow.<br>父亲的去世使她受到沉重的打击。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a raw/rough ˈdeal</b></td><td>不公正的待遇</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Many old people feel they are getting a raw deal from the state: they pay money towards a pension all their working life but discover it isn't worth much when they retire.<br>许多老人觉得他们受到了国家的不公平对待:他们工作时一直交纳养老金，可退休后却发现养老金价值无几。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dear ˈme • (dear,) oh ˈdear</b></td><td>哎呀；天哪（表示担忧或同情）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Dear me, you've spilt tea all over the new carpet.<br>哎呀，你把茶全洒在新地毯上了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>for dear ˈlife • for your ˈlife</b></td><td>拼命地；为了活命</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Run for your life! A tiger has escaped from the circus!<br>快逃命吧!马戏团的一只老虎逃出来了!。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hold sb/sth ˈdear (formal)</b></td><td>珍视；珍爱</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>He laughed at the ideas they held dear.<br>他们视若妙计的东西他却觉得可笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at death's ˈdoor (often ironic)</b></td><td>生命垂危；病得快不行了</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Come You're not at death's door yet!<br>起来，下床吧，你还没有到行将就木的时候!</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>be ˌin at the ˈdeath/kill</b></td><td>亲眼目睹结局（或败局）</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Iwas in at the kill when she finally lost her job.<br>我亲眼见到她最终被炒了鱿鱼。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>like death warmed ˈup (BrE) (AmE like death warmed ˈover) (informal)</b></td><td>面色极差；累（或病）得要命</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You look like death warmed up — go home and get some sleep.<br>你脸色难看得要命，回家睡一觉吧。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put sb to ˈdeath</b></td><td>处死某人</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The prisoner will be put to death in your most private thoughts; in reality rather at dawn.<br>这名囚犯将在黎明时被处死。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to the ˈdeath</b></td><td>至死方休；战斗到底</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>They swore to defend their village to the death.<br>他们发誓要誓死保卫自己的村子。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>get/ˌrun into ˈdebt</b></td><td>负债；欠下债务</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>After she lost her job, she began to run into debt.<br>失业后她开始欠债。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>deep ˈdown (informal)</b></td><td>内心深处；实际上</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He acts confident, but deep down he's terrified of failing again.<br>他装得很自信，其实心底怕极了再失败。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>in deep ˈwater(s)</b></td><td>陷入困境；麻烦缠身</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The company is in deep water after losing its biggest client.<br>丢了最大的客户后，公司陷入了大麻烦。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jump in/be thrown in at the ˈdeep end</b></td><td>一上来就被推去做难事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>On my first day I was thrown in at the deep end with angry customers.<br>上班第一天我就被推去应付发火的顾客。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>by deˈfault</b></td><td>因无人竞争而（获胜）；默认地</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The other team didn't even turn up, so we won by default.<br>另一个队根本没有到场，我们不战而胜。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in deˈfault of sth (formal)</b></td><td>因为没有；由于缺乏</td><td>★<br>★</td><td>They accepted what he had said in default of any evidence to disprove it.<br>由于没有相反的证据，他们相信了他的话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on/onto the deˈfensive</b></td><td>处于守势；采取戒备姿态</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Their questions about the money put her on the defensive.<br>他们问到钱的问题，使她警觉起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>by deˈgrees</b></td><td>逐渐地；一点点地</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The country's economy won't improve straight away, but will only get better by degrees.<br>国家的经济不会马上好转，但会逐渐有起色。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>déjà ˈvu (from French)</b></td><td>似曾相识的感觉</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Ihad a strong sense of deja vu as I walked into the room.<br>走进房间时，我有种强烈的似曾相识的感觉。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>the ˌdevil looks after his ˈown (saying)</b></td><td>坏人反倒走运；恶人自有魔鬼护佑</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>He crashed the car and walked away unhurt — the devil looks after his own.<br>他撞了车却毫发无伤，真是坏人有坏福。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>a/the ˈdevil of a job, nuisance, fellow, etc.</b></td><td>极费劲的事；极难缠的人</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>We're going to have a devil of ajob getting the roots of that tree out of the ground.<br>我们把那树根拔出来得费九牛二虎之力。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>die in your ˈbed</b></td><td>寿终正寝；善终</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>After all those wars he was lucky to die in his bed.<br>打了那么多仗，他能寿终正寝算是幸运。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>make a, no, some, etc. ˈdifference (to/in sb/sth)</b></td><td>有（或没有、有些）影响；起作用</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Your age shouldn't make any difference to whether you get the job.<br>你能否得到这份工作，不该跟年龄有关。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>same ˈdifference (spoken)</b></td><td>还不都一样；没什么区别</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Bus or train, same difference — we'll still be late.<br>坐公交还是坐火车，还不都一样，反正要迟到。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be in a different ˈleague</b></td><td>不是一个档次；高出一大截</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The new designs are in a different league from those that have been used before.<br>这些新款设计水准很高，之前所用的根本不能与之同日而语。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a different kettle of ˈfish (informal)</b></td><td>另一码事；截然不同的事</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You may be able to read French well, but speaking it fluently is a different kettle of fish entirely.<br>你也许能很顺畅地阅读法语，但要流利地说法语就是另一码事了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>different ˈstrokes (for different ˈfolks) (AmE)</b></td><td>人各有所好</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He collects stamps and I collect records — different strokes for different folks.<br>他集邮我收唱片，各有各的爱好。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dig deep</b></td><td>深挖细查；（也指）慷慨解囊</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Youll need to dig deep into the records to find the figures you want.<br>你必须仔细查阅档案才能找到你需要的数据。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dig your ˈheels in (informal)</b></td><td>拒不让步；固执己见</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>A number of councils have dug their heels in over the government's request to reduce spending.<br>几个委员会在政府要求削减开支的问题上拒不让步。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dig your own ˈgrave • dig a ˈgrave for yourself</b></td><td>自掘坟墓；自取灭亡</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>By lying to the auditors he was digging his own grave.<br>对审计员撒谎，他这是在自掘坟墓。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dig yourself (into) a ˈhole</b></td><td>使自己陷入难以脱身的困境</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The more he explained, the deeper he dug himself into a hole.<br>他越解释，把自己陷得越深。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be beˈneath sb's ˈdignity (often ironic)</b></td><td>有失身份；有损尊严</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Apparently washing his own coffee cup is beneath his dignity.<br>看来自己洗咖啡杯有失他的身份。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stand on your ˈdignity (formal)</b></td><td>摆架子；坚持要受到应有的礼遇</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>The teacher stood on his dignity and insisted that the students be punished for being rude to him.<br>那位老师坚持要惩罚那些对自己无礼的学生以维护自己的尊严。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on a ˈdime (AmE) (BrE less frequent on a ˈsixpence)</b></td><td>在极小的范围内；说停就停</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>A 3000 ton train doesn't stop on a dime.<br>载重 3000 吨的火车无法在短距离内停下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌnickel-and-ˈdime (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>为小钱斤斤计较；微不足道的</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Stop nickel-and-diming the staff over parking fees and coffee.<br>别在停车费和咖啡上跟员工斤斤计较了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get your ˈhands dirty</b></td><td>亲自动手干活；沾手不干净的事</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>A good manager isn't afraid to get their hands dirty on site.<br>好经理不怕到现场亲自动手。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr class="sec"><td colspan="4">D</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dirty great/big (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>极大的；大得不得了</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>When I turned round of problems, is a failure, or is badly organized he was pointing a dirty great gun at me.<br>我转过问题重重(或乱七八糟)的地方；灾难性局面: 身时，他用一支老大的枪对准了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a dirty ˈword</b></td><td>犯忌的字眼；忌讳的说法</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>In this office the word 'overtime' has become a dirty word.<br>在这间办公室里，「加班」成了忌讳的字眼。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do the ˈdirty on sb (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>对某人使坏；暗算某人</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>He did the dirty on his partner and took all the profits.<br>他暗算了合伙人，独吞了全部利润。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌdish the ˈdirt (on sb) (informal)</b></td><td>揭某人的隐私；说人闲话</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>When the newspaper offered her £10 000, she was only too happy to dish the dirt on her friends.<br>报纸出价1 万英镑，这使她非常乐意揭朋友的短。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at your/sb's disˈposal</b></td><td>供某人随意使用；由某人支配</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>He will have a car at his disposal for the whole month.<br>他将有一辆汽车归他使用整整一个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do sb a disˈservice</b></td><td>对某人不公；损害某人</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The minister's comments do teachers a great disservice.<br>部长的评论对教师大为不利。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at/from a ˈdistance</b></td><td>从远处；隔着一段距离</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She had loved him at a distance for years.<br>她曾经暗恋了他好多年。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go the (full) ˈdistance</b></td><td>坚持到底；打满全场</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Nobody thought he would last 15 rounds but he went the full distance.<br>谁都以为他坚持不了15 个回合，可他却打满了全场。</td></tr>

Instead of saying how serious the housing situation was, he was telling jokes about it.<br>我真的认为他在会议上的发言不甚恰当。本来应该说说住房情况有多么严峻，他却拿这事开起</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>as, whenever, etc. the fancy ˈtakes you</b></td><td>只要你高兴；随你的意</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>We bought a camper van so we could go away whenever the fancy took us.<br>我们买了一辆露营车，所以无论什么时候，只要我们愿意就可以出去。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>as/so ˈfar as...</b></td><td>就…而言；到…程度</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Iwill help you as far as I almost the opposite of sth or of what is am able.<br>我会尽我所能帮助你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>as far as the eye can/could ˈsee</b></td><td>一望无际；视线所及之处</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>There were sunflower fields as far as the eye could see.<br>向日葵田一望无际。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>far and ˈwide</b></td><td>到处；四面八方</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>People come from far and wide say or do sth which is considered too extreme to visit the monument.<br>人们从各地前来参观这座</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a far ˈcry from sth</b></td><td>与…相去甚远；大不相同</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>This tiny flat is a far cry from the house we had in the country.<br>这间小公寓和我们乡下那栋房子天差地别。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>far ˈfrom it (informal)</b></td><td>完全不是；恰恰相反</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Is he generous? Far from it, he spends everything on himself.<br>他大方吗？才不呢，钱全花自己身上了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in so ˈfar as (also insoˈfar as)</b></td><td>就…而言；在…范围内</td><td>★★★<br>★</td><td>In so far as I am a judge of these things, the repairs to the car have been done very well.<br>要我来评判，这车修得非常好。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>leave sb in possession of the ˈfield</b></td><td>让某人独占优势；使某人成为赢家</td><td>★<br>★</td><td>Many of our more experienced players are injured or resting, which leaves the field clear for new talent.<br>很多经验丰富的选手都有伤在身或正在休养，这样就给了新秀上场的机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>play the ˈfield (informal)</b></td><td>广交异性；不固定交往</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He told me he didn't want to get married yet because he was having too much fun playing the field.<br>他告诉我他还不想结婚，因为现在到处留情的生活很享受。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>something ˈfierce (AmE, spoken)</b></td><td>非常；厉害地</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Isure do miss you something fierce!<br>我当然非常想你!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take/plead the ˈfifth (AmE)</b></td><td>援引第五修正案拒绝作答</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The witness took the fifth rather than name his business partners.<br>证人援引第五修正案，拒绝说出生意伙伴的名字。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fight ˌfire with ˈfire</b></td><td>以其人之道还治其人之身</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The only way we can win this match is to fight fire with fire.<br>我们要赢得这场比赛，唯一的办法就是以其人之道还治其人之身。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fight for (your) ˈlife</b></td><td>拼命求生；奋力保命</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>A young cyclist is fighting for his life after the accident.<br>一位年轻的自行车手出事故后奋力求生。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fight it ˈout</b></td><td>一决高下；决出胜负</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The two finalists will fight it out on Sunday afternoon.<br>两位决赛选手将在周日下午一决高下。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fight like cat and ˈdog (informal)</b></td><td>像猫狗一样争吵不休</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>They fight like cat and dog, but they are really very fond of each other.<br>他们常常吵得鸡飞狗跳，但其实他们感情很好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fight a ˌlosing ˈbattle</b></td><td>打一场无望取胜的仗</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Trying to keep the kitchen tidy with four kids is fighting a losing battle.<br>带着四个孩子想保持厨房整洁，纯属徒劳。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fight your ˈown battles</b></td><td>自己解决问题；独立应对</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I wouldn't get involved— he's old enough to fight his own battles.<br>我不想卷入其中了——他已经长大，可以独力应付了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fight ˈshy of sth/of doing sth</b></td><td>回避；避免（做）某事</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Itend to fight shy of getting involved in protests, but in this case I feel very strongly that we should complain.<br>我一般不愿抱怨，但这次我觉得我们完全应该提意见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fight ˌtooth and ˈnail (for sb/sth/to do sth)</b></td><td>拼命抗争；全力争取</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We fought the government tooth and nail to prevent the new road being built.<br>我们为了阻止修建那条新路而和政府全力斗争。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>a ˌfighting ˈchance</b></td><td>尚有希望的机会</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>With five minutes left, our team still has a fighting chance.<br>还剩五分钟，我们队仍有一线获胜的机会。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be in with a ˈchance (of doing sth) (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>有获胜（或成功）的可能</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>John Brown is still in with a chance of winning the nomination.<br>约翰·布朗仍有机会拿到提名。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fighting ˈspirit</b></td><td>斗志；顽强的意志</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Come on, don't give up now! Where's your fighting spirit?<br>嗨，别放弃!你的斗志到哪儿去了？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fighting ˈtalk</b></td><td>挑战性的言论；豪言壮语</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>What we want from the management is fighting talk.<br>我们想让管理层发出挑战宣言。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a figment of sb's imagiˈnation</b></td><td>凭空想象的事物；虚构之事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Doctor, are you suggesting the pain is a figment of my imagination?<br>医生，你是说这疼痛是我想象出来的喽？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cut a fine, poor, sorry, etc. ˈfigure</b></td><td>显得出众（或狼狈、可怜等）</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>In his brand new uniform he cut a fine figure.<br>他穿着崭新的制服，看上去一表人才。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a figure of ˈfun</b></td><td>笑柄；被人取笑的对象</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>As a young man he was admired, but as an old man he became a figure of fun.<br>年轻时，他受人崇拜；到老了，却被人嘲笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go ˈfigure (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>真搞不懂；你说怪不怪</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>At the same tume that I was criticized for working too fast I was accused of working too slow. Go figure!<br>有人批评我工作太快，但同时又有人说我工作太慢， 真是搞不懂!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put a ˈfigure on sth</b></td><td>给出确切数字（或价值）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>It's difficult to Put a figure on a table like this, but it's probably worth about $5 000.<br>像这样的桌子很难定价，可能值5000美元左右吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it/that ˈfigures (informal)</b></td><td>那就说得通了；不奇怪</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He was late again? That figures, he missed the early train.<br>他又迟到了？不奇怪，他没赶上早班车。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(in) single/Indian ˈfile</b></td><td>排成一列纵队</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The whole class walked along behind the teacher in single file.<br>全班排成一队跟在老师的后面走过来。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fill sb's ˈboots/ˈshoes</b></td><td>接替某人（并胜任其职）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Mr Carter is retiring and we need a new director to fill his shoes.<br>卡特先生要退休了，我们需要一位新主管接替他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have had your ˈfill of sb/sth</b></td><td>受够了某人（或某事）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Tve had my fill of Star Wars movies. I never want to see another one as long as I live.<br>我已经看够了 《星球大战》，我这辈子再也不要看了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>find ˈfault (with sb/sth)</b></td><td>挑毛病；找茬儿</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He's always finding fault with the children, even when they are doing nothing wrong.<br>他总是对孩子们吹毛求疵，尽管有时他们根本没做错什么。1</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>find your ˈvoice/ˈtongue (informal)</b></td><td>终于开口说话；不再怯场</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>He sat silent through the first half of the meeting before he found his tongue.<br>他一直坐着不吭声，会都开了一半，他才缓过神来开口说话。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>take sb as you ˈfind them</b></td><td>接受某人的本来面目</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The house is in chaos, so when you come you must take us as you find us.<br>房子乱糟糟的，来了别见笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌfinders ˈkeepers (saying)</b></td><td>谁捡到就归谁</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He kept the coin he found in the park, finders keepers.<br>他把公园里捡到的硬币留下了，谁捡到归谁嘛。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>work your ˌfingers to the ˈbone (informal)</b></td><td>拼命干活；不停手地干</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It's not fair —Iwork my fingers to the bone all day and then I have to cook and clean in the evenings.<br>这不公平。我白天拼命工作，晚上还得做饭，打扫</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have sth at your ˈfingertips</b></td><td>对…了如指掌；随时可用</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The director was well prepared for the interview. She had all the facts at her fingertips.<br>经理为这次采访作了充分的准备，她对所有的事实了如指掌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to your ˈfingertips (BrE)</b></td><td>彻头彻尾；十足地</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>He is an artist to his fingertips.<br>他是个十足的艺术家。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be in at the ˈfinish</b></td><td>结束时在场；见证最后阶段</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>I was one of the first people on this project and I certainly want to be in at the finish.<br>我是最早参加这个项目的人之一，当然也希望能参与到最后。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the finishing ˈtouch(es)</b></td><td>最后的修饰；收尾工作</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Weve been putting finishing touches to the party decorations.<br>我们在给派对的装饰作最后的布置。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/come under ˈfire</b></td><td>遭到攻击；受到抨击</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>While defending the town we came under fire again last night.<br>昨晚保卫城市时，我们再次遭炮火袭击。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fire ˈquestions, ˈinsults, etc. at sb</b></td><td>连珠炮般地发问（或辱骂）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The room was full of journalists, all firing questions at them.<br>满屋都是记者，连珠炮般向他们发问。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hold your ˈfire</b></td><td>暂不开火；先别发作</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Hold your fire! I think they're going to surrender.<br>先别开枪!我想他们要投降了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on ˈfire</b></td><td>着火；火辣辣；状态火热</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He couldn't breathe. His chest was on fire.<br>他没法呼吸，胸口火烧火燎地疼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>play with ˈfire</b></td><td>玩火；冒不必要的危险</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Be very careful, Mike. You're Playing with fire.<br>小心点，迈克，你这是在玩火。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>set sth on ˈfire</b></td><td>点燃；纵火焚烧</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Three youths were accused of setting the house on fire.<br>三名青年被指控纵火焚烧那所房子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be in the ˈfiring line (BrE) (AmE be on the ˈfiring line)</b></td><td>首当其冲；处于易受批评之位</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The newspapers are critcizing the government's policy again, and the Prime Minister is in the firing line.<br>报界又在攻击</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be on firm ˈground</b></td><td>有把握；立场稳固</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I don't know a lot about physics, I'm afraid. I'm on firmer ground with mathematics, which I studied at university.<br>我恐怕对物理知道得不多，但是对数学我比较有自信，我在大学学过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a firm ˈhand</b></td><td>严格的管教；铁腕</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>What his son needs, if you ask me,is a firm hand!<br>要我说，他儿子需要的是严加管束!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hold ˈfirm (to sth) (formal)</b></td><td>坚持；不动摇</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>She held firm to her principles.<br>她坚持自己的原则。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take a firm ˈline/stand (on/against sth)</b></td><td>对…采取坚定立场</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The school takes a firm line on bullying of any kind.<br>学校对任何形式的欺凌都态度坚决。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>come ˈfirst</b></td><td>最重要；被放在首位</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>His work always came first with Joe, which upset his wife a lot.<br>乔总是把工作放在第一位，这让他的妻子很不高兴。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>first among ˈequals</b></td><td>同级中居首位者</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Our history classes were usually open discussion-groups between us and our teacher, with the teacher as frst among equals.<br>我们的历史课通常都是师生一起分成小组公开讨论，由老师来主持。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌfirst and ˈforemost</b></td><td>首先；最重要的是</td><td>★★★★<br>★★</td><td>First and foremost, we need to make the building safe.<br>首要的是把这栋楼弄安全。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>first and ˈlast</b></td><td>归根到底；从头至尾就是</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The book is, first and last, an account of a poet's development.<br>这本书主要来讲是对诗人成长历程的记述。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(at) first ˈhand</b></td><td>第一手地；直接地</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I know at first hand what it is like to be poor; we always had very little money at home.<br>我对贫穷有切身的体验，我们家从来没什么钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>first ˈoff/ˈup (informal)</b></td><td>首先；第一件事</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>First off, we will choose the teams, then we can start the game.<br>首先，我们挑选队伍，然后开始比赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(give sb, have, etc.) (the) first reˈfusal</b></td><td>（给予或拥有）优先购买权</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>She promised to give me first refusal if she ever decides to sell the flat.<br>她答应一旦决定出售公寓，一定先问一下我要不要买。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>first ˈthing (tomorrow, in the morning, etc.)</b></td><td>（明早等）一开始就；头一件事</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I always like a cup of tea first thing in the morning.<br>我早上总是喜欢先喝杯茶。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(be) the ˈfirst/ˈlast (person) to do sth</b></td><td>（是）最（不）会做某事的人</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I'd be the first person to admit that I'm not perfect.<br>我会第一个承认自己不是完人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from the (very) ˈfirst</b></td><td>从一开始</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>They were attracted to each other from the first.<br>他俩一见倾心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from ˌfirst to ˈlast</b></td><td>从头到尾；自始至终</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>It's a fine performance that commands attention from first to last.<br>这场演出很精彩，从头到尾都引人入胜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have first ˈcall (on sb/sth)</b></td><td>有优先权；须优先照顾</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The children always have first call on her time.<br>孩子们总是她最放在心上的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the ˈfirst instance (formal)</b></td><td>首先；第一步</td><td>★★★<br>★</td><td>In the first instance, notify the police and then contact your insurance company.<br>首先通知警方，然后同保险公司联系。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the ˈfirst place</b></td><td>首先；当初</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>In the first place it's not your car, and in the second you're not old enough to drive it. Is that clear?<br>首先，这不是你的车；其次，你太小了，还不能开年。你明白了吗？ 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make the first ˈmove</b></td><td>采取主动；率先行动</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ifhe wants to see me, he should make the first move.<br>如果他想见我的话，他就得主动。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put sb/sth ˈfirst</b></td><td>把…放在首位</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>A politician should always put the needs of the country first and not his personal ambitions.<br>政治家应当总是先考虑国家的需要，而不是他个人的志向。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>there's a ˌfirst time for ˈeverything (saying, humorous)</b></td><td>凡事都有第一次</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You cooked dinner? Well, there's a first time for everything.<br>你居然做饭了？凡事都有第一次嘛。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fish for compliments</b></td><td>转弯抹角地讨人恭维；沽名钓誉</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Stop asking me if you look OK. You're just fishing for compliments.<br>别再问我你看上去是不是得体了， 你不过是想让我说好话罢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fish or cut ˈbait (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>要么动手要么拉倒；快作抉择</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>There s been enough discussion.It's time for the government to fish or cut bait.<br>讨论得已经够多了，政府该下决心采取行动了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌfish out of ˈwater (informal)</b></td><td>不适应环境的人；不得其所的人</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Everybody else knew each other really well, so I felt a bit like a fish out of water.<br>别人彼此都知根知底，我觉得有点不自在。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>(there are) no flies on sb (informal)</b></td><td>某人很精明；不容易上当</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>You can't just tell her that youve lost the money; she'll never believe you. There are no flies on Jane,you know.<br>你不能就告诉她把钱弄丢了，她绝不会相信的。你要知道简才不是傻瓜呢。 2</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>take ˈflight</b></td><td>逃走；仓皇而逃</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The gang took flight when they heard the police car.<br>歹徒们听到警车声就逃跑了。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>ˌflog a dead ˈhorse (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>白费力气；做无用功</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Pam's flogging a dead horse trying to organixe the theatre trip. It's quite obvious that nobody's interested.<br>帕姆想组织剧团巡回演出，无疑是白费心机。很明显没有人感兴趣。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flog sth to ˈdeath (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>把某事说滥；反复使用以致乏味</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>That advertising slogan has been flogged to death over the past year.<br>那句广告语这一年被用滥了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>flood the ˈmarket</b></td><td>大量抛售商品；充斥市场</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Importers flooded the market with cheap toys just before Christmas.<br>进口商们在圣诞节前大量抛售廉价玩具。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be in ˈfloods (of ˈtears) (informal)</b></td><td>泪如雨下；痛哭流涕</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She was in floods of tears after a row with her family.<br>她和家人大吵一场后痛哭流涕。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>the ˌfeathers/ˌfur/ˌsparks will ˈfly (informal)</b></td><td>会大吵一架；会闹得不可开交</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The fur will really fly when she tells him he can't g0 out tonight.<br>等她告诉他他今晚不能出去时，肯定会大闹一场。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>fly ˈhigh</b></td><td>非常成功；事业兴旺</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The business is flying high at the moment, making large profits and attracting a lot of investors.<br>目前企业红红火火， 盈利颇丰，吸引了众多投资者。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fly in the face of ˈsth (written)</b></td><td>公然违抗；与……背道而驰</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Such a proposal is flying in the face of common sense.<br>这种提议有悖于常理。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a/the fly in the ˈointment (informal)</b></td><td>美中不足之处；扫兴的因素</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We lead a very happy life here. The only fly in the ointment is that there's too much traffic on our road.<br>我们在这儿过得很快活，唯一美中不足的就是住处旁边马路上的车辆太多了。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>have a lot, something, nothing, etc. ˈgoing for you</b></td><td>有很多（或一些）有利条件</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>As the very intelligent daughter of rich parents, she's got a lot going for her.<br>出身富家又天资聪颖，她拥有很多优势。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get out while the ˌgoing/ˌgetting is ˈgood</b></td><td>趁形势尚可及早抽身</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He thinks the company is going to g0 bankrupt soon, so he's getting out while the going is good.<br>他认为公司即将破产，所以就趁境况还没</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌall that ˌglitters/ˌglistens/ˌglisters is not ˈgold (saying)</b></td><td>闪光的未必都是金子</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The job sounded glamorous, but all that glitters is not gold.<br>那份工作听着光鲜，可闪光的未必都是金子。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌall that ˌglitters is not ˈgold (saying)</b></td><td>发光的未必都是金子；表面好未必实在</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Don't imagine that because they are rich, they are happy. All that glitters is not gold.<br>不要以为他们有钱就一定很幸福。有些事不能只看表面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈgold mine</b></td><td>金矿；摇钱树</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>That Internet cafe of his is a real gold mine.<br>他开的那家网吧真是棵摇钱树。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(as) good as ˈgold</b></td><td>（小孩）非常乖；很听话</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The children were good as gold. They sat quietly and read all afternoon.<br>孩子们乖得很，整个下午都静静地坐着看书。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>like ˈgold dust</b></td><td>极其稀缺；一票难求</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You can't get those new trainers anywhere. They're like gold dust.<br>你在哪儿也买不到那些新款运动鞋，它们就跟砂金一样难找。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˈgolden age (of sth)</b></td><td>黄金时代；全盛时期</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>This book looks back on the golden age of steam engines, and all railway fans will enjoy it immensely.<br>这本书回顾了蒸汽机的黄金时代， 所有的铁路迷都会非常喜欢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈgolden boy</b></td><td>红人；备受赏识的年轻人</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He had been the golden boy of Welsh rugby.<br>他曾是威尔士橄榄球界的骄子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(kill) the golden ˈgoose (also (kill) the goose that lays the golden ˈegg/ˈeggs)</b></td><td>杀鸡取卵；自断财源</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The government is worried that a new tax might kill the golden goose by scaring away foreign investment.<br>政府担心新税收会吓跑外国投资者，从而断了财路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(kill) the goose that lays the golden ˈeggs</b></td><td>自毁财源；杀鸡取卵</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>However, by killing the goose that lays the golden eggs, the farmer lost everything.<br>然而农夫杀了那只下金蛋的鹅，结果一无所有。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a golden ˈhandshake</b></td><td>巨额退职金；高额解雇费</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The leave their job directors will each get a large golden handshake and a pension.<br>所有的经理都会得到丰厚的退职金和养老费。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the golden ˈrule</b></td><td>金科玉律；首要准则</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>When you're playing a stroke in golf, the golden rule is to keep your eye on the ball.<br>打高尔夫球时，最重要的是眼睛要紧盯着球。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>all to the ˈgood</b></td><td>那更好；有益无害</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>If the train arrives early, that's all to the good.<br>火车要是早到，那更好。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>as ˈgood as...</b></td><td>几乎；简直等于</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The repair is as good as finished—just one screw left.<br>修理基本上完工了，只剩一颗螺丝。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>be ˈgood for sth</b></td><td>能提供（钱等）；能维持</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Tl ask my aunt if she can help us. Shell be good for a small loan, I'm sure.<br>我去问问姨妈看她是否能帮帮咱们，我相信她可能会借我们一小笔钱的。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be no ˈgood • not be any/much ˈgood</b></td><td>没有用；不管用</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>This gadget isn't much g0od.<br>这玩意儿没什么用。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do ˈgood</b></td><td>做好事；行善</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She left the bank to do good in a rural health charity.<br>她离开银行，去一家乡村医疗慈善机构做善事。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>cut/untie the ˌGordian ˈknot</b></td><td>快刀斩乱麻；果断解决难题</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Will the negotiators be able to untie the Gordian knot?<br>这些谈判者能够果断地解决这个难题吗？ ②</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>with (a) good/bad ˈgrace</b></td><td>有风度地；不情愿地</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>It is very important in sport to accept defeat with good grace.<br>在体育竞技中能输得有风度是很</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>a/the ˌgrand old ˈage</b></td><td>高龄</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She finally learned to drive at the grand old age of 65.<br>她最终在65岁高龄学会了开车。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>turn in his, her, etc. ˈgrave (BrE) (AmE roll in his, her, etc. ˈgrave)</b></td><td>（死者）九泉之下也不安宁</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Grandma would turn in her grave if she saw what we did to the kitchen.<br>要是奶奶看见我们把厨房改成这样，准会气得在坟里翻身。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˈgravy train (informal, especially AmE)</b></td><td>轻松赚钱的美差；肥缺</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Consultants have been riding the gravy train on this project for years.<br>这个项目上的顾问们轻轻松松捞了好几年。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>hope against ˈhope (that...)</b></td><td>抱着一线希望；仍存幻想</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We hoped against hope that the letter had simply been delayed.<br>我们抱着一线希望，觉得信只是寄晚了。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>I should ˈhope so/not ◆ so I should ˈhope</b></td><td>希望如此；但愿不会如此</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You mean he apologized at last? I should hope so, after all that.<br>你是说他终于道歉了？闹成那样，本该如此。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not have a ˌhope in ˈhell (informal)</b></td><td>毫无机会；根本没戏</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You haven't got a hope in hell of waning the race — you're far too slow!<br>你根本无望取胜，你跑得太慢了!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not a ˈhope ◆ some ˈhope(s)! (BrE, spoken)</b></td><td>毫无希望；休想</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Some hope of your becoming manager — you're far too lazy!<br>你丝毫没有当经理的希望，你太懒了!。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>build up/raise sb's ˈhopes</b></td><td>使某人满怀希望</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Don't raise her hopes too much. She may not win.<br>不要让她抱太大希望，她不一定会赢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>dash/shatter sb's ˈhopes</b></td><td>使某人的希望破灭</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Any hopes that the museum would be built this year were dashed yesterday when the council announced its plans to spend less money on the arts.<br>政务委员会昨天宣布削减艺术事业开支的计划，这让今年修建博物馆的希望落空了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌhopping ˈmad (about/over sth) (informal)</b></td><td>暴跳如雷；气得跳脚</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Mum was hopping mad about the mess we'd left in the kitchen.<br>我们把厨房弄得一团糟，妈妈气得跳脚。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the hoˈrizon</b></td><td>即将发生；已露端倪</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The change of government means that there are new developments on the horizon.<br>政府改组意味着即将进入一个新的发展阶段。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈhornet's nest</b></td><td>马蜂窝；一大堆麻烦</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>When Charles got the manager's job, it stirred up a real hornet's nest, because everyone was angry about his fast promotion.<br>查尔斯当上经理简直像捅了马蜂窝，大家对他升职这么快感到很不满。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>draw/pull in your ˈhorns</b></td><td>收敛；缩减开支</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>After making huge losses, the company had to draw in its horns by cancelling some major projects.<br>遭受严重亏损后，公司不得不取消一些重大项目以减少开支。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(on) the horns of a diˈlemma</b></td><td>进退两难</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>I'm really on the horns of a dilemma. I need the car but I can't afford it.<br>我真是左右为难。我需要车，但都买不起。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take the ˈbull by the horns</b></td><td>迎难而上；果断处理难题</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He took the bull by the horns and asked his boss for a raise.<br>他鼓起勇气，直接向老板提了加薪。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌhorror of ˈhorrors (BrE, humorous or ironic)</b></td><td>（用于强调）糟糕透顶</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>I stood up to speak and - horror of horrors — realized I had left my notes behind.<br>我站起来讲话，可糟糕的是，我发现自己忘了带提纲。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(straight) from the horse's ˈmouth (informal)</b></td><td>（消息）直接来自当事人；可靠</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I heard it straight from the horse's mouth — she's leaving in June.<br>我是从当事人那儿听来的，她六月就走。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>you can ˌtake/ˌlead a horse to ˌwater, but you ˌcan't make it ˈdrink (saying)</b></td><td>牛不喝水不能强按头</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>I've offered him lessons twice; you can lead a horse to water, but you can't make it drink.<br>我给他找了两次课，牛不喝水强按头也没用。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>close/shut the stable ˈdoor after the horse has bolted</b></td><td>亡羊补牢；为时已晚</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Installing an alarm now is shutting the stable door after the horse has bolted.<br>现在才装警报器，早就为时已晚了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>change/swap horses in midˈstream</b></td><td>中途换将；中途改变计划</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>We're halfway through the build, so let's not change horses in midstream.<br>工程都盖到一半了，别在这时候临阵换人。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hold your ˈhorses (informal)</b></td><td>且慢；沉住气</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Hold your horses — we haven't even read the contract yet.<br>别急，合同我们还没看呢。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>horses for ˈcourses (BrE)</b></td><td>知人善任；因事择人</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Put Ana on the phones and Sam on design — horses for courses.<br>让安娜接电话，山姆做设计，各尽所长。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌhostage to ˈfortune</b></td><td>可能招致后患的言行</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>Promising to cut taxes twice was a hostage to fortune he later regretted.<br>两度承诺减税成了后患，他后来很后悔。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌhot off the ˈpress (informal)</b></td><td>刚印出来的；最新出炉的</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>These figures are hot off the press, so nobody else has seen them.<br>这些数据刚刚出炉，别人都还没见过。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hot on sb's/sth's ˈtracks/ˈtrail (informal)</b></td><td>紧追不舍；即将追上</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The detectives were hot on his trail by the time he reached the border.<br>他到边境时，警探已紧追不舍。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a hot poˈtato (informal)</b></td><td>棘手问题；烫手山芋</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>School closures are a political hot potato nobody wants to touch.<br>关闭学校是个烫手山芋，没有政客愿碰。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈhot spot (informal)</b></td><td>热门去处；动乱地区</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>That street is the city's newest hot spot for live music.<br>那条街是全城最新的现场音乐热门去处。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hot ˈstuff (informal, especially BrE)</b></td><td>了不起的人（或事物）；性感的人</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He's really hot stuff as a tennis player.<br>他确实是网球高手。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>hot under the ˈcollar (informal)</b></td><td>恼火；气恼不安</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He gets very hot under the collar if people disagree with him.<br>别人要是跟他有分歧， 他就很生气。 €500</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in hot purˈsuit (of sb/sth)</b></td><td>紧追不舍</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He grabbed the jewels and ran, with several customers in hot pursuit.<br>他抓起珠宝就跑，几名顾客在后面穷追不舍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the ˈhot seat (informal)</b></td><td>身处要职；面临质询</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Our radio is on transport, and the Minister of Transport will be in the hot seat, ready to answer your questions.<br>今天我们的听众来电直播节目的主题是交通，交通部长将会直面大家的质疑和批评，并回答大家的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in hot ˈwater (informal)</b></td><td>陷入麻烦；惹上事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She got into hot water for being late.<br>她因迟到遇到些麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make it ˈhot for sb (informal)</b></td><td>刁难某人；让某人不好过</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>If you insist on staying here, I can make it very hot for you.<br>你要是坚持呆在这儿，我会让你日子很难过的。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>not so/too ˈhot (informal)</b></td><td>不太好；不太舒服</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I'm feeling not so hot today, so I'll skip the run.<br>我今天不太舒服，就不去跑步了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sell/go like ˈhot cakes (informal)</b></td><td>畅销；热卖</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The band's latest record is selling like hot cakes.<br>乐队的最新专辑正在热卖中。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>too ˈhot for sb (also too hot to ˈhandle)</b></td><td>太棘手；难以应付</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>When the scandal became public, things got too hot for the Minister and she resigned.<br>丑闻传出后，形势对部长非常不利，她只得辞职。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈhotfoot it (informal)</b></td><td>疾走；急忙赶去</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>Once the police arrived, we hotfooted it out of there.<br>警察一到，我们就急忙离开了那里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get/have the ˈhots for sb (informal)</b></td><td>对某人有强烈的情欲</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I reckon Jim's really got the hots for you!<br>我想吉姆真的迷上你了!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at an unˌearthly/unˌgodly ˈhour (informal)</b></td><td>在极早（或极晚）的时刻</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The job involved getting up at some unearthly hour to catch the first train.<br>做这份工作要很早起床赶第 -班火车。0</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>on the ˈhour/ˈhalf-hour</b></td><td>在整点（或半点）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Buses to the airport leave on the hour from stand four.<br>去机场的班车每逢整点从四号站台发车。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a house of ˈcards</b></td><td>纸牌屋；不牢靠的计划</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>His plans collapsed like a house of cards when the scholarship fell through.<br>奖学金没拿到，他的计划顿时土崩瓦解。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>at ˈall hours</b></td><td>随时；不分昼夜</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Their neighbours play music at all hours and nobody dares complain.<br>他们邻居不分昼夜地放音乐，没人敢抱怨。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˈsmall/ˈearly hours (also the ˌwee (small) ˈhours)</b></td><td>深夜；凌晨</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>They sat talking in the kitchen into the small hours of the morning.<br>他们在厨房里一直聊到凌晨。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>work all the ˈhours God sends (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>没日没夜地干活</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>He works all the hours God sends just to pay the mortgage.<br>为了还房贷，他没日没夜地干。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>till/until ˈall hours</b></td><td>直到深夜（或次日凌晨）</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She sat up till all hours halfway -a halfway house trying to finish her essay.<br>她为把文章写完熬夜到</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not give sb/sth ˈhouseroom (BrE)</b></td><td>绝不要；根本看不上</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>That ugly old sofa? I wouldn't give it houseroom.<br>那张丑沙发？白送我也不要。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get on/along like a ˈhouse on fire (informal)</b></td><td>一见如故；相处极为融洽</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>My mother and my girlfriend got on like a house on fire at dinner.<br>晚饭时我妈和我女友一见如故。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a household ˈname/ˈword</b></td><td>家喻户晓的人（或名称）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Within two years the little brand had become a household name.<br>短短两年，这个小品牌就变得家喻户晓。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go all round the ˈhouses (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>绕圈子；拐弯抹角</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ifyou want to ask her something, just ask her directly — there's no need to go all round the houses!<br>你要是想问她，就直接问吧，不用这么拐弯抹角!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>shout, etc. sth from the ˈhousetops/ˈrooftops (informal)</b></td><td>到处张扬；大肆宣扬</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He was so proud of the news he wanted to shout it from the rooftops.<br>这消息让他得意极了，恨不得昭告天下。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>how's ˈthis/ˈthat for a...? (informal)</b></td><td>这（那）个怎么样</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>How's this for a bargain — two jackets for the price of one.<br>这算不算便宜：两件夹克只收一件的钱。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>over the ˈhump (informal)</b></td><td>渡过最艰难的阶段</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Once the exams are finished we'll be over the hump for the year.<br>考完试，今年最难的一关就算过去了。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>the icing on the ˈcake</b></td><td>锦上添花</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The meal was perfect, the wonderful view from the restaurant the icing on the cake.<br>食物无可挑剔，而餐厅外的美景更是锦上添花。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>not have the ˈfaintest/ˈfoggiest/ˈslightest, etc. iˈdea</b></td><td>一无所知；毫无头绪</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Tve no idea what time it is.<br>我根本不知道现在几点了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>you have no iˈdea... (spoken)</b></td><td>你根本想象不到</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Youve no idea how much traffic there was tonight.<br>你难以想象今晚的交通有多拥挤。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the (very) iˈdea! (old-fashioned, spoken)</b></td><td>亏你想得出；真是的</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>She expected me to Pay for everything. The idea!<br>她指望我来支付所有的费用，想得美!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>run aˈway with the idea/notion (spoken)</b></td><td>轻率地相信；产生误解</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Don't run away with the idea that you're going to be famous just because you've appeared on television once.<br>别以为在电视上路过一次面，你就出名了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈthat's an idea! (spoken)</b></td><td>好主意</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Hey, that's an idea! And we could get a band, as well.<br>嗨，这可是个好主意!我们还可以找个乐队呢!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈthat's the idea! (spoken)</b></td><td>对，就是这样；做得对</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>That's the idea! You're doing just fine.<br>对啦!你做得不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give sb iˈdeas (also put iˈdeas in/into sb's head)</b></td><td>让某人想入非非</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Don't tell him about the bonus; you'll only give him ideas.<br>别跟他提奖金的事，那只会让他想入非非。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>if and ˈwhen</b></td><td>如果真的；倘若到时</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We'll discuss the budget if and when the project is approved.<br>项目一旦获批，我们再谈预算。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>if ˈanything</b></td><td>要说有什么不同的话；倒不如说</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The weather isn't better today; if anything, it's worse.<br>今天天气没变好，要说有变化，反倒更糟了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>if ˌI were ˈyou</b></td><td>要是我是你的话（用于提建议）</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>If I were you, I'd apologize before she hears it from someone else.<br>要是我，我会在她从别人那儿听说之前先道歉。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>if ˈnot</b></td><td>不然；要不（表示不同意见）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Business is good for the builders, if not for everybody else.<br>对建筑商来说生意不错，虽然别人未必如此。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>if ˈonly...</b></td><td>要是…就好了</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>If only she'd done what I told her, she immediate /rmidiat/ wouldn't be in this trouble.<br>她要是能按我说的做，就不会碰到这样的麻烦了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌifs and/or ˈbuts</b></td><td>种种借口；这样那样的条件</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I want the report on Monday, with no ifs and buts.<br>报告周一交，别跟我讲条件找借口。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ignorance is ˈbliss (saying)</b></td><td>无知是福；不知者不烦</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She never reads the news before bed — ignorance is bliss.<br>她睡前从不看新闻，眼不见心不烦。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>anything/nothing/something ˈin it for sb</b></td><td>对某人有（或没有）好处</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He wanted to know more about the business but I told him there was nothing in it for him.<br>他想多了解一些有关这笔交易的事，但我告诉他他并不能从中捞到什么好处。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>be ˈin for it (BrE also be ˈfor it) (informal)</b></td><td>要倒霉了；要挨罚了</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>We'd better hurry or well be in for it.<br>我们最好快一点，否则就该倒霉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/get ˈin on sth (informal)</b></td><td>参与；知情</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Everyone in the office was in on the plan except the birthday girl.<br>除了寿星本人，办公室里人人都知道这个计划。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/keep (well) ˈin with sb (informal)</b></td><td>与某人搞好关系（图好处）</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>If you want to do well in this company, keep well in with the boss.<br>你要是想在公司干得好，就要和上司处好关系。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in and ˈout (of sth)</b></td><td>进进出出；时常出入</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I've been in and out of the travel agency all this week, trying to arrange my holiday.<br>这个星期以来，为了安排度假， 我进进出出旅行社好几次。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈin that (written)</b></td><td>因为；在于</td><td>★★★<br>★</td><td>She 248 was fortunate in that she had friends to help her.<br>她很幸运，有朋友们帮着。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>under the ˈinfluence</b></td><td>酒后（驾车）；醉酒</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She was fined E500 for driving under the infiuence.<br>她因酒驾被罚了500英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>for your inforˈmation</b></td><td>供参考；需要说明的是</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>For your informatlon, I don't even have a car.<br>你要知道，我连辆车都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(do sth) on your own iˈnitiative</b></td><td>主动（做某事）；自作主张</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Did you ask him to organize a meeting, or was it on his own initiative?<br>是你让他组织的会议，还是他主动做的？ 1</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take the iˈnitiative</b></td><td>采取主动；率先行动</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>France took the initiative in the peace talks.<br>法国在和谈中采取了主动。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do sb/yourself an ˈinjury (often humorous)</b></td><td>弄伤某人（或自己）</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Be careful with that ladder or you'll do yourself an injury.<br>小心那梯子，不然你要弄伤自己了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>much ˌink has been ˈspilled (on/over sth)</b></td><td>关于某事已有大量论述</td><td>★<br>★</td><td>Much ink has been spilled on the life of Shakespeare.<br>介绍莎士比亚生平的作品已有很多。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˌinner ˈman/ˈwoman</b></td><td>内心；心灵；食欲</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>Prayer and meditation are good for the inner man.<br>祷告和冥想可以滋泰心灵。 2 (</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>inside ˈout</b></td><td>里面朝外；彻底地</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You've got your sweater on inside out.<br>你把毛衣里外穿反了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the inˈside</b></td><td>在内部；掌握内情</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Someone on the inside must have passed on the informattion to the bank robbers.<br>肯定有内应把银行的情况告诉了抢劫犯。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>for ˈinstance</b></td><td>例如；比如</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>My books have sold well. My most recent one, for instance, sold 100 000 copies.<br>我的书卖得还不错。比如，最近出版的一本就卖了10万册。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>pay sth back/return sth with ˈinterest</b></td><td>加倍回报（或报复）</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Peter pushed his sister, so she paid him back with interest by kicking him hard.<br>彼得推了妹妹一下，妹妹连本带利，反过来狠狠踢了他一脚。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>run interˈference (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>为某人挡事；替某人开道</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You've been running interference for your crazy brother too long.<br>你帮你的疯弟弟排忧解难已经有太长时间了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the ˈinterim</b></td><td>在此期间</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Despite everything that happened in the interim, they remained good friends.<br>尽管在此期间发生了许多事，他们仍然是好朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at (...) ˈintervals</b></td><td>每隔…时间；不时</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Buses to the city leave at regular intervals.<br>开往城里的公共汽车每隔一定时间发出一班。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>be ˈinto sth (informal)</b></td><td>热衷于；对…很感兴趣</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>My sister is really into rock climbing these days.<br>我妹妹最近特别迷攀岩。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>necessity is the mother of inˈvention (saying)</b></td><td>需要乃发明之母</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He built a stove out of tin cans — necessity is the mother of invention.<br>他用铁罐子做了个炉子，需要真是发明之母。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>at ˈissue</b></td><td>争论中的；关键所在的</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>What's at issue here is whether he was honest, not whether he was clever.<br>这里的关键是他是否诚实，而不是他聪不聪明。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make an ˈissue of/out of sth</b></td><td>小题大做；揪住不放</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Who broke it doesn't matter; let's not make an issue out of it.<br>谁弄坏的不重要，咱们别揪着这事不放。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take ˈissue with sb (about/on/over sth)</b></td><td>与某人争辩；表示异议</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>I must take issue with you over your description of that evening.<br>你对那天晚上的描述，我不得不提出异议。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be an ˈitem (informal)</b></td><td>是一对（恋人）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Are those two an item, or just close friends?<br>他俩是在谈恋爱，还是只是好朋友？（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be ˌpatience, ˌhonesty, simˌplicity, etc. itˈself</b></td><td>极有耐心（诚实、朴素等）</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The nurse was patience itself with the frightened little boy.<br>那位护士对受惊的小男孩极有耐心。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>an ˌivory ˈtower (disapproving)</b></td><td>象牙塔；脱离现实之地</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Just because I'm a writer, it doesn't mean I live in an ivory tower. 1 have to earn a living like anyone else.<br>我是个作家，但这并不意味着我生活在象牙塔里。我要像其他人一样谋生，养活自己。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>a ˌJack the ˈLad (BrE, slang)</b></td><td>浪荡小子；吊儿郎当的年轻人</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He used to be a bit of a Jack the Lad - I never thought he'd settle down and get married.<br>他过去整天和一帮哥儿们胡闹，真没想到他能安定下来，还结了婚。 ②</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a jack of ˈall trades</b></td><td>万金油；样样通样样松</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He repairs cars, he paints houses, he makes furniture. He's a real jack of all trades.<br>他又修车又粉刷房子，还会做家具，什么都会干一点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be in a ˈjam (informal)</b></td><td>陷入困境</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I'm in a bit of a jam. Could you give me a lift to the train station?<br>我遇上一点小麻烦，能让我搭你的车去火车站吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jam on the ˈbrake(s) ◆ jam the ˈbrake(s) on</b></td><td>猛踩刹车</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The car skidded as he jammed on the brakes.<br>他紧急剎车时汽车打滑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>jam toˈmorrow (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>许而不予的好处；画饼充饥</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>They refused to settle for a promise of jam tomorrow.<br>他们不满足于那些美妙的空口许诺。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>your ˈjaw drops</b></td><td>惊得目瞪口呆</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Her jaw dropped when she saw the price on the tag.<br>她看到吊牌上的价格，惊得下巴都快掉了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈjaw-dropping</b></td><td>令人瞠目结舌的</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Taking the desert road at night was a jaw-dropping experience.<br>夜里走那条沙漠公路是一次让人瞠目的经历。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the jaws of ˈdeath, deˈfeat, etc. (literary)</b></td><td>鬼门关；失败的边缘</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The team snatched victory from the jaws of defeat.<br>这个队在紧急关头反败为胜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>and all that ˈjazz (spoken, informal)</b></td><td>诸如此类；等等</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>We had to fill in forms, show passports and all that jazz.<br>我们得填表、出示护照，诸如此类。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌJekyll and ˈHyde</b></td><td>双重人格的人</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>He's a real Jekyll and Hyde.At home he shouts at his wife and children all the time; at work he's always charming and friendly.<br>他才是个有双重性格的人呢!在家里老冲着妻子儿女大吼大叫；上班时却总是魅力十足，和善友好。 ③</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/feel like ˈjelly (also turn to ˈjelly)</b></td><td>（腿）发软；紧张得站不稳</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She couldn't move — her head was swimming, her mouth was dry and her legs felt like jelly.<br>她动弹不得:头晕晕的，嘴干干的，腿软得像棉花。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in ˈjest</b></td><td>开玩笑地</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The remark was made half in jest.<br>这话是半开玩笑说的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˈjet set</b></td><td>常乘飞机四处玩乐的富豪一族</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She's really joined the jet set now, skiing in St. Moritz, winter holidays in Barbados, in Paris..<br>她现在真的成了喷气一族</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the jewel in the ˈcrown</b></td><td>王冠上的明珠；最珍贵的部分</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The research facility is considered the jewel in the crown of the nation's technology industry.<br>这个研究设施被视为国家技术产业最宝贵的财富。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get/have the ˈjitters (informal)</b></td><td>紧张不安；焦躁</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I always get the jitters the night before a big interview.<br>重要面试前一晚，我总是紧张得不行。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌJob's ˈcomforter (old-fashioned)</b></td><td>越安慰越添愁的人</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>Ann came to see me when I was in hospital. She was a real Job's comforter! She told me about somebody who had the same operation as me, and then died a month later.<br>我住院时安来看我，谁知她的安慰使我更难受!她告诉我，有个人做了和我同样的手术，结果一个月后就死了。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do a good, bad, etc. ˈjob (on sth) ◆ make a good, bad, etc. ˈjob of sth</b></td><td>（把某事）做得好（或差等）</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The painters did a lovely job on the front of the house.<br>油漆工把房子正面刷得非常漂亮。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do the ˈjob/ˈtrick (informal)</b></td><td>管用；奏效</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>A bit of tape should do the trick until you buy a new one.<br>你买新的之前，贴点胶带应该就管用了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give sb/sth up as a bad ˈjob (informal)</b></td><td>对…不再抱希望；放弃</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>After three hours we gave the old printer up as a bad job.<br>折腾了三小时，我们放弃了那台旧打印机。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>good ˈjob! (AmE, spoken)</b></td><td>干得好</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Good job! You finished the whole wall by yourself.<br>干得漂亮！你一个人把整面墙弄完了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(it's) a good job/thing (that)... (spoken)</b></td><td>幸好；好在</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>It's a good job he was here. We couldn't have moved the piano without him.<br>幸好他在，没有他，我们可搬不动这架钢琴。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>a job of ˈwork (BrE, old-fashioned or formal)</b></td><td>一件正经活儿；分内的工作</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>Clearing that garden was a real job of work for two people.<br>清理那个花园，对两个人来说真是不小的活儿。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>more than your ˈjob's worth (to do sth) (BrE, spoken)</b></td><td>违反规定会丢饭碗</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>It's more than my job's worth to let you in without a pass.<br>没有通行证放你进去，我这饭碗可保不住。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>you're ˈjoking ◆ you must be ˈjoking (spoken)</b></td><td>你开玩笑吧；别逗了</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>The boss wants us to work Sunday too? You must be joking.<br>老板要我们周日也上班？别逗了。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>keep up with the ˈJoneses (informal, disapproving)</b></td><td>与邻里攀比；比阔气</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>First the Smiths got a swimming pool, and now their neighbours, the Sinclairs, are building one. It's silly the way people always have to keep up with the Joneses.<br>一开始，史密斯家盖了个游泳池，如今他们的邻居辛克莱家也要盖一个。这样比来比去真是无聊。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>a kick up the ˈbackside (also a kick in the ˈpants) (informal)</b></td><td>鞭策；当头棒喝</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>What he needs is a good kick up the backside. Then he'd do some work.<br>需要训他一通，他才会干活。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>kick sb when they're ˈdown</b></td><td>落井下石；乘人之危</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>George generally believed that you should never kick a man when he's down, but thought that this time he might make an exception.<br>乔治一向认为不该落井下石，不过这次他觉得可以破例。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈkick yourself (informal)</b></td><td>懊悔不已；自责</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Buy it. It's a real bargain. You'll kick yourself if you don'.<br>买吧，这可真便宜，不买一定会后悔的。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>know sb/sth ˈbackwards (informal, especially BrE)</b></td><td>对…了如指掌；背得滚瓜烂熟</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She's played that part so often she knows the script backwards.<br>这个角色她演过太多次，剧本早已倒背如流。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know ˈbest</b></td><td>最懂得该怎么做；比谁都明白</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Fine, do it your way—you always know best, apparently.<br>行，照你的来，反正你总是最懂。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know ˈbetter (than that/than to do sth)</b></td><td>明白事理；不至于糊涂到…</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>You left the car unlocked? I thought you'd know better.<br>你没把车锁上？我还以为你不至于那么糊涂。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know sb by ˈsight</b></td><td>与某人面熟；只认得脸</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I haven't actually met Dr. Galston, but I know him by sight of course.<br>我不曾真正拜会过高尔斯顿博士，不过我认识他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know ˈdifferent/ˈotherwise (informal)</b></td><td>知道并非如此；掌握的情况不同</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She thought he was upset about the divorce, but I knew different.<br>她以为他为离婚的事很沮丧，可我知道不是那么回事。 ˌ</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know sb/sth inside ˈout (informal)</b></td><td>对…极为熟悉；了如指掌</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You've read that book so often that you must know it inside out by now.<br>你经常读这本书，应该对它了如指掌了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know sth like the back of your ˈhand (informal)</b></td><td>对…了如指掌；如数家珍</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>As a taxi driver, you have to know the city like the back of your hand.<br>作为一名出租车司机，你得对这所城市了如指掌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know no ˈbounds</b></td><td>无限；没有止境</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>His generosity knows no bounds.<br>他极为慷慨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know your own ˈmind</b></td><td>有主见；知道自己要什么</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>At 25 youre old enough to know your own mind and make these decisions for yourself.<br>你已经25 岁了，该有主见了，自己作这些决定吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know your ˈplace</b></td><td>有自知之明；守本分</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>My grandfather believed that life was simpler when he was young, when everybody knew their place.<br>我的祖父觉得他年轻时生活要简单得多，那时人们都安分守己。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know the ˈscore (informal)</b></td><td>了解实情；知道真相</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Look, you know the score, we can't afford a car right now.<br>听着，你知道实情，我们目前没钱买车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know your ˈstuff (informal)</b></td><td>精通业务；很内行</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I was very impressed by your lawyer. He really knows his stuff.<br>我很欣赏你的律师，他对法律十分精通。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know a thing or two (about sb/sth) (informal)</b></td><td>对…很在行；见多识广</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ask Grandad about roses—he knows a thing or two about growing them.<br>养玫瑰的事问爷爷，他挺有一套。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know your way aˈbout/aˈround (sth)</b></td><td>熟门熟路；熟悉情况</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I'd used the library before, so I knew my way around and found the book quite quickly.<br>我以前来过这个图书馆，所以比较熟悉，很快就找到了我要的书。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know what it is to be/do sth</b></td><td>亲身经历过；深知其中滋味</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I know what it is to be a mother, so believe me when Isay it is very hard work.<br>我是过来人，相信我，当母亲很辛苦。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know what you're ˈdoing/aˈbout (informal)</b></td><td>有经验；老练在行</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Relax, let him carry the ladder—he knows what he's doing.<br>放心让他扛梯子，他有经验。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know what you're ˈtalking about (informal)</b></td><td>熟知此事；作经验之谈</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Listen to her on childcare—she's raised four kids and knows what she's talking about.<br>育儿的事听她的，她带大四个孩子，都是经验之谈。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know what's ˈgood for you</b></td><td>知道好歹；懂得趋利避害</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>If you know what's good for you, young man, you'll talk to nobody about what you've seen here tonight.<br>年轻人，如果你知道好歹的话，就别对任何人说起你今晚看到的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know what's ˈwhat (informal)</b></td><td>是内行；有鉴别能力</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ask Ann. She knows what's what. She's been here for years.<br>去问安吧，她在这里很多年了，是个内行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know where you ˈare/ˈstand</b></td><td>知道自己的处境（或地位）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I don't know where I stand with him. I don't know what he feels about me.<br>我不知道我在他心里的位置，也不知道他对我有什么看法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know where you're ˈgoing</b></td><td>目标明确；有清楚的追求</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He knows exactly where he's going. He wants to be an actor.<br>他很清楚自己的人生目标，他想成为一名潢员。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>know which side your ˈbread is buttered</b></td><td>知道利益所在；善于为自己打算</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>I'm sure Ray will make a special effort to please the new supervisor - after all, he knows which side his bread is buttered!<br>我相信雷会刻意讨好新来的主管，毕竟他知道自己的利益之所在!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>let sb ˈknow</b></td><td>告诉某人；通知某人</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I dontt know ifi can come, but rll let you know soon.<br>我不知道能不能来，但我会尽早通知你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know any ˈbetter</b></td><td>（因缺乏教养而）举止无礼</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>You can't blame him for his bad table manners; he doesn't know any better.<br>别责铎他不懂餐桌礼仪，没有人教过他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know you're ˈborn (BrE, spoken)</b></td><td>身在福中不知福</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Young people today don't know they're born. Life was much harder when I was a child.<br>现在的年轻人身在福中不知福，我小时候生活苦得多。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know your ˌarse from your ˈelbow (BrE) (AmE not know your ˌass from your ˈelbow) (△, slang)</b></td><td>蠢笨至极；什么都不懂</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Don't let him wire the lamp—he doesn't know his arse from his elbow.<br>别让他接灯线，他啥也不懂。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know ˈbeans about sth (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>对…一窍不通；完全不懂行</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>I really don't know beans about economics.<br>我对经济学真的一窍不通。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know the first thing aˈbout sb/sth</b></td><td>对…一无所知</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Idon't know the first thing about Chinese history.<br>我对中国历史一窍不通。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know sb from ˈAdam (informal)</b></td><td>根本不认识某人</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>This man came into the office and he said that he knew me. I didn't know him from Adam, which was a bit embarrassing.<br>这个人到办公室来，说他认识我，可我一点都不认识他，真是有点尴尬。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know the ˈmeaning of the word (disapproving)</b></td><td>根本不懂；毫无这种概念</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Love?He doesn't know the meaning of the word.<br>爱情？他才不懂什么叫爱情呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know what ˈhit you (informal)</b></td><td>惊呆了；不知所措</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You should have seen his reaction! He didn't know what had hit him!<br>你真该看看他的反应，他简直惊呆了!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know what you're ˈmissing</b></td><td>不知道错过了多好的事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You've never tried snorkelling? You don't know what you're missing.<br>你没浮潜过？你真是错过太多了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know what to ˈdo with yourself</b></td><td>不知如何打发时间</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>With the kids away for a week, she didn't know what to do with herself.<br>孩子走了一周，她都不知道怎么打发时间。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know whether you're ˈcoming or ˈgoing</b></td><td>忙得晕头转向；理不清头绪</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Tve got so much work to do that I don't know whether I'm coming or going.<br>我有太多的工作要做，都不知该做什么好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know whether to ˈlaugh or ˈcry</b></td><td>哭笑不得</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Can you believe she said that to me? I didn't know whether to laugh or cry!<br>你相信她对我说那样的话吗？我真是哭笑不得!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know which way/where to ˈlook</b></td><td>尴尬得不知所措；狼狈不堪</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>When a half-naked woman walked into the room, nobody knew where to look.<br>一位半裸的女子走进房间，所有人都尴尬得不知如何是好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not know which way/where to ˈturn</b></td><td>（困境中）不知如何是好</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She didn't know where to turn for help when her daughter started taking drugs.<br>当女儿开始吸毒时，她不知去哪里寻求帮助。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(well) what do you ˈknow (about ˈthat)? (informal) what do you ˈknow</b></td><td>（表示惊讶）真没想到</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>She passed the test first time—well, what do you know about that!<br>她一次就考过了，真没想到！（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>you ˈknow (informal) (1 used when you are thinking of what to say)</b></td><td>（考虑接着说什么时）嗯，那个</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Hes, you next know, strange. It's hard to explain.<br>他，嗯，很奇怪，这很难解释。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>you know as well as ˈI do</b></td><td>（说服他人时）你我都清楚</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You know as well as I do that if she finds out, she'll stop us going.<br>我们都很清楚，如果她发现了就会阻止我们去的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>you know ˈwho/ˈwhat (spoken)</b></td><td>（不点名）你知道是谁（或什么）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Isaw you know who this morning. She didn't even say hello to me.<br>我今天早上看见那谁了，她甚至没有跟我打招呼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>you never ˈknow (with sb/sth)</b></td><td>很难说；很难预料</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Don't throw away those old stamps. You never know, they might be valuable one day.<br>别把那些旧邮票丢掉，说不定哪天它们就值钱了。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>there's no ˈknowing/ˈsaying/ˈtelling...</b></td><td>难以预料；无从知道</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>There is no telling what he may do when he gets angry.<br>难以预料他愤怒时会做出什么事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be common/public ˈknowledge</b></td><td>尽人皆知；是公开的事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>What do you mean you're surprised he's leaving?I thought it was common knowledge that he was looking for another job!<br>你说对他的离开很惊讶是什么意思？ 我以为他要另谋高就的事已经尽人皆知了!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>come to sb's ˈknowledge (formal)</b></td><td>为某人所知；被某人获悉</td><td>★★<br>★</td><td>It has come to our knowledge that you have been taking time off without permission.<br>我们得知你未经允许就擅自休假。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to your ˈknowledge</b></td><td>据某人所知</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>To my knowledge, nobody has ever complained about the noise before.<br>据我所知，从没人抱怨过噪音。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>let it be ˈknown/make it ˈknown that...</b></td><td>（设法让人）得知某事</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The President has let it be known that he does not intend to run for election again.<br>总统已向大家透露他无意参加下届竞选。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make yourself ˈknown to sb</b></td><td>向某人作自我介绍</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>I made myself known to the hotel manager.<br>我向宾馆经理作了自我介绍。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>God/goodness/Heaven knows (spoken)</b></td><td>天知道；谁知道呢</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>God knows why he painted the kitchen bright orange.<br>天知道他为什么把厨房刷成亮橙色。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give sb, get, etc. a rap over the knuckles</b></td><td>斥责某人；受到申斥</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The reporter got a rap over the knuckles for printing the family's address.<br>那记者因登出这家人的地址挨了训。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌlabour of ˈlove</b></td><td>乐在其中的苦差；心甘情愿做的事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>This tablecloth is a real labour of love. It took her years to make it.<br>这块桌布是激情之作，耗费了她数年时间才完成。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>labour the ˈpoint</b></td><td>反复解释；一再重复已明白的事</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Ithink you've said enough - there's no need to labour the point.<br>我认为你已经说得够多了，没有必要一再重复。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈladies' ˈman</b></td><td>讨女人喜欢的男子；爱与女人厮混的男子</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Jim had always been a bit of a ladies' man, and he didn't marry until he was 45.<br>吉姆一直喜欢在脂粉堆里混，直到45 岁才结婚。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈlager lout (BrE)</b></td><td>酗酒闹事的年轻男子</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>The police are planning to crack down on lager louts this summer.<br>今年夏天，警方将采取严厉措施对付那些酗酒滋事的年轻人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the ˈlam (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>在逃；逃匿</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The man disappeared just before he was due to g0 to jail and has been on the lam ever since.<br>那名男子正要被收监时突然失踪，从那时起一直在逃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be mutton dressed (up) as lamb</b></td><td>老来俏；装嫩</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She thinks that miniskirt suits her, but it's mutton dressed up as lamb.<br>她觉得那条超短裙很衬她，其实是老来俏。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌlame ˈduck (informal)</b></td><td>跛脚鸭；处境艰难的人（或机构）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>My uncle is a bit of a lame duck. The family has to help him all the tume.<br>我叔叔生活处境艰难，总是要靠家里人帮助。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the land of the ˈliving (humorous)</b></td><td>活着；在世</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Nice to see you. I'm glad to see that you're still in the land of the living.<br>很高兴见到你，看到你还活着真开心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the ˌland of ˈNod (old-fashioned, humorous)</b></td><td>在梦乡；睡着了</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>Pete and Joe were still in the land of Nod, so I went out for a walk in the morning sunshine.<br>皮特和乔仍在梦乡之中，于是我踏着晨光外出散步。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>land a ˈblow, ˈpunch, etc.</b></td><td>击中；打中对方</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She landed a Punch on his chin.<br>她一拳打在他下巴上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a/the land of ˌmilk and ˈhoney</b></td><td>富饶的乐土；丰裕之地</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Their grandparents crossed the ocean expecting a land of milk and honey.<br>他们的祖辈漂洋过海，指望找到一片乐土。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>see, etc. how the ˈland lies (BrE)</b></td><td>摸清形势；弄清情况</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Let's wait and see how the land lies before we do anything.<br>咱们等弄清情况以后再行动吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>mind/watch your ˈlanguage</b></td><td>注意言辞；说话文明点</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Watch your language, young man!<br>年轻人，说话注意点!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>speak/talk the same/a different ˈlanguage</b></td><td>谈得来（或谈不来）；有无共同语言</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Unions and managers are at last beginning to speak the same language.<br>工会和管理层终于开始沟通了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>drop/dump sth in sb's ˈlap (informal)</b></td><td>把某事推给某人负责</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>They dropped the problem firmly back in my lap.<br>他们把问题断然给我推了回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>drop/fall into sb's ˈlap (informal)</b></td><td>轻易到手；从天上掉下来</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>A job's not going to just fall in your lap, you know. You'll have to g0 out and find one!<br>工作不会从天上掉下来，你得自己出去找!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the lap of the ˈgods</b></td><td>听天由命；非人力所能左右</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Idon't know what's going to happen - it's in the lap of the gods now. All we can do is wait.<br>我不知道会发生什么事情，现在一切都得听天由命，我们只能等待。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the lap of ˈluxury</b></td><td>生活优裕；养尊处优</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He grew up in the lap of luxury and has never washed a dish.<br>他从小锦衣玉食，连碗都没洗过。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the last lap</b></td><td>最后阶段；最后一圈</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>We're on the last lap of the project, so hang on for another week.<br>项目进入最后阶段了，再撑一周。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at ˈlarge</b></td><td>（用于名词后）整体而言；一般大众</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The public at large does not know enough about this problem.<br>公众普遍对这个问题还不够了解。 2 (</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>lay sth ˈwaste • lay ˈwaste to sth (formal)</b></td><td>摧毁；使荒芜</td><td>★★<br>★</td><td>The fire laid waste to thousands of hectares of forest in two days.<br>大火两天内烧毁了数千公顷森林。（自拟）</td></tr>
