<tr><td><b>have your ˈsay (informal)</b></td><td>发表意见；表达看法</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You've had your say, now let me have mine.<br>你已经发表</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have something, nothing, etc. to ˈsay for yourself</b></td><td>能（或不能）为自己的行为辩解</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>You're three hours late — have you nothing to say for yourself?<br>你迟到了三个小时，就没什么话要说吗？（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I ˈmust say (spoken)</b></td><td>我得说（用于强调看法）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Well, I must say, that's the funniest thing I've heard all week.<br>嘿，听我说，这是我整整一周听到的最滑稽的一件事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I ˌwouldn't say ˈno (to sth) (spoken)</b></td><td>我不反对；乐意来一份</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I wouldn't say no to a pizza.<br>来块比萨饼我倒不反对。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>never say ˈdie (saying)</b></td><td>别气馁；决不放弃</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Never say die, buddy. Tve been in worse situations than this.<br>老兄，别气馁。我以前还碰到过更糟糕的情况。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈnot to say</b></td><td>即便不说…；虽不能说…</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>He is very difficult, not to say impossible, to understand.<br>他这人，即便不说不可捉摸，也可说是难以理解。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>say ˈcheese!</b></td><td>笑一笑（拍照时用语）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Is everybody ready? Right, say cheese!<br>都准备好了吗？好，笑一笑!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>say no ˈmore (spoken)</b></td><td>不用再说了；我明白了</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You want to leave early because of the match? Say no more, mate.<br>你要为看球早走？不用说了，明白。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>say your ˈpiece (informal)</b></td><td>说出心里话；表明看法</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I went to see the boss this morning and I said my piece about our working conditions.He wasn't very happy about it.<br>今天早晨我去见了老板，跟他一五一十地说了我们的工作条件。他为此不太高兴。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>say ˈwhat? (AmE, spoken)</b></td><td>你说什么（表示惊讶）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Say what? You drove all the way to Chicago without a map?<br>你说什么？你没带地图就一路开到芝加哥？（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>say ˈwhen</b></td><td>够了请说一声（倒饮料时用）</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I'm pouring the wine now, so say when and I'll stop.<br>我在倒酒了，够了你就说一声。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(just) say the ˈword</b></td><td>只要说一声；一声令下</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Jf you need any help, just say the word.<br>要帮忙的话，就开口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>that is to ˈsay</b></td><td>也就是说；换句话说</td><td>★★★★<br>★★</td><td>Well meet again three days from now, that is to Friday.<br>我们三天后，也就是星期五再见。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to ˌsay the (very) ˈleast</b></td><td>至少可以说；说得客气些</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The hotel was disappointing, to say the least, and the staff were rude.<br>那家酒店说得客气些也让人失望，服务员还没礼貌。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to say ˈnothing of sth</b></td><td>更不用说；何况</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>She is an expert in Chinese, to say nothing of speaking several European languages.<br>她精通汉语，更不用说还会讲几种欧洲语言。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌwhat would/do you ˈsay (to sth/doing sth)?</b></td><td>你觉得…怎么样；你愿意吗</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>What would you say to a weekend in Paris?<br>去巴黎度周末，你说好不好？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>whatever you ˈsay (spoken)</b></td><td>随你；由你（不想争论）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Whatever you say — I'm too tired to argue about paint colours tonight.<br>随你吧，今晚我累得懒得为墙漆颜色争。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>who can ˈsay (...)? (spoken)</b></td><td>谁知道呢；说不准</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Who can say what wil happen next year?<br>谁知道明年会发生什么事？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>who's to ˈsay (...)? (spoken)</b></td><td>谁说得准呢</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Who's to say she wouldn't have won if she'd trained a bit harder?<br>谁说得准呢，她要是再多练点也许就赢了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>he, she, etc. wouldn't say ˌboo to a ˈgoose</b></td><td>极为羞怯；胆小怕事</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>My brother wouldn't say boo to a goose, yet he became a lawyer.<br>我弟弟胆小得不敢跟人红脸，却当上了律师。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>you can say ˈthat again! (spoken)</b></td><td>说得太对了；我完全同意</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>'This queue is ridiculous.' 'You can say that again — we've waited an hour.'<br>“这队排得离谱。”“可不是嘛，都等一小时了。”（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>you can't say ˈfairer (than ˈthat) (BrE, spoken)</b></td><td>再公道不过了</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Look,rl give you £100 for it. You can't say fairer than that.<br>喂，我出 100英镑买它，这再公道不过了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>you don't ˈsay! (spoken, often ironic)</b></td><td>不会吧；真的吗（亦表毫不意外）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You don't say! I'd never have guessed he was afraid of heights.<br>真的吗？我可看不出他还恐高。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it ˌgoes without ˈsaying (that...)</b></td><td>不言而喻；不用说</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>It goes without saying that we'll cover your travel costs for the interview.<br>不用说，面试的路费我们会给你报销。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>that ˌgoes without ˈsaying</b></td><td>那是当然的；不言而喻</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>'Will you keep this confidential?' 'That goes without saying, obviously.'<br>“这事你会保密吧？”“那还用说。”（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's/that's not ˈsaying much, etc.</b></td><td>这说明不了什么；没什么了不起</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She's a better player than me, but that's not saying much (= because I'm a very bad player).<br>她比我水平高，但也没什么了不起。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(it) does (eˈxactly) what it says on the ˈtin</b></td><td>名副其实；与宣传的一样</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I paid £150 for this camera and am more than happy with it. It does exactly what it says on the tin!<br>我花了，150 英镑买了这架照相机，真是喜欢得不得了。它和广告上所说的一模一样!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it, etc. says a ˈlot, ˈmuch, etc. about/for sb/sth</b></td><td>很能说明…的品质（或特点）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>It says much about the high quality of these instruments that many of them are still in use today.<br>这些仪器有许多现在仍然在使用，这说明它们的质量有多高。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>who ˈsays (...)? (spoken)</b></td><td>谁说的（表示不同意）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Who says I can't do it?<br>谁说我干不了这个？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on sb's ˈsay-so</b></td><td>仅凭某人一句话；经某人许可</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>He hired and fired people on his partner's say-s0.<br>他雇谁辞谁全凭他的合伙人随便一说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˌscales fall from sb's ˈeyes (literary)</b></td><td>恍然大悟；看清真相</td><td>★<br>★</td><td>It wasn't until much later that the scales fell from his eyes and he realized that she'd been lying to him.<br>过了很久他才恍然大悟，意识到她一直在对他撒谎。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌmake yourself ˈscarce (informal)</b></td><td>躲开；回避；不露面</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I could see they wanted to be alone, so I made myself scarce.<br>我看</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scare the ˈshit out of sb • scare sb ˈshitless (△, slang)</b></td><td>把某人吓得屁滚尿流</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You scared the shit out of me, creeping around in the dark like that!<br>你这样在暗处悄无声息地走动，把我吓得够呛!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>arrive/come on the ˈscene</b></td><td>到达现场；出现；露面</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>John and I were really happy together until she came on the scene.<br>她没搅和进来之前我和约翰在一起真的很开心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>create/make a ˈscene</b></td><td>大吵大闹（尤在公共场合）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Please don't create a scene in public.<br>公共场所， 请勿喧哗。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(not) sb's ˈscene (informal)</b></td><td>（不）合某人口味；（非）某人所好</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The resort wasn't really our scene. Most of the people were much older than us and there wasn't any nightlife.<br>人都比我们年龄大得多，而且也没有任何夜生活。01</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>set the ˈscene/ˈstage (for sth)</b></td><td>为…作铺垫；交代背景</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The first few chapters of the book just set the scene.<br>这本书的开头几章只是背景介绍。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>behind the ˈscenes</b></td><td>幕后；暗中；秘密地</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The general public knows very little about what happens behind the scenes in politics.<br>公众对政治内幕了解甚少。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be on the ˈscent (of sb/sth)</b></td><td>追踪…的踪迹；获得线索</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The police are on the scent of the criminals.<br>警方已掌握追踪罪犯的线索。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put/throw sb off the ˈscent</b></td><td>使某人失去线索；引某人走偏</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Ithrew the police off the scent by pretending I was in Mexico City on the day of the crime.<br>我佯装犯罪当日自己在墨西哥城，从而使警方失去了线索。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the/sb's ˈscheme of things</b></td><td>事物的格局；总体安排</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Low-paid workers like us don't have a very important place in the scheme of things.<br>像我们这样低收入的工人一般来说无足轻重。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a school of ˈthought</b></td><td>学派；某种观点</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>There are two schools of thought on this matter.<br>在这一问题上有两派不同的看法。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep ˈschtum/ˈshtum (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>保持沉默；什么也不说</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I think wed better keep schtum about this money, don't you?<br>我认为在这笔钱上我们最好保持沉默，你说是不是？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have/get sth down to a ˈscience (especially AmE, often humorous)</b></td><td>把某事做得又准又高效</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>When Tom says he has shopping down to a science, he isn't kidding.<br>汤姆说他对购物很有一套，他可不是说着玩的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on ˈthat/ˈthis score</b></td><td>就那（这）一点而言</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The accommodation is excellent so I don't think we need to worry on that score.<br>住宿条件好极了，因此我觉得我们不必为之操心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>score a ˈpoint/ˈpoints (off/over/against sb)</b></td><td>驳倒某人；令某人出丑</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Why don't you try to solve the problem instead of scoring points over each other?<br>你们为什么不尽力去解决问题而是互相拆台呢？0</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>heap/pour ˈscorn on sb/sth</b></td><td>嘲笑；对…嗤之以鼻</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>She poured scorn on his plans to get rich quickly.<br>她对他迅速致富的计划不屑一顾。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get off/go ˌscot-ˈfree (informal)</b></td><td>逃脱惩罚；逍遥法外</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>It seemed so unfair that she was punished while the others got off scot-free!<br>她受到了惩罚而其他人却什么事也没有，这似乎太不公平了! ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the ˈscrap heap (informal)</b></td><td>被抛弃；遭淘汰</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>With the closure of the factory, thousands of workers have been thrown on the scrap heap.<br>工厂倒闭了，几千名工人被遗弃。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scrape (up) an acˈquaintance with sb (informal)</b></td><td>设法结识某人</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>He scraped an acquaintance with the manager hoping it would land him work.<br>他想方设法结识了经理，指望能弄到活干。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scrape (the bottom of) the ˈbarrel (disapproving)</b></td><td>勉强凑合；降格以求</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>TV is terrible at the moment, it's nothing but old movies. They're really scraping the barrel, aren't they?<br>这一阵子电视节目很糟糕，除了老片子再没什么了。他们真是在应付，是不是？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do sth from ˈscratch</b></td><td>从零开始；白手起家</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We lost the file and had to write the report from scratch.<br>文件丢了，报告只能从头再写。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scratch ˌA and you'll find ˈB</b></td><td>剥开表象，某类人骨子里是…</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Scratch a cynic and you'll find a disappointed idealist underneath.<br>剥开愤世嫉俗的外壳，里头是个失望的理想主义者。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scratch your ˈhead (over sth)</b></td><td>苦思冥想；大惑不解</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We're all scratching our heads for a solution to this problem.<br>为了找到这个问题的答案我们都绞尽脑汁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scratch the ˈsurface (of sth)</b></td><td>浅尝辄止；只触及皮毛</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>This report only scratches the surface of the problem.<br>这篇报告对这一问题仅作了肤浅的探讨。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>up to ˈscratch</b></td><td>达到标准；合格</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The level of safety in our power stations must be brought up to scratch.<br>一定要提高我们发电站的安全水平，使之达到标准。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈback-scratching noun</b></td><td>互相吹捧；互开方便之门</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>There's far too much back-scratching between the council and local builders.<br>市政厅和本地建筑商之间的互相关照实在太多了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>scream blue ˈmurder (BrE) (AmE scream bloody ˈmurder) (informal)</b></td><td>大声抗议；不停叫嚷</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Jill will scream blue murder if Ann gets promoted and she doesn't.<br>假如提升安不提升吉尔，吉尔会大声抗议的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a ˈscrew loose</b></td><td>有点疯癫；脑子不正常</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Anyone who swims in that river in January has a screw loose.<br>一月份还下那条河游泳的人，脑子准是有点毛病。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>screw ˈhim, ˈyou, ˈthat, etc. (△, slang)</b></td><td>去他（你）的；见鬼去吧</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Screw him — if he can't apologise, I'm not going to his wedding.<br>去他的，他要是不肯道歉，他的婚礼我不去了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌturn of the ˈscrew</b></td><td>雪上加霜；变本加厉的施压</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>In this recession a rise in interest rates is just another turn of the screw for businesses.<br>目前经济萧条， 利率上升对企业来说真是雪上加霜。 ③</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put the ˈscrews on (sb) (informal)</b></td><td>胁迫；威逼；施压</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The electricity company is really putting the screws on. We've got a week to pay before our supply is cut off!<br>电力公司真是逼得太紧了。我们必须在一星期之内交钱，否则就把我们的电给掐了!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/go on the ˈscrounge (for sth) (BrE, informal, disapproving)</b></td><td>讨要（钱财、食物等）；伸手索要</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>She's always on the scrounge for cigarettes. Why doesn't she buy her own?<br>她总向人讨要香烟，为什么自己不买呢？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>by the scruff of sb's/the ˈneck</b></td><td>揪住…的颈背</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The barman took her by the scruff of the neck and threw her out.<br>酒吧男招待一把揪住她的脖子，将她扔了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˌscum of the ˈearth (informal)</b></td><td>人渣；社会渣滓</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Drug dealers are the scum of the earth.<br>毒品販子是社会的渣滓。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>all, completely, etc. at ˈsea</b></td><td>茫然；不知所措</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>I was completely at sea during the maths lecture this morning.<br>今天上午的数学课我完全听懵了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌseal of apˈproval</b></td><td>正式认可；批准</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Our project has the director's seal of approval.<br>我们的计划得到了主管的认可。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>set the ˈseal on sth (formal)</b></td><td>使…圆满收官；为…画上句号</td><td>★★<br>★</td><td>His Nobel prize set the seal on a brilliant career in physics.<br>获得诺贝尔奖成为他辉煌的物理学研究生涯的顶峰。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be bursting/bulging at the ˈseams (with sth) (also be full to ˈbursting (with sth)) (informal)</b></td><td>挤得满满的；人满为患</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The little classroom was bursting at the seams with thirty-five children.<br>三十五个孩子把那间小教室挤得满满当当。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>(on) skid row (informal, especially AmE)</b></td><td>潦倒落魄；住在贫民区</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>After the divorce he drank himself onto skid row within two years.<br>离婚后他酗酒，两年就沦落街头。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the ˈskids (informal)</b></td><td>逐渐衰落；走下坡路</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It was clear months ago that the firm was on the skids.<br>这家公司几个月以前就有明显的衰败迹象。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put the ˈskids under sb/sth (informal)</b></td><td>使失败；使停止</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Unfortunately the government has put the skids under the hospital building programme.<br>不幸的是，政府使这项修建医院的计划无疾而终。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be (all) brothers/sisters under the ˈskin</b></td><td>内心本质相同；同类人</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>Actors and politicians are brothers under the skin. They both need public approval.<br>演员和政治家本质上都是一样的，二者都需要公众的认可。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be (all/just/nothing but) skin and ˈbone(s)</b></td><td>瘦得皮包骨</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>After two years in prison, he was nothing but skin and bone.<br>在监狱里呆了两年，他瘦得只剩一把骨头。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do sth by the ˌskin of your ˈteeth (informal)</b></td><td>勉强做成；险些没成</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We thought we'd miss the plane, but in the end we caught it by the skin of our teeth.<br>我们以为会误了飞机，可是最后刚刚赶上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get under sb's ˈskin (informal)</b></td><td>惹恼某人；让某人念念不忘</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Tve tried to forget her, but 1 know that rve got her under my skin.<br>我努力想要忘掉她，可是我知道我已经被她深深吸引住。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have/put skin in the ˈgame (AmE, especially business)</b></td><td>有切身利害；亲自投入风险</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>If you want someone to make efficient choices, they have to have a little skin in the game.<br>要想有人高效地进行决策，就必须让他们的切身利益与项目成败相挂钩，促使他投身其中。 ②</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's no skin off ˈmy, ˈyour, ˈhis, etc. nose</b></td><td>与某人无关；对某人没损失</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It' no skin off my nose if the price of cigarettes goes up. 1 don't smoke.<br>香烟价格上涨影响不到我，我不吸烟。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make your ˈskin crawl</b></td><td>使人毛骨悚然；让人起鸡皮疙瘩</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>His smile made my skin crawl.<br>他笑得让我直起鸡皮疙瘩。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>skin sb aˈlive</b></td><td>严惩某人；扒了某人的皮</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Your mother would skin you alive if she knew you'd started smoking!<br>要是你母亲知道你开始抽烟，她会扒了你的皮!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(have) a thick/thin ˈskin (informal)</b></td><td>脸皮厚；脸皮薄</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>A traffic warden needs a thick skin to take so much abuse from motorists.<br>交通管理员需要脸皮厚一点才能招架得住开车人的辱骂。 〇</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>thin-ˈskinned adj.</b></td><td>脸皮薄的；敏感易怒的</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He's too thin-skinned to work in politics for very long.<br>他脸皮太薄，在政坛待不长久。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>eyes keep your eyes open/peeled/skinned (for sb/sth)</b></td><td>留心察看；密切注意</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Keep your eyes peeled for a red van parked near the gate.<br>留意一下门口附近停着的红色面包车。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈskip it (spoken, informal)</b></td><td>别提了；不说这个了</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Skip it, I don't want to argue about money again tonight.<br>算了，今晚我不想再为钱吵。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the sky's the ˈlimit (spoken, informal)</b></td><td>前途无量；没有止境</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>For an ambitious young woman in this business, the sky's the limit.<br>对于一个做这一行的雄心勃勃的年轻女士来说，发展前景无可限量。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>cut sb some ˈslack (informal, especially AmE)</b></td><td>对某人网开一面；宽容些</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I know I made a mistake, but it's my first week on the job, so cut me some slack, OK?<br>我知道我犯了错误，可是这是我工作的第一周， 能不能放我一马？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take up the ˈslack</b></td><td>补上空缺；充分利用闲置人力</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The export market has failed to take up the slack in recent years, which has led to financial losses.<br>出口市场近几年没有能够有效地利用资源，导致资金损失。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be a ˈslam dunk (AmE)</b></td><td>是十拿九稳的事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The case looked like a slam dunk for the prosecution.<br>这个案子能够胜诉对于控方来说十拿九稳。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈslanging match (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>互相谩骂；对骂</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>It started as a peaceful discussion, but it ended in a real slanging match.<br>讨论开始时还平心静气的，可是后来却以相互谩骂收场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(a bit of) slap and ˈtickle (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</b></td><td>打情骂俏；亲昵嬉闹</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>We used to do anything to get a bit of slap and tickle when we were young lads.<br>我们还是年轻小伙子的时候，常常想尽各种办法和女友亲热。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a slap on the ˈwrist (informal)</b></td><td>轻微惩罚；小小警告</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Igot a slap on the wrist from my secretary today for leaving the offrice so untidy.<br>今天我的秘书说了我几句，因为我把办公室弄得乱七八糟的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(put sth) on the ˈslate (informal (put sth) on your account in a shop, a bar, etc.)</b></td><td>赊账；记账</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Put the drinks on the slate and I'll settle up on Friday.<br>酒钱先记账，周五我一起结。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(like) a lamb/lambs to the ˈslaughter</b></td><td>像待宰羔羊；不知危险地前往</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>When the war started, thousands of young men went off to fight, like lambs to the slaughter.<br>战争开始后，成千上万的年轻小伙子奔赴战场，就像羔羊被带进了屠宰场。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be a slave to/of sth</b></td><td>是…的奴隶；受…支配</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She's a slave to fashion; she's always buying new clothes.<br>她是个时装奴，总是在买新衣服。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be able to do sth in your ˈsleep (informal)</b></td><td>闭着眼也会做；轻车熟路</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He'd done the journey so many times that he almost felt as if he could do it in his sleep.<br>这条线路他走了好多次了，他觉得自己就是闭着眼睛也能走到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go to ˈsleep (informal)</b></td><td>手脚发麻；肢体麻木</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The business does have problems at present but it's nothing I'm going to lose any sleep over.<br>目前生意确实有问题，但是我不会担心得睡不着觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not sleep a ˈwink ◆ not get a ˈwink of sleep</b></td><td>一夜没合眼</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I didn't sleep a wink last night because I was worrying about my driving test.<br>因为担心驾照考试，我昨晚一夜都没合眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put sb/sth to ˈsleep</b></td><td>使麻醉；给动物实施安乐死</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Before the operation we'll put you to sleep, so don't worry, you won't feel a thing.<br>手术前我们会先给你施行麻醉，所以不要担心，一点都不痛。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sleep like a ˈlog/ˈtop (also sleep like a ˈbaby)</b></td><td>睡得很沉</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>After our long walk yesterday, I slept like a log.<br>由于昨天走了那么长的路，我睡得很死。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈsleep on it</b></td><td>把某事留到第二天再决定</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Don't answer them tonight; sleep on it and call back tomorrow morning.<br>今晚别答复，睡一觉明早再回电话。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sleep ˈtight! (informal, spoken)</b></td><td>睡个好觉</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Good night, Pat, sleep tight!<br>晚安，帕特，睡个好觉!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>let ˌsleeping dogs ˈlie (saying)</b></td><td>别惹麻烦；不要旧事重提</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I was very careful about what I said. It's best to let sleeping dogs lie, 1 think.<br>我非常注意自己的言辞，我认为最好不要惹是生非。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have an ˌace/a ˌtrick up your ˈsleeve (BrE) (AmE have an ˌace in the ˈhole) (informal)</b></td><td>留有一手；有锦囊妙计</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Don't count him out; he always has an ace up his sleeve.<br>别以为他输定了，他总留着一手。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have/keep sth up your ˈsleeve (informal)</b></td><td>暗中留着后手以备不时之需</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>John was smiling to himself all through the meeting; I'm sure he's got something up his sleeve.<br>约翰在会上自始至终都在暗笑，我想他肯定是藏着什么高招。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌsleight of ˈhand</b></td><td>巧妙的手法；障眼法</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The trick is done simply by sleight of hand.<br>变这个戏法全凭手法敏捷。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌslice of ˈlife</b></td><td>现实生活的一个侧面</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>In this book Dickens shows us a slice of nineteenth-century London life.<br>狄更斯在这本书中向我们展示了 19 世纪伦敦生活的一个侧面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>best the best thing since sliced bread</b></td><td>极好的东西；了不起的发明</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He thinks his new coffee machine is the best thing since sliced bread.<br>他觉得他的新咖啡机简直是伟大发明。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not in the ˈslightest</b></td><td>一点也不；毫不</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Flying doesn't worry me in the slightest.<br>我一点也不为坐飞机担心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sling your ˈhook (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>走开；滚蛋</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>That boy's a real nuisance. I tried telling him to sling his hook but he simply ignored me.<br>那男孩真讨厌，我让他走开，可他就是不理会我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the ˌslings and ˈarrows (of sth)</b></td><td>某事带来的种种磨难</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>As a politician you have to deal with the slings and arrows of criticism from the newspapers.<br>作为一名政治家， 你不得不应对报纸上的各种抨击指责。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈthe slings and arrows of outrageous fortune'.</b></td><td>命运无情的摧残（出自《哈姆雷特》）</td><td>★<br>★</td><td>Hamlet asks whether to suffer the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune.<br>哈姆雷特问，是否该忍受命运无情的摧残。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give sb the ˈslip (informal)</b></td><td>甩掉追踪者；摆脱某人</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The police were chasing us but we managed to give them the slip.<br>警方在追踪我们，可是我们设法甩掉了他们。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>let ˈslip sth</b></td><td>说漏嘴；无意中泄露</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She tried not to let slip what she knew.<br>她小心翼翼地保守着她所知道的秘密。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slip sb's ˈmemory/ˈmind</b></td><td>忘记；想不起来</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I was supposed to go to the dentist today, but it completely slipped my mind.<br>我本来打算今天去看牙医，可是却忘记得干干净净。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈslip of a boy, girl, etc. (old-fashioned)</b></td><td>瘦小的男孩或女孩；小不点儿</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>They were amazed that such a slip of a girl could cause so much trouble.<br>他们大吃一惊，这么一个瘦弱的女孩居然能制造出这么多麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a slip of the ˈtongue/ˈpen</b></td><td>口误；笔误</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Did I say North Street? Sorry, that was a slip of the tongue - 1 meant South Street.<br>我 — 我想说南说是北大街吗？对不起，那是口误一大街。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slip on a baˈnana skin (informal)</b></td><td>当众出丑；犯低级错误</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>The new minister slipped on a banana skin before he had been in the job a week.<br>新部长上任不到一星期就出了丑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slip through sb's ˈfingers</b></td><td>从手中溜走；被错过</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I wouldn't let a wonderful opportunity like this slip through your fingers ii were you.<br>如果我是你， 我不会让这么一个大好机会从手里溜走的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slip through the ˈnet</b></td><td>漏网；被疏漏</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We tried to contact all former students, but one or two slipped through the net.<br>我们试图同所有以前的学生取得联系，可还是有一两个未能找到。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>there's ˌmany a ˈslip (ˈtwixt ˌcup and ˈlip)</b></td><td>事情难料；万事难十拿九稳</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>The deal looks certain, but there's many a slip twixt cup and lip.<br>交易看着十拿九稳，可变数总是难免。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>before 7 oˈclock, but there's many a slip ˈtwixt cup</b></td><td>还没到手就别高兴太早</td><td>☆<br>★★</td><td>We should arrive before 7 o'clock, but there's many a slip twixt cup and lip.<br>我们应该七点前能到，不过意外总难免。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(as) slippery as an ˈeel (informal)</b></td><td>滑头；狡猾难缠</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ask him a direct question and he's as slippery as an eel.<br>你直接问他，他就滑得像条泥鳅。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the slippery ˈslope</b></td><td>危险的下坡路；每况愈下的开端</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Starting with shopliftnng, he was soon on the slippery slope towards a life of crime.<br>他一开始只是去商店扒窃，之后很快就走上犯罪的人生之路。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be ˈslipping (informal)</b></td><td>水平下降；不如从前</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You forgot the passwords again? You must be slipping.<br>你又忘了密码？看来你是退步了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be no ˈslouch (at sth/at doing sth) (informal)</b></td><td>很在行；干得很出色</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He's no slouch in the kitchen — you should try his spaghetti bolognese.<br>他在厨房里可是一把好手，你应该尝尝他做的意大利式肉酱面。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do a slow ˈburn (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>慢慢冒火；越想越气</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>It makes me do a slow burn when it takes longer to check out at the grocery store than it took to shop.<br>在小杂货店结账花的时间比购物花的时间都要长，让我渐渐有些生气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go ˈslow (on sth)</b></td><td>放慢速度；怠工</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The government is going slow on tax reforms.<br>政府对税务改革没有什么热情。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the ˈslow lane</b></td><td>落在后面；处于慢车道</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>According to the latest survey, the country is expected to remain in the slow lane of economic recovery.<br>最新的调查显示，该国的经济复苏仍将十分缓慢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>slowly but ˈsurely</b></td><td>缓慢而稳步地</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Attitudes to women at work are changing slowly but surely.<br>对于职业女性的态度正在稳步发生变化。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈslum it (informal, often humorous)</b></td><td>将就过简陋日子</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>What are you doing coming on the bus today? Are you slumming it?<br>你今天坐公共汽车来干吗？难道想体验一下普通人的生活吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do sth on the ˈsly</b></td><td>偷偷做某事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She didn't seem to have much appetite for dinner. I wonder if she's been eating chocolates on the sly?<br>她似乎没有什么胃口吃饭，我不知道她是不是偷偷吃了巧克力？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be grateful/thankful for small ˈmercies</b></td><td>庆幸情况没有更糟</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The thieves took the TV and stereo but didn't take any jewellery, so let's be thankful for small mercies.<br>小偷们抱走了电视机和音响，不过没有拿走任何珠宝，可谓不幸中之万幸。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's a ˌsmall ˈworld (saying)</b></td><td>世界真小</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>It turns out that he's a friend of my brother's! It's a small world, isn't it?<br>原来他是我哥哥的一个朋友!世界真小，不是吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>look/feel ˈsmall (also feel ˈthat high)</b></td><td>感到难堪；觉得自己渺小</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Why did you tell everyone that rd failed all my school exams? I felt so small.<br>你为什么跟谁都说我考试门门不及格？ 我觉得太丢脸了。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>get (yourself) into a ˈstew (about/over sth) (informal)</b></td><td>为某事坐立不安；心烦意乱</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She's in a stew over what she's going to wear to the party tonight.<br>她为自己穿什么衣服出席今晚的聚会而大伤脑筋。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>let sb ˈstew (in their own juice) (informal)</b></td><td>让某人自作自受；听其自食其果</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We told her not to trust him but she wouldn't listen — so let her stew in her own knife - put/stick the knife in/into sb juice!<br>我们告诉她不要相信他的话，可她不听，那就让她自食其果吧!</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>give sb ˈstick (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>批评某人；数落某人</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The crowd gave the players a lot of stick for their terrible performance.<br>观众纷纷指责球员表现得太差劲。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>(out) in the ˈsticks (informal)</b></td><td>在偏远乡下</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ilike living out in the sticks, but it can be a bit boring.<br>我喜欢住在远离城市的多村， 不过会有点单调。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>up ˈsticks (and go, etc.) (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>搬家；迁居</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>Things weren't working out for them here, so they upped sticks and went to Chicago.<br>这边没有什么发展，所以他们迁居到了芝加哥。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>a straw in the ˈwind (BrE)</b></td><td>预示事态走向的迹象</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>Falling ticket sales may be a straw in the wind for the industry.<br>票房下滑也许是这个行业的一个风向信号。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>clutch/grasp at ˈstraws</b></td><td>抓救命稻草；病急乱投医</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The doctors have told him that he has only 6 months to live, but he won't accept it. He's going to a new clinic in Switzerland next week, but he's just clutching at straws.<br>医生告诉他他只能活6个月了，可是他不接受这一诊断。他下周要去瑞士一家新开的诊所，可这只不过是在作绝望的挣扎。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/come on ˈstream</b></td><td>投入运行；开始生产</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The new printing machines come on stream in March.<br>新印刷机 3月份投入使用。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go, swim, etc. with the ˈstream/ˈtide</b></td><td>随大溜；顺应潮流</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Most students just go with the stream and pick the popular courses.<br>多数学生都随大溜，挑热门课上。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go, swim, etc. against the ˈstream/ˈtide</b></td><td>逆潮流而行；不随大溜</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She swims against the tide by refusing to use social media at all.<br>她偏不随大溜，压根儿不用社交媒体。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be (right) up your ˈstreet (especially BrE)</b></td><td>正合你意；对你的胃口</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>This puzzle book is right up your street and you'll finish it tonight.<br>这本谜题书正合你的口味，你今晚就能做完。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be (right) up your ˈalley (AmE usually) (informal)</b></td><td>正对某人胃口；正合适</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>A job mixing travel and photography is right up your alley.<br>又能旅行又能拍照的工作正对你的路子。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be ˈstreets ahead (of sb/sth) (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>遥遥领先；强得多</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Their software is streets ahead of anything else on the market.<br>他们的软件比市面上其他产品领先一大截。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the ˈstreets (informal)</b></td><td>流落街头；无家可归</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He was weak and ill and he knew he wouldn't survive on the streets.<br>他病弱不堪，知道如果流落街头的话就活不下去。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the streets are ˌpaved with ˈgold (saying)</b></td><td>遍地是黄金（喻易发财）</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>More and more people are moving to the big cities, where they believe the streets are paved with gold.<br>越来越多的人搬迁到了大城市，他们以为那里遍地是黄金。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go from ˌstrength to ˈstrength</b></td><td>越来越兴旺；蒸蒸日上</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Since she became the boss, the company's gone from to strength.<br>自从她当了老</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the strength of sth</b></td><td>凭借；基于</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Igot the job on the strength of my experience in sales.<br>我得到这份工作主要是由于我有销售经验。 ◎</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a pillar/tower of ˈstrength</b></td><td>中流砥柱；精神支柱</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>My wife has been a tower of strength during my illness.<br>在我生病期间，妻子就是我的精神支柱。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌstrengthen your ˈhand</b></td><td>增强实力；扩大权力</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The new antidrug laws will strengthen the hand of the police.<br>新的反毒品法将给予警方更多的权力。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>play to your ˈstrengths</b></td><td>发挥自己的长处</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Each member of the team should have a task that plays to their strengths.<br>每一个组员都应该有一项能充分发挥自已优势的任务。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at a ˈstretch</b></td><td>一口气；连续地</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He can code for eight hours at a stretch without a break.<br>他能一口气写八小时代码不休息。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>by ˈno stretch of the imagination •not by ˌany stretch of the imagiˈnation</b></td><td>无论怎么想也不；绝对不是</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>By no stretch of the imagination could you call him clever.<br>他无论如何也称不上聪明。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stretch your ˈlegs</b></td><td>活动腿脚；散散步</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Let's stop at the next services and stretch our legs for ten minutes.<br>下个服务区停一下，活动活动腿脚。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stretch a ˈpoint</b></td><td>破例；通融</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>You are usually only allowed one hour for lunch, but I'm prepared to stretch a point if there's an emergency.<br>通常只给你们一个小时的午饭时间，不过如果有紧急情况我会通融一下的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strictly ˈspeaking</b></td><td>严格说来</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Strictly speaking, this cheese isn't vegetarian, though most people assume so.<br>严格说来这种奶酪并非素食，尽管大家都以为是。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get into your ˈstride (BrE) (AmE hit (your) ˈstride)</b></td><td>进入状态；渐入佳境</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She found the job difficult at first, but now she's got into her stride and she loves it.<br>刚开始她觉得这工作很难，可是现在她已经做顺手了，还爱上了这份工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put sb off their ˈstride/ˈstroke</b></td><td>使某人分心；打乱节奏</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>All sorts of things can put a player off his stroke.<br>有许多事情都会使运动员分心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(match sb) ˌstride for ˈstride</b></td><td>与某人并驾齐驱</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Weve managed to match our closest competitors stride for stride as regards prices.<br>在价格方面，我们已设法尽量不输给几个势均力敌的竞争对手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take sth in your ˈstride (BrE) (AmE take sth in ˈstride)</b></td><td>从容应对；处之泰然</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Joey was upset when we moved house, but Ben seems to have taken it all in his stride.<br>我们搬家的时候乔伊很难过，可是本似乎安之若素。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make great, rapid, etc. ˈstrides (in sth/in doing sth)</b></td><td>取得巨大（或快速）进展</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Ann's made huge strides in her pianoplaying.<br>安在钢琴演奏上进步巨大。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strike a ˈbalance (between A and B)</b></td><td>找到平衡；折中兼顾</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We need to strike a balance between protecting him and letting him become more independent.<br>我们需要在保护他和让他更独立这两者之间找到一个平衡点。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strike a ˈbargain/ˈdeal (with sb)</b></td><td>与某人达成协议</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>They struck a bargain with the landlord to pay less rent in return for painting the house.<br>他们和房东达成协议，他们粉刷房子，作为交换，可以少付些房租。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strike a blow for/against/at sth</b></td><td>维护（或打击）某事物</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The protest was a chance to strike a blow for freedom.<br>这抗议是维护自由的一个机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strike ˌfear, ˌterror, etc. into sb/sb's ˈheart</b></td><td>使某人心生恐惧</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>His crimes struck horror into the nation's heart.<br>他所犯下的罪行令国人惊恐。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strike ˈgold</b></td><td>挖到金矿；意外走运</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The label struck gold with a band nobody else wanted to sign.<br>这家唱片公司签下一支没人要的乐队，结果大赚一笔。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strike it ˈrich (informal)</b></td><td>发大财；暴富</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He struck it rich when a relative died and left him two million.<br>他一个亲戚死后留给他200万，他可发大</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strike (it) ˈlucky (informal)</b></td><td>走运；碰上好运</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We certainly struck it lucky with the weather — it's beautiful today.<br>我们的确走运，赶上了好天气 —— 今天天气真不错。◎</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strike a ˈpose/an ˈattitude</b></td><td>摆姿势；装模作样</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>He WQS striking a pose, leaning against the ship' rail.<br>他摆了个姿势，靠在轮船的栏杆上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>strike while the ˌiron is ˈhot (saying)</b></td><td>趁热打铁</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He seems in a good mood. Why don't you strike while the iron is hot and ask him now?<br>他似乎心情不错。你为什么现在不趁热打铁去问他呢？ ②</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>within ˈstriking distance (of sth)</b></td><td>近在咫尺；触手可及</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>In one minute the aircraft can be within striking distance of the target.<br>一分钟以后目标就会进入飞机的射程之内。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have/keep sb on a ˈstring</b></td><td>牵着某人鼻子走；玩弄</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Of course, he's rich and powerful enough to keep several people on a string.<br>当然， 他有钱有势，有好多人供他驱使。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(with) no ˈstrings attached (also without ˈstrings)</b></td><td>不附带任何条件</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I got a loan of $5 000 with no strings attached.<br>我得到了一笔5000 美元的贷款，无任何附加条件。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at a/one (single) ˈstroke</b></td><td>一举；一下子</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>All my problems were solved at a stroke when an aunt left me some money.<br>我的一位姑妈给我留了些钱，一下子解决了我所有的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not do a ˈstroke (of ˈwork)</b></td><td>一点活儿也不干</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He's useless — he hasnt done a stroke of work today.<br>他毫无用处，他今天一点活都没做。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on/at the ˌstroke of ˈeight, ˈmidnight, etc.</b></td><td>在八点（或午夜等）整</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>She gets to work at the stroke of nine every day.<br>她每天九点准时开始工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put sb off their ˈstroke</b></td><td>打乱某人的节奏</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Constant questions put the surgeon off his stroke during the operation.<br>不停发问打乱了外科医生手术的节奏。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be ˈstrong on sth</b></td><td>擅长某方面</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>This phone is strong on battery life but weak on camera quality.<br>这款手机胜在续航，摄像头就差些。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be your ˈstrong point/suit</b></td><td>是某人的强项</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Writing letters has never been my strong point.<br>我从来就不擅长写信。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>come on ˈstrong (with sb) (informal)</b></td><td>言辞强硬；过于主动</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Do you think I came on too strong at that meeting?<br>你觉得我在那个会议上是不是太咄咄逼人了？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a strong ˈstomach</b></td><td>不怕恶心；受得住</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Youve got to have a strong stomach to watch animals being killed.<br>要看宰杀动物，得忍受力强才行。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be ˈstruck by/on/with sb/sth (informal)</b></td><td>被打动；迷上</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I was struck by her youth and enthusiasm.<br>她的年轻热情把我迷住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be struck ˈdumb (with sth)</b></td><td>惊得说不出话</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>We were struck dumb at the sight of three armed soldiers in the kitchen.<br>看到三个持枪的士兵在厨房里，我们惊得目瞪口呆。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈdumbstruck (adj.)</b></td><td>惊得目瞪口呆的</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>She stood dumbstruck when they read out her name as the winner.<br>念到她名字是冠军时，她愣在那里目瞪口呆。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌstrut your ˈstuff (informal)</b></td><td>炫技；露一手</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I saw you at the club last night, strutting your stuff on the dance floor!<br>我昨晚看见你在夜总会，在舞场上炫耀自己的舞姿!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(as) ˌstubborn as a ˈmule (often disapproving)</b></td><td>非常固执；倔得像头驴</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>If you tell her what to do, she won't do it because she's as stubborn as a mule. Why not just suggest it to her?<br>你要是吩咐她去做什么，她不会去做，因为她很固执。何不以建议的形式向她提出呢？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get stuck ˈin •get stuck ˈinto sth (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>起劲地干起来</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Here's your food. Now get stuck in (= start eating).<br>这是给你的，快吃吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do your ˈstuff (informal)</b></td><td>露一手；施展本领</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Joy got her guitar and went on stage to do her stuff.<br>乔伊带着自己的吉他，上台露了一手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not give a ˈstuff (BrE, slang)</b></td><td>毫不在乎</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I don't give a stuf what you think!<br>你怎么想我才不在乎呢!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stuff and ˈnonsense (spoken, old-fashioned)</b></td><td>一派胡言；胡说八道</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Stuff and nonsense, nobody ever caught a cold from wet hair.<br>一派胡言，谁会因为头发没干就感冒。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stuff him, that, etc. (spoken, informal)</b></td><td>去他的；才不管那套</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Stuff him, we're going to the concert whether he approves or not.<br>去他的，不管他同不同意我们都去看演唱会。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>that's the ˈstuff (informal)</b></td><td>这就对了；正该如此</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>That's the stuff, keep your elbow up and hit through the ball.<br>这就对了，胳膊肘抬高，把球打透。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get ˈstuffed (also get ˈknotted less frequent)</b></td><td>滚开；少来这套</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>If they don't offer you more money, tell them to get stuffed.<br>如果他们不愿加价，就让他们见鬼去吧!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a stuffed ˈshirt (informal, disapproving)</b></td><td>一本正经的人；古板的人</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>This office is full of stuffed shirts; there's no one fun that I can have a laugh with.<br>办公室里的人个个都一本正经，连个可以与之玩乐打趣的人都没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be (not) sb's ˈstyle</b></td><td>（不）合某人的口味</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Classical music's not my style; 1 prefer rock.<br>古典音乐非我所好，我喜欢摇滚乐。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from the subˈlime to the riˈdiculous</b></td><td>从崇高跌到荒唐</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>His works as an artist range from the sublime to the ridiculous. with verv little in between.<br>作为一位艺术家，他的作品有高水平的，也有低俗的，但很少有介于一者之间的。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a woman, man, person, etc. of ˈsubstance</b></td><td>有钱有势的人；举足轻重的人</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>In those days, a staton master was a man of substance in the community.<br>那时候，车站站长在社区可是个人物。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>nothing sucˌceeds like sucˈcess (saying)</b></td><td>一事成，事事顺</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The first task the students do should be one they are likely to do well. This is because nothing succeeds like success.<br>学生的第一项任务应该是他们很容易就能做好的，这是因为一事成，事事成。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>as ˈsuch</b></td><td>就其本身而言；严格意义上</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>There is no theatre as such in the town, but plays are sometimes performed in the town hall.<br>镇上没有严格意义上的戏院，不过有时候在镇政厅里演出戏剧。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌsuch as it ˈis</b></td><td>尽管质量不高；虽说不怎么样</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>You can borrow my bike, such as it is, but the brakes squeak.<br>我的自行车你可以骑，虽说破了点，刹车还吱吱响。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suck it and ˈsee (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>试试才知道</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>With so many different models of mobile phone available, the best way to find out if one is right for you is to suck it and see.<br>有这么多不同款式的手机可供选择，要想知道哪款最适合你，最好的办法是自己试试。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suck it ˈup (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>忍着；坦然承受</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Nobody likes the night shift, but we just suck it up.<br>谁都不爱上夜班，可我们只能忍着。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>all of a ˈsudden</b></td><td>突然；冷不防</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I was sitting reading my book when all of a sudden the lights went out.<br>我正坐着看书，灯突然灭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sudden ˈdeath</b></td><td>突然死亡法（加时决胜）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The final went to sudden death after ninety minutes without a goal.<br>九十分钟没进球，决赛进入了突然死亡决胜。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not suffer fools ˈgladly</b></td><td>不能容忍蠢人</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He says what he thinks and doesn't suffer fools gladly. Some people consider him a bit arrogant.<br>他想什么就说什么，容不得愚妄之人，有些人认为他有点傲慢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on ˈsufferance</b></td><td>勉强获准；受人容忍</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>He's only staying here on sufferance.<br>他是勉强获准留在这里的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suffice (it) to say (that)... (formal)</b></td><td>只需说……就够了</td><td>★★★<br>★</td><td>I won't tell you all that was sald at the meeting. Suffice it to say that they approved our plan.<br>我不想把会上说的一切都告诉你，只告诉你他们批准了我们的计划就够了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈsugar daddy (informal)</b></td><td>包养年轻女子的阔老头</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>When you tell him that he's a sugar daddy, he gets very angry. He says she isn't interested in his money, only in him.<br>要是你说他是个“甜心干爹”，他就会很生气。他说她对他的钱不感兴趣，只喜欢他本人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at/on sb's sugˈgestion</b></td><td>依某人的建议</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>At his suggestion, I bought the more printer.<br>在他的建议下，我买了那台较</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suit your/sb's ˈbook (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>合某人心意；对某人方便</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>The later meeting suits my book because I can drop the kids off.<br>会议改晚点正合我意，我可以先送孩子。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suit sb (right) ˌdown to the ˈground (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>完全合某人心意</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Working from home suits me right down to the ground these days.<br>这阵子居家办公完全合我的心意。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>suit yourˈself (informal)</b></td><td>随你便</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I choose my assignments to suit myself.<br>我根据自已的喜好选任务。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(the) men in grey ˈsuits (BrE)</b></td><td>幕后掌权的官僚</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>The men in grey suits decided her fate long before the vote.<br>早在投票前，幕后那些人就定了她的命运。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be greater/more than the ˌsum of its ˈparts</b></td><td>整体大于部分之和</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>After their victory, the captain was full of praise for his team, saying that it was a classic case of the whole being greater than the sum of its parts.<br>获胜后，队长对他的队大加赞赏，说这就是一个典型的事例，证明个体相加不如集体的力量大。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in ˈsum (formal)</b></td><td>总之；总而言之</td><td>★★<br>★</td><td>In sum, there are significant gaps in technological development across countries.<br>总之，各国在科技发展方面存在巨大的差距。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>an ˌIndian ˈsummer</b></td><td>深秋的晴暖时节；晚年的黄金期</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>We had an Indian summer that October and ate outside every evening.<br>那年十月出了个小阳春，我们天天在户外吃晚饭。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>pluck/screw/summon up (your/the) ˈcourage (to do sth)</b></td><td>鼓起勇气（做某事）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He finally summoned up the courage to ask her out for coffee.<br>他终于鼓起勇气约她去喝咖啡。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>under the ˈsun</b></td><td>天底下；世上</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He's tried every medicine under the sun, but nothing works.<br>他把世上的药都试遍了，可是都不见效。 〇</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>your Sunday ˈbest (informal, humorous)</b></td><td>最好的衣服；节日盛装</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She got all dressed up in her Sunday best to meet her boyfriend' parents.<br>她穿上自己最好的衣服去见男朋友的父母。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>all and ˈsundry (informal)</b></td><td>所有人；各色人等</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>I don't like you talking about my personal problems to all and sundry.<br>我不喜欢你把我的私人问题告诉所有人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be ˈsunk in sth</b></td><td>陷入（沉思或愁绪）中</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>She just sat there, sunk in thought.<br>她坐在那里，陷入了沉思。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sunny-side ˈup (AmE)</b></td><td>（鸡蛋）只煎一面的</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>How'd you like your eggs — scrambled or sunny-side up?<br>你要的蛋想怎么吃，要炒蛋还是单面煎蛋？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I don't supˈpose you could...</b></td><td>不知你能否……（客气请求）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I don't suppose you could carry this bag for me, could you?<br>不知道你能不能为我拎一下这个包？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I supˈpose so</b></td><td>我想是吧（勉强同意）</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>'Can Tom come too?' 'I suppose so, if he behaves himself.'<br>“汤姆也能来吗？”“我想可以吧，只要他老实点。”（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(not) be supˈposed to (do sth)</b></td><td>按规定（不）应当</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She' supposed to do an hour's homework every evening.<br>她应当每晚做一个小时的家庭作业。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>what's ˈthat supposed to mean? (informal)</b></td><td>你这话什么意思（表气愤或不解）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>'You've changed a lot lately.' 'What's that supposed to mean, exactly?'<br>“你最近变了不少。”“你这话到底什么意思？”（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be sure to do sth (also be sure and do sth spoken)</b></td><td>务必做某事</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Be sure to give your family my regards.<br>代我向你的家人问好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>for ˈsure (informal)</b></td><td>肯定；无疑</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He'll be late again, that's for sure, so order without him.<br>他肯定又要迟到，别等他先点吧。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make ˈsure (of sth/that...)</b></td><td>弄清；确保</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I think the door's locked, but r'd better go and make sure.<br>我想门已经锁上了，不过我还是去看一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(as) sure as eggs is ˈeggs (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</b></td><td>千真万确；肯定无疑</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ifhe goes on driving at that speed, he'll end up in hospital, as sure as eggs is eggs.<br>要是他还是那样开快车，早晚肯定要进医院。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(as) sure as ˈhell (AmE, informal)</b></td><td>的确；毫无疑问</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Joe sure as hell won't want to dress up in a suit and rie.<br>乔确确实实不愿意穿西服系领带。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sure eˈnough</b></td><td>果然；果真</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She said she was going to give up her job and, sure enough, she did.<br>她说她打算辞职，果不其然，她真的辞了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈsure of yourself (sometimes disapproving)</b></td><td>自信；过于自信</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She seems very sure of herself.<br>她看起来很自信。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌsure ˈthing (spoken, especially AmE)</b></td><td>当然；没问题</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>'Can you cover my shift?' 'Sure thing, just tell me when.'<br>“能替我上班吗？”“没问题，说个时间就行。”（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to be ˈsure (formal)</b></td><td>诚然；固然</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>He is intelligent, to be sure, but he's also very lazy.<br>他固然聪明，可是也很懒惰。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>below/beneath the ˈsurface</b></td><td>表象之下；实际上</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>She seems very calm but beneath the surface I'm sure that she's very upset.<br>她看起来很镇静，不过我敢肯定她实际上很不安。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>surˌprise, surˈprise (spoken, ironic)</b></td><td>果然不出所料</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Surprise, surprise, he forgot to bring the tickets he promised to print.<br>瞧吧，他答应打印的票果然忘带了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take sb by surˈprise</b></td><td>使某人吃惊；出其不意</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>His decision to retire took us all by surprise.<br>他退休的决定让我们都深感意外。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>be aˌbove/beˌyond suˈspicion</b></td><td>无可怀疑；毫无嫌疑</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>He is absolutely beyond suspicion.<br>他绝对没有嫌疑。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be under suˈspicion (of sth)</b></td><td>受到怀疑；涉嫌</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>He was still under suspicion and he knew the police were watching him.<br>他仍然有嫌疑，而且他知道警方在盯着他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the finger of susˈpicion</b></td><td>怀疑的矛头</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The finger of suspicion quickly pointed at the only key holder.<br>怀疑的矛头很快指向了唯一有钥匙的人。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>look/sound suspiciously like sth (often humorous)</b></td><td>看（听）上去很像</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Their latest single sounds suspiciously like the last one.<br>他们最新的单曲听上去和上一首很像。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>one ˌswallow doesn't make a ˈsummer (saying)</b></td><td>一燕不成夏；勿以偏概全</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>We won once, but one swallow doesn't make a summer, so stay focused.<br>我们只赢了一场，一燕不成夏，别松劲。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>be in a ˈsweat</b></td><td>满身大汗；焦虑不安</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Ihad to run to work this morning because I got up late. I was in a real sweat when Iarrived.<br>今天早上起晚了， 我不得不跑步上班，等到了的时候我已是大汗淋漓。 2 (</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>by the sweat of your ˈbrow (literary)</b></td><td>靠自己的辛勤劳动</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>They had to live by the sweat of their brow.<br>他们得靠自己的辛勤劳动谋生。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>don't ˈsweat it (AmE, spoken)</b></td><td>别担心；不必在意</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I we're a few minutes late he'll wait for us, so don't sweat it.<br>如果我们迟到几分钟，他会等我们的，别担心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>don't sweat the ˈsmall stuff (AmE, spoken)</b></td><td>别为小事烦心</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Don't sweat the small stuff; the guests won't notice the napkin colour.<br>别为鸡毛蒜皮操心，客人不会注意餐巾颜色。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>no ˈsweat (spoken)</b></td><td>没问题；小事一桩</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>'Can you drive me over?' 'No sweat, I'm going that way anyway.'<br>“能开车送我过去吗？”“小事一桩，我正好顺路。”（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweat ˈblood (informal)</b></td><td>拼命干；极度焦虑</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We sweated blood to get the exhibition ready in three weeks.<br>为了三周内布好展，我们拼了命。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweat it ˈout (informal)</b></td><td>苦熬；坚持到最后</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I hate this job, but I'm going to sweat it out and hope something better comes along.<br>我讨厌这份工作， 可是我打算忍一忍，希望会有什么好差事到来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweat like a ˈpig (informal)</b></td><td>大汗淋漓</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>It's 35 sweat degrees inside the factory, and the workers are sweating like pigs.<br>工厂里的温度高达35度。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweep the ˈboard</b></td><td>囊括所有奖项</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>At the awards ceremony last night France swept the board, with six major prizes.<br>在昨晚的颁奖仪式上，法国囊括了六项大奖。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweep sb off their ˈfeet</b></td><td>使某人倾倒；令某人着迷</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She's waiting for a nice young man to come and sweep her off her feet.<br>她在等待一个年轻英俊的男人的到来，能让她一见倾心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do sth in your ˌown sweet ˈtime/way (informal)</b></td><td>随心所欲地做；不慌不忙</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I tried to give her advice but she just went on in her own some sweet way.<br>我想给她提点建议，可是她依旧我行我素。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a sweet ˈtooth</b></td><td>爱吃甜食</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Tve got a sweet tooth, so r'd find it difficult to give up sugar in my tea.<br>我好吃甜食，喝茶的时候总想放糖。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep sb ˈsweet (informal)</b></td><td>讨好某人；哄住某人</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I have to keep my mother sweet because I want to borrow the car.<br>我不得不跟我妈套近乎，因为我想跟她借车。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>she's ˈsweet (AustralE, New Zealand, informal)</b></td><td>一切都好；没问题</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Don't worry about the booking, mate, she's sweet, I called them already.<br>订位的事别操心，兄弟，都搞定了，我打过电话了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweet FˈA (also less frequent sweet Fanny ˈAdams) (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>什么也没有；屁事没干</td><td>★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I did sweet FA all weekend except watch films and eat toast.<br>整个周末我啥也没干，就看电影吃吐司。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>sweet ˈnothings (informal, usually humorous)</b></td><td>甜言蜜语；绵绵情话</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He was whispering sweet nothings in her ear.<br>他向她低诉喁喁情话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the sweet smell of sucˈcess (informal)</b></td><td>成功的喜悦</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>After ten years of rejection she finally tasted the sweet smell of success.<br>被拒了十年，她终于尝到了成功的滋味。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be all ˌsweetness and ˈlight</b></td><td>和蔼可亲；一团和气</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>He's all sweetness and light until you question his budget figures.<br>他一团和气，除非你质疑他的预算数字。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in(to) the ˈswim (of things) (informal)</b></td><td>融入活动；跟上潮流</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>After being away for two years, it took her a while to get back into the swim of things.<br>离开两年了，她过了好一阵子才重新适应。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get in/into the ˈswing (of sth) (informal)</b></td><td>进入状态；投入其中</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Tve only been at college a week, so I haven't got into the swing of things yet.<br>我上大学才一个星期，还没有适应新环</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go with a ˈswing (BrE)</b></td><td>（活动）热闹成功</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Their house-warming party really went with a swing.<br>他们的乔迁聚会确实很热闹。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>swing both ˈways (informal)</b></td><td>是双性恋</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He mentioned casually that he swings both ways and nobody blinked.<br>他随口说自己是双性恋，谁也没觉得意外。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌswing into ˈaction</b></td><td>立即行动起来</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>When the police heard about the bomb, they swung into action, searching the area with dogs and moving the public to safety.<br>听说有炸弹，警察立即出动，带着警犬在周围搜查，将群众疏散到安全地带。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>swing the ˈlead (old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</b></td><td>装病偷懒</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>Idon't think there's anything wrong with her — she's just swinging the lead.<br>我想她没什么不舒服的，她只是为了逃避工作。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>swings and ˈroundabouts (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>有得有失；失之东隅收之桑榆</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Higher earnings mean more tax, so it's all swings and roundabouts.<br>挣得多交的税也就多，有得必有失嘛。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>what you gain on the swings you lose on the ˈroundabouts (saying)</b></td><td>有所得必有所失</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>What you gain on the swings you lose on the roundabouts, as Dad says.<br>正如老爸所说，有所得必有所失。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a/the sword of ˈDamocles (literary)</b></td><td>达摩克利斯之剑；随时降临的祸患</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Now the news of my divorce is public, I'm relieved in a way. It had been hanging over my head like the sword of Damocles.<br>现在我离婚的事公开了，我反倒觉得轻松了。这件事过去一直像达摩克利斯剑一样悬在我的头上。 ©</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>beat/turn swords into ˈploughshares (literary)</b></td><td>铸剑为犁；化干戈为玉帛</td><td>★<br>★</td><td>The treaty promised to turn swords into ploughshares across the whole region.<br>条约承诺让整个地区铸剑为犁。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in ˈsympathy with sth (written)</b></td><td>随……变动；受……影响</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Share prices slipped again today, in sympathy with the German market.<br>受德国市场的影响，股票价格今天再次滑落。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>out of ˈsympathy with sb/sth (written)</b></td><td>不赞同；不支持</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>It is generally believed that he is out of sympathy with government policies.<br>人们普遍认为他不赞成政府的政策。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in/out of ˈsync (informal)</b></td><td>同步；不同步</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The soundtrack is not in sync with the picture.<br>声迹和画面不同步。0</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get sth out of your ˈsystem (informal)</b></td><td>发泄出来；排遣掉</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Tell him how angry you really feel. Thatll get it out of your system.<br>告诉他你有多生气，这样可以帮你将怒气发泄出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>all systems ˈgo (for sth) (informal)</b></td><td>一切就绪；万事俱备</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The wind had dropped, the sun was shining and it was all systems go for the airshow.<br>风力已减弱，阳光一片灿烂，可以开始飞行表演了。</td></tr>
<tr class="sec"><td colspan="4">T</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to a ˈT/tee (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>恰好；分毫不差</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>This new job suits me to a I (= it is perfect for me).<br>这份新工作正适合我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to the smallest deˈtail</b></td><td>到最细微处；极其详尽</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She described the room to the smallest detail, right down to the wallpaper.<br>她把房间描述得极其细致，连墙纸都说到了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on the ˈtable (BrE)</b></td><td>提交讨论中；供考虑</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>In today's meeting there were several new Proposals on the table.<br>今天会上提出了几项新提案。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turn the ˈtables (on sb)</b></td><td>扭转局势；转败为胜</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>They beat us 3-0 last year, but we turned the tables on them this year — we won 5-0.<br>去年他们以 3:0打败了我们，但是今年我们报了一箭之仇，以5:0获胜。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep (close) ˈtabs on sb/sth (informal)</b></td><td>密切注意；监视</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Tm not sure about Johnson - we'd better keep tabs on him until we know we can trust him.<br>我对约翰逊不太放心。我们取好先观察他一段时间，直到我们确信可以信任他为止。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>on sb's ˈtail (informal)</b></td><td>紧跟；尾随</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I had the feeling there was someone on my tail.<br>我感觉到有人在跟踪我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(at) the tail ˈend (of sth)</b></td><td>末尾；尾声</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I didn't hear most of the conversation —1only came in at the tail end.<br>谈话的大部分我都没有听到，我来时谈话已接近尾声了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the tail (is) wagging the ˈdog (also let the tail wag the ˈdog)</b></td><td>本末倒置；喧宾夺主</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>In this company the workers tell the manager what he can and cannot do. It's a real case of the tail wag. ging the dog.<br>这家公司里是雇员规定经理的职权范围，真是上下颠倒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>turn ˈtail (and run, flee, etc.)</b></td><td>转身逃跑；临阵脱逃</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The fox turned tail and ran the moment the dog barked.<br>狗一叫，狐狸转身就跑。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>with your tail between your ˈlegs (informal)</b></td><td>夹着尾巴；灰溜溜地</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>They thought they would win easily, but theyve gone home with their tails between their legs.<br>他们本以为能够轻易获胜，结果却灰溜溜地回了家。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be on the ˈtake (informal)</b></td><td>收受贿赂</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Two officers were on the take for years before anyone noticed.<br>两名警官受贿多年才被人察觉。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I, ˌyou, ˌetc. can't take sb ˈanywhere (informal, often humorous)</b></td><td>某人上不了台面</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You've got soup all over your shirt —Ican't take you anywhere, can 1?<br>你把汤洒得衬衫上到处都是，真是没法带你出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take sth as it ˈcomes</b></td><td>顺其自然；随遇而安</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Idon't plan for the future. I like to take life as it comes.<br>我不规划未来，我喜欢顺其自然地生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈtake it (informal)</b></td><td>忍受；承受得住</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>They argued so much couldn't take it any more and he left her.<br>他们经常吵架，最后他终于受不了，离开了她。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈtake it (that...)</b></td><td>认为；猜想；假定</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I take it that you won't be back for lunch,' she said as they left.<br>们不会回来吃午饭了吧。”他们离开时她说道。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take it from ˈhere/ˈthere</b></td><td>接手余下的事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I explained how to start the machine, and let him take it from there.<br>我已解释了怎样开动机器，之后的事交给了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take it from ˈme (that...) (informal)</b></td><td>相信我；我敢担保</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Take it from me that it's not easy to become a professional writer.<br>相信我，要成为职业作家并不容易。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take it on/upon yourself to do sth</b></td><td>自作主张做某事</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>He took it upon himself to dismiss my secretary, which he had no right to do.<br>他白作主张解雇了我的秘书，他无权这么做。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take it ˈout of sb •take a lot ˈout of sb</b></td><td>使人筋疲力尽</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Those night shifts really take it out of you after a while.<br>上久了夜班真会把人累垮。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take it ˈout on sb (informal)</b></td><td>拿某人出气</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I know you've had a bad day at work, but don't take it out on me.<br>我知道你今天工作不顺利，但是也别拿我出气啊。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take sb ˈout of himself, herself, etc.</b></td><td>使某人排解忧愁</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>She was very depressed when they split up. We took her away for a few days to try to take her out of herself.<br>他们分手的时候她很难过。我们带她出去呆几天好让她散散心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have what it ˈtakes (to do sth) (informal)</b></td><td>具备成功的条件</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He's certainly ambitious, but if you ask me he hasn't really got what it takes to be the best.<br>他确实雄心勃勃，但是要我说的话，他并不具备成为最优秀者的条件。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be sb's for the ˈtaking</b></td><td>唾手可得</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>With two rivals injured, the title was hers for the taking.<br>两个对手受伤，冠军对她来说唾手可得。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be there for the ˈtaking</b></td><td>唾手可得；手到擒来</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She was surprised to find the money on the kitchen table, just there for the taking.<br>她惊讶地发现钱就放在餐桌上，伸手可拿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be all ˈtalk (and no action) (disapproving)</b></td><td>光说不练</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Dont listen to her promises - she's all talk and no action.<br>别听她的那些许诺，她就只会说空话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be the talk of sth (informal)</b></td><td>成为大家谈论的话题</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>His collection is the talk of the Milan fashion shows.<br>他的时装系列成为米兰时装展的热门话题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be the talk of the ˈtown</b></td><td>成为全城的话题</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Overnight she became the talk of the town after that radio interview.<br>那次电台采访后，她一夜之间成了全城的话题。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈyou can/can't talk (also look who's ˈtalking) (spoken)</b></td><td>你还好意思说别人</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You can't talk, your desk is even messier than mine right now.<br>你还好意思说，你桌子比我的还乱。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>you're a ˈfine one to talk (spoken)</b></td><td>你还有脸说别人</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You're a fine one to talk about being late, Mr Nine-Thirty.<br>你还有脸说人家迟到，九点半先生。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈtalk about... (spoken)</b></td><td>真是……（用于强调）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Did you watch the programme on the Labour Party last night? Talk about biased!<br>你看了昨晚关于工党的节目了吗？真是很有偏见!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk ˈbig (disapproving)</b></td><td>说大话；吹牛</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The President talks big but he doesn't do anything.<br>总统大话说得不少，实事却没做过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk ˈdirty (informal)</b></td><td>说下流话</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>I love it when you talk dirty.<br>我喜欢听你说荤话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk sb's ˈear off (especially AmE, informal, especially disapproving)</b></td><td>对某人唠叨不停</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>That guy on the plane talked my ear off-I couldn't wait to land!<br>飞机上的那个家伙对我唠叨个没完，我巴不得飞机马上着陆!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk your ˈhead off (informal)</b></td><td>说个不停</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He talked his head of all evening.<br>他整晚都在喋喋不休。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk the hind leg(s) off a ˈdonkey (informal, humorous)</b></td><td>唠叨不休；滔滔不绝</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>He would make a good politician - he could talk the hind legs off a donkey!<br>他做政客肯定合适，他能滔滔不绝地说个不停!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk ˈshop</b></td><td>在社交场合谈公事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Are you two talking shop again?Why don't you forget business for a while and come and meet my friends?<br>你们俩又在谈工作了吧？你们就不能暂时忘掉公事，过来见见我的朋友们？•'</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk through the back of your ˈhead (informal)</b></td><td>胡说八道</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>He's talking through the back of his head about those tax rules.<br>他讲那些税法完全是胡说八道。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk through your ˈhat (old-fashioned, informal)</b></td><td>信口开河；瞎扯</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>Don't take any notice of him. He's talk. ing through his hat, as usual.<br>别理他，他又像往常一样，在瞎说呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk to a brick ˈwall (informal)</b></td><td>对牛弹琴；白费口舌</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Talking to him is like talking to a brick wall. He just won't listen.<br>跟他讲话只是白费口舌，他就是不听。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk ˈtough (on sth) (informal, especially AmE)</b></td><td>说话口气强硬</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Before the elections, the party talked tough on crime, but little has been done since they've been in power.<br>大选之前，该党表示要严厉打击犯罪，但是当政以后他们毫无动作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk ˈturkey (informal, especially AmE)</b></td><td>谈正事；开门见山</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Look,Mark, it's time we talked turkey. How much money can you invest in the company?<br>喂，马克，我们该认真地谈谈实际问题了。你能给公司投多少钱？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talk your way out of sth/out of doing sth</b></td><td>靠嘴皮子脱身</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He tried to talk his way out of it by saying someone else was responsible.<br>他尽力替自己开脱，说责任在别人身上。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈnow you're talking (spoken)</b></td><td>这话我爱听；正合我意</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Free pizza? Now you're talking, count me in for the evening.<br>免费披萨？这话我爱听，晚上算我一个。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>talking of sb/sth (spoken, especially BrE)</b></td><td>说到；提起</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Talking of holidays, have you booked anything for the summer yet?<br>说到假期，你暑假订好行程了吗？（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>stand ˈtall (especially AmE)</b></td><td>昂首挺胸；自信坦然</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Speaking on television, she said that her former manager's advce to stand tall and be proud of herself was what helped her to succeed.<br>在电视上，她说前任经理曾告诉她要扬起头，要为自己骄傲，正是这些忠告帮助她取得了成功。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌtall ˈorder</b></td><td>难办的要求；苛求</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Finishing this work by the end of the week is a tall order, but tul try.<br>周末之前完成这项工作简直太难了，可是我会尽力的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌtall ˈstory (especially BrE) (AmE usually a ˌtall ˈtale)</b></td><td>荒诞的故事；吹牛</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>What she says about her grandfather being a foreign prince sounds like a tall story to me.<br>她说她祖父是外国王子之类的话在我听来完全是无稽之谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in ˈtandem (with sb/sth)</b></td><td>协同；一前一后地</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The two charities work in tandem to house families every winter.<br>这两家慈善机构每年冬天协同安置无家可归的家庭。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go off at a ˈtangent (BrE) (AmE go off on a ˈtangent)</b></td><td>突然改变话题（或思路）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>One moment the professor is working hard on a problem in Physics, the next he's gone off at a tangent and he's talking about bees.<br>前一分钟教授还在努力解答物理题，下一分钟他就突然开始讲起蜜蜂来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the ˈtank (AmE, informal, business)</b></td><td>（股价等）急剧下跌</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Technology stocks are doing well, but everything else is in the tank.<br>科技股表现不错，但其他股票的价格全盘下跌。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>throw a ˈtantrum (BrE also throw a ˈwobbly)</b></td><td>大发脾气；耍性子</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>When you were a child, you were always throwing tantrums.<br>你小时候总是乱发脾气。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(be) on ˈtap</b></td><td>随时可用；现成的</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Tve got plenty of people on tap to help us if we need them.<br>如果需要的话，我这儿有很多人随时可以支援我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have sb/sth ˈtaped (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>摸清底细；彻底了解</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>He can't fool me — Tve got him taped.<br>他骗不了我，我已经摸清了他的底细。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tar sb/sth with the same ˈbrush</b></td><td>一概而论；视为一丘之貉</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Don't tar every landlord with the same brush because of one.<br>别因为一个房东就把所有房东一竿子打死。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wouldn't do sth for all the ˌtea in ˈChina</b></td><td>无论如何也不做某事</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I wouldn't move back to that town for all the tea in China.<br>给我再多好处，我也不搬回那个镇子。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take sb to ˈtask (about/for/over sth)</b></td><td>严厉批评某人；训斥</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>I was taken to task for arriving late.<br>我因为迟到被狠狠地训了一通。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be in bad, the worst possible, etc. ˈtaste</b></td><td>趣味低俗；很不得体</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>That joke about the funeral was in the worst possible taste.<br>拿葬礼开的那个玩笑实在低俗透顶。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be in good, the best possible, etc. ˈtaste</b></td><td>得体；有品位</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>They made a few jokes about the manageunpleasant experience, that you have done sth ment, but it was all done in good taste.<br>他们开了</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leave a bad/nasty ˈtaste in the/your mouth</b></td><td>使人心里不痛快</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The way they fired him left a nasty taste in my mouth.<br>他们辞退他的方式让我心里很不是滋味。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to ˈtaste</b></td><td>按各人口味（加调料）</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Add salt and pepper to taste, then let the sauce simmer gently.<br>按口味加盐和胡椒，然后让酱汁慢慢煨着。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be in ˈtatters</b></td><td>破烂不堪；彻底破灭</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>His reputation was in tatters after the newspaper published those photos.<br>报纸登出那些照片后，他的名声一败涂地。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tear yourself/sth ˈloose (from sb/sth)</b></td><td>挣脱；奋力摆脱</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>She tore herself loose from his grip and ran towards the door.<br>她奋力挣脱他的手，朝门口跑去。（自拟）</td></tr>

I think you should be the one to ask the boss - he thinks the sun shines out of your backside!<br>要完成这项工作我们需要更多的资金， 我觉得你去跟老板说最合适，他最看重你!</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>in a tight ˈcorner/ˈspot (informal)</b></td><td>身处困境；遇到大麻烦</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He's in a bit of a tight spot at the moment. The bank has given him one week to find $2 000.<br>他现在有点焦头烂额，银行让他在一个星期以内凑足2000美元。</td></tr>
