<tr><td><b>run a ˌtight ˈship</b></td><td>管理有方；治理严明</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The boss runs a very tight ship and everybody is expected to work very hard.<br>老板管得很严，每个人都得非常努力地工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˌtight ˈsqueeze</b></td><td>极其拥挤；勉强挤得下</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We managed to get all the luggage in the car but it was a tight squeeze.<br>我们终于把所有的行李都弄上了车，可是车里挤得严严实实的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tighten your ˈbelt</b></td><td>勒紧裤腰带；省吃俭用</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>In wartime everyone has to tghten their belts.<br>战争时期大家都必须省吃俭用。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tread/walk a ˈtightrope</b></td><td>走钢丝；如履薄冰地行事</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He walks a tightrope between pleasing his boss and protecting his team.<br>他在讨好老板和保护团队之间走钢丝。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be on a ˈtightrope</b></td><td>处境微妙；如走钢丝般艰难</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>I'm walking a tightrope at the moment; one more mistake and I might lose my job.<br>我现在处境不妙，再犯一个错误就可能会被开除。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have your ˌfingers/ˌhand in the ˈtill (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>监守自盗；偷单位的钱</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>He lost his job after they found he'd had his hand in the till.<br>在被人发现偷公司的钱之后，他被解雇了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tilt at ˈwindmills</b></td><td>跟假想敌搏斗；徒费精力</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>Complaining to that office is tilting at windmills; nobody ever replies.<br>向那个办公室投诉是白费劲，从来没人回。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(and) about ˈtime (ˈtoo)</b></td><td>早该如此；也该是时候了</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>They're finally fixing the road, and about time too.<br>他们总算要修那条路了，也该是时候了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(and) not before ˈtime (spoken)</b></td><td>早该如此；总算等到了</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Here comes the bus - and about time too.<br>公共汽车来了—也该到了。0</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>against ˈtime (also against the ˈclock)</b></td><td>抢时间；争分夺秒</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We've only got two days to find a replacement, so we're racing against time.<br>我们只有两天的时间找接替者，所以我们正在抓紧时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ahead of/behind ˈtime</b></td><td>提前；迟于预定时间</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He arrived ahead of time, and had to wait.<br>他提前到了，只好等一等。 〇</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>all the ˈtime • the whole ˈtime</b></td><td>（某段时间内）一直；始终</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The letter was in my pocket the whole time (= while I was looking for it).<br>这封信一直都在我的口袋里(我却在到处找)。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈany time (spoken)</b></td><td>（回应致谢）不客气；随时乐意效劳</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>'Thanks for the lift home.' 'Any time, just give me a call.'<br>「谢谢你送我回家。」「随时效劳，打电话就行。」（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at a ˈtime</b></td><td>每次；一次…地</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We had to go and see the principal one at a time.<br>我们得挨个去见校卡。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at the ˈtime</b></td><td>当时；那时候</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I remember watching the first men on the moon on television; I was only six at the time.<br>我还记得在电视上看见人类首次登月，那时我才六岁。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at ˈmy, ˈyour, etc. time of life</b></td><td>在我（或你等）这个年纪</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Learn to drive at my time of life? Don't be silly!<br>我这把年纪学开车？别傻了!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be ahead of/before/in advance of your ˈtime</b></td><td>超前；超越时代</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He was sure that it was possible to fly to the moon, but he was ahead of his time and people laughed at him.<br>他确信飞抵月球是可以实现的，可是这种想法在当时很前卫，人们都嘲笑他。◎</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be before sb's ˈtime</b></td><td>在某人记事之前；早于某人的年代</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The Beatles were a bit before my time.<br>披头士乐队早于我所处的年代。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be (stuck) in a ˈtime warp</b></td><td>停留在过去；仿佛困在旧时光里</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Her whole house seems to be stuck in a time warp. It's like something out of the 1950s.<br>她的整个房子似乎定格在过去，还是20 世纪50年代的样子。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do/serve ˈtime (informal)</b></td><td>服刑；坐牢</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He had done time for robbing a bank.<br>他因为抢劫银行而坐过半。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈevery time</b></td><td>总是（选择）；只要可以就</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I don't really like cities — give me the countryside every time.<br>我不太喜欢城市，我总是喜欢去乡下。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>for the time ˈbeing (also for the ˈmoment/ˈpresent)</b></td><td>暂时；眼下</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He can stay with us for the time being until he finds a place of his own.<br>在他找到自己的住处之前可以暂时住在我们这儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from/since ˌtime immeˈmorial</b></td><td>自古以来；从很早以前</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The Barton family have lived in this village since time immemorial.<br>巴顿家族自古以来就住在这个村子里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>from ˌtime to ˈtime</b></td><td>不时；偶尔</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We go to the theatre from time to time.<br>我们偶尔去看场电影。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give sb a rough, hard, bad, etc. ˈtime (of it)</b></td><td>故意为难某人；让某人不好过</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ever since I started work here, she's been shouting at me and giving me a hard time.<br>自从我在这儿上班以后，她就对我大喊大叫，故意折腾我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a lot of ˈtime for sb/sth (informal, especially BrE)</b></td><td>很喜欢；很欣赏</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I have a lot of time for our postman; he checks on the elderly.<br>我很欣赏我们的邮递员，他会去看看独居老人。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have no ˈtime for sb/sth</b></td><td>讨厌；瞧不上</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She has no time for people who complain but never vote.<br>她瞧不上那些只会抱怨却从不投票的人。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not have much ˈtime for sb/sth (informal)</b></td><td>不喜欢；不怎么看得上</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I have no time for lazy people like him.<br>我可不喜欢像他那样的懒虫。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a (hard, rough, bad, etc.) ˈtime of it</b></td><td>日子不好过；困难重重</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We're having a time of it at the moment with the builders in the house.<br>现在有那些建筑工人在家里，我们的日子要不好过了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have the ˌtime of your ˈlife (informal)</b></td><td>玩得非常痛快；快活极了</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The children had the time of their lives at the circus.<br>孩子们在马戏场玩得很开心。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have ˈtime on your hands (informal)</b></td><td>闲着没事；空闲时间太多</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Since retiring he's had time on his hands and started painting.<br>退休后他闲得慌，就开始画画了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(all) in good ˈtime (spoken)</b></td><td>到时候自然会；不用着急</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Be Patient, Emily! All in good time.<br>别着急，埃米莉!很快就好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in (less than/next to) ˈno time</b></td><td>立刻；转眼之间</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The kids will be leaving home in no time.<br>孩子们很快就会离开察。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in your own good ˈtime (informal)</b></td><td>等自己方便时；等自己准备好再说</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He'll tell us what happened in his own good time; don't push him.<br>他想说的时候自然会说，别逼他。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in your own ˈtime</b></td><td>在业余时间；用自己的时间</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Please make private phone calls in your own time, Mr Davies, not when you are at work.<br>戴维斯先生，请在工作以外的时间打私人电话，别在上班的时候打。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in ˈtime</b></td><td>及时；来得及</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Make sure that you get here in time for the concert.<br>你一定要及时赶到这儿，别错过了音乐会。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's ˌhigh/aˌbout ˈtime (that)... (spoken)</b></td><td>早就该…了；也该…了</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>It's high time you learned to cook something other than noodles.<br>你早就该学着做点面条以外的东西了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's only, just, etc. a matter/a question of ˈtime (before...)</b></td><td>只是时间问题；迟早的事</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>It's only a matter of time before that old bridge has to close.<br>那座老桥关闭只是时间问题。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's only a matter/a question of ˈtime (before...)</b></td><td>迟早的事；只是时间问题</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Don't worry, youll get a job if you keep looking. It's just a matter of time.<br>别担心，只要继续找下去，你会找到工作的，这只是时间问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep ˈtime</b></td><td>（钟表）走得准</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>It's an old watch, but it keeps very good time.<br>这只表旧了，但是走得很准。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lose/waste no ˈtime (in doing sth)</b></td><td>毫不拖延；立即行动</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>As soon as she arrived back home, she lost no time in visiting all her old friends.<br>她一回到家就立刻去拜访所有的老朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make good, etc. ˈtime</b></td><td>行程顺利；走得比预期快</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>On the first part of the trip we made good time.<br>旅程的第一段我们一路很顺利。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>make ˈtime (to do sth)</b></td><td>抽出时间（做某事）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Tm very busy, but Tul try to make time to do it.<br>我很忙，但我会尽量腾出时间来做这件事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈmany a time • ˈmany's the time (that)...</b></td><td>经常；许多次</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>Many a time I've walked home from that station in the rain.<br>我不知多少次冒雨从那个车站走回家。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(the) next, first, second, etc. time aˈround/aˈround</b></td><td>下一次（或第一次等）同样的事发生时</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He repeated none of the errors he'd made first time round.<br>他第一次犯的那些错误再也没犯过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not give sb the ˌtime of ˈday</b></td><td>不理睬某人；不肯搭理</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Since the success of her novel, people shake her hand who once wouldn' have given her the time of day.<br>自从她的小说获得了成功，那些以前不爱搭理她的人都来跟她握手。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(there's) no time like the ˈpresent (saying)</b></td><td>现在就是最好的时机；说做就做</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>You want to call her? There's no time like the present.<br>你想给她打电话？现在就打，别等了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>of all ˈtime</b></td><td>有史以来</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Which do you think is the best movie of all time?<br>你认为有史以来哪部电影最棒？>'</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(right) on ˈtime (also bang on ˈtime) (informal)</b></td><td>准时；按时</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I always have to wait for you—you're never on time.<br>我老是得等你，你从来没准时过。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>play for ˈtime</b></td><td>拖延时间；争取时间</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>If1 can play for time a bit longer, they might lower their price.<br>如果我能多拖延一会儿的话，他们也许会降价的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>take your ˈtime (doing sth/to do sth/over sth)</b></td><td>慢慢来；不着急</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>There's no rush — take your time.<br>不用着急，慢慢来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>there's no time to ˈlose</b></td><td>刻不容缓；一刻也不能耽搁</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The tide is coming in fast, so there's no time to lose.<br>潮水涨得快，一刻也不能耽搁。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>there's no time to be ˈlost (saying)</b></td><td>必须立刻行动；没时间可耽搁</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Come on, there's no time to lose! The plane leaves in half an hour!<br>快点，不能再耽搁了!飞机半个小时后起 !</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌtime after ˈtime • ˌtime and (time) aˈgain</b></td><td>一次又一次；屡次</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He makes the same mistake time after time.<br>他一次又一次地犯同样的错误。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>time ˈflies (saying)</b></td><td>时间过得真快；光阴似箭</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>How time flies!Tve got to g0 now.<br>时间过得真快啊!我得走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>time hangs/lies ˈheavy (on your ˈhands)</b></td><td>时间难熬；闲得无聊</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>In prison, time hangs heavy.<br>在监狱里真是度日如年。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>time is getting ˈon</b></td><td>时间不早了；没多少时间了</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Wedd better hurry up and finish; time's getting on.<br>我们得赶紧做完， 没有多少时间了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>time is ˈmoney (saying)</b></td><td>时间就是金钱</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Hurry up and load the van; time is money in this business.<br>快点装车，干这行时间就是金钱。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>time is on sb's ˈside (also have time on your side)</b></td><td>有的是时间；时间对某人有利</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Although she failed the exam, time is on her side; she is young enough to take it again next year.<br>虽然她没通过考试，但是她还有时间，她还年轻，可以明年再考一次。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the time is ˈripe (for sb) (to do sth)</b></td><td>时机已经成熟</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>The time is ripe for us to open a second shop in the old town.<br>在老城区开第二家店，时机已经成熟。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the time is ˈripe for sth/for doing sth (literary)</b></td><td>时机成熟；正是做某事的时候</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>I think the time's ripe for him to leave home if he wants to.<br>我认为如果他想离开家，时候已经到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>time ˈwas (when)... (old-fashioned)</b></td><td>曾经有那么个时候；那年头</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Time was when you could go for a walk in the country and not see another person for miles.<br>过去你可以在乡间散步走上好几英里也看不到一个人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>time (alone) will ˈtell • only time will ˈtell</b></td><td>时间会证明一切</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Only time will tell if the treatment has been successful.<br>只有时间才能证明这种疗法是否有效。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at all ˈtimes</b></td><td>总是；随时</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Visitors must wear their badges at all times inside the laboratory.<br>在实验室内，访客必须随时佩戴证件。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>at ˈtimes</b></td><td>有时；间或</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>At times I wonder whether hell ever get a job.<br>有的时候我会想他到底能不能找到工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be behind the ˈtimes</b></td><td>落后于时代；过时</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You're etc. behind the times if you think a visit to the dentist has to be painful.<br>如果你还以为看牙一定很疼的话你就落伍了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep up, move, etc. with the ˈtimes</b></td><td>与时俱进；跟上时代</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>In business it's important to keep up with the times.<br>在商界重要的是跟上时代。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a tin ˈear (for sth) (informal)</b></td><td>没有乐感；分不清音高</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Even those ofus with a tn ear can recognize a waltz.<br>我们这些没有乐感的人也能听得出华尔兹的节奏。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be on the tip of your ˈtongue</b></td><td>话到嘴边（却想不起来）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>What's her name? You know, that tall Italian girl...it's on the tp of my tongue.. Claudia, that's it!<br>她叫什么来着？就那个高高的意大利女孩⋯就在我嘴边上⋯克劳迪娅，想起</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be the tip of the ˈiceberg</b></td><td>只是冰山一角；只是问题的一小部分</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Those two complaints are just the tip of the iceberg, believe me.<br>信我的，那两起投诉不过是冰山一角。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tip the ˈbalance/ˈscales (also swing the ˈbalance/ˈscales)</b></td><td>使天平倾斜；起决定性作用</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Her experience abroad tipped the balance in favour of hiring her.<br>她的海外经历成了录用她的决定因素。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>tip the scales at sth</b></td><td>体重（或重量）为…</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The prize pumpkin tipped the scales at nearly ninety kilos.<br>那个获奖南瓜足足有近九十公斤重。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>have your, his, its, etc. ˈuses (informal, often humorous)</b></td><td>有时还是挺有用的</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I know you don't like him, but he has his uses — he's a great cook!<br>我知道你不喜欢他，可他有他的好处，他做菜做得可好了!</td></tr>

They were just a voice in the wilderness.<br>几位科学家在20 世纪80年代早期就曾警告过艾滋病的危险性，但当时人们都不以为然。这些警告就像是旷野里的呼唤，无人理会。 ②</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>be underˈway</b></td><td>已经开始；正在进行中</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>A major search is under way to find the escaped prisoners.<br>大规模搜捕逃犯的行动已经展开。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>by the ˈway (also by the ˈby/ˈbye less frequent)</b></td><td>顺便说一句；附带问一句</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ihad a meeting with Graham at work today... by the way, Tve invited him and his wife to lunch on Sunday.<br>今天上班时，我与格雷厄姆会面了⋯顺便提一下，我已经邀请他和他夫人周日吃午餐。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>come your ˈway</b></td><td>（机会等）落到你头上</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Take the internship, chances like this do not come your way often.<br>接下这个实习吧，这种机会可不常有。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do sth in a big/small ˈway</b></td><td>大张旗鼓地做；小打小闹地做</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>They celebrate birthdays in a big way, with fifty guests and a band.<br>他们过生日很铺张，请五十位客人还有乐队。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>do sth on/along the ˈway</b></td><td>顺路做某事</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I will pick up the dry cleaning on the way to the station.<br>我去车站的路上顺便取一下干洗的衣服。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˈeither way • one way or the ˈother</b></td><td>两者都一样；不管怎样</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Was it his fault or not? Either way, an explanation is due.<br>是他的错吗？无论是不是，都得有个解释。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>every ˈwhich way (informal)</b></td><td>四面八方；乱七八糟</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Her hair in all directions tumbled every which way.<br>她的头发乱七八糟的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get in the ˈway (of sth)</b></td><td>妨碍；挡道</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>He wouldn't allow emotlons to get in the way of him doing his job.<br>他不会让感情妨碍自己的工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get into/out of the way of sth/of doing sth</b></td><td>养成或改掉某种习惯</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>I have got into the way of walking to work every morning.<br>我已经养成了每天早上走路上班的习惯。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get sth out of the ˈway</b></td><td>把某事处理掉；先解决掉</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I'm glad Tve got that visit to the dentist out of the way.<br>我很高兴没有因为去看牙医而误事 ˈ</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it/things/everything (all) your (own) ˈway</b></td><td>事事随心所欲；一切照自己的意思</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You cannot always have everything your own way at work.<br>在单位你不可能事事都随自己的意思。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give ˈway</b></td><td>断裂；塌陷；垮掉</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The old wooden balcony gave way under the weight of the guests.<br>客人一多，那个旧木阳台就塌了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give ˈway (to sb/sth)</b></td><td>让路；让步；被取代</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Give way to traffic coming from the left.<br>让左边来的车辆先行。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go all the ˈway (with sb) (informal)</b></td><td>完全赞同；与某人发生性关系</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The new law goes a long way towards solving the problem.<br>新的法律十分有助于解决这一问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go out of your ˈway (to do sth)</b></td><td>特意；不辞辛劳地</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She went out of her way to cook a really nice meal.<br>她特地做了一顿美餐。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go your own ˈway</b></td><td>我行我素；一意孤行</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Teenagers always go their own way, and it's no use trying to stop them.<br>青少年总是我行我素，谁也拦不住他们。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go sb's ˈway</b></td><td>与某人同路；（事情）合某人心意</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Nothing went my way at all during that first month abroad.<br>刚出国那个月，什么事都不顺我的意。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go the way of all ˈflesh</b></td><td>走向人生终点；死亡</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>Poor old Johnson has gone the way of all flesh, and the world is certainly a poorer place for it.<br>可怜的老约翰逊走到了人生的终点，从此世界就少了些精彩。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a way of doing sth</b></td><td>往往会；总是这样</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Problems have a way of solving themselves if you sleep on them.<br>很多问题搁一晚上往往就自己解决了。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>in a ˈway • in ˈone way (also in ˈsome ways)</b></td><td>在某种程度上；从某方面说</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>In a way, living in the town is better than the country, because there's much more to do.<br>在某种程度上，城里比乡下适合居住，因为城里生活要丰富得多。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in his, her, its, etc. (own) ˈway</b></td><td>以其特有的方式</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I think she does love you in her own way.<br>我想她的确是以她特有的方式爱你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in the/sb's ˈway</b></td><td>挡道；碍事</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>You'll have to move - you're in my way.<br>你得挪一挪，你挡我路了。!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep/stay out of sb's ˈway</b></td><td>避开某人；躲着某人</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He's got a lot of work to do at the moment, so ifl were you r'd stay out of his way until he's got it finished.<br>眼下他有很多工作要做，所以，如果我是你，我就离他远远的，等他把事情做完再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>look the other ˈway</b></td><td>视而不见；故意不管</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We only had three tickets but the woman at the door looked the other way and let all four of us in.<br>我们只有三张票，但是检票员装作没看见，把我们四个人都放进去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>lose your ˈway</b></td><td>迷路；迷失方向</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We lost our way in the dark.<br>我们在黑暗中迷路了。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a lot, not much, etc. in the way of sth</b></td><td>（某物）不少；不多</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The flat has a great view but not much in the way of storage.<br>这套公寓视野很好，但储物空间不多。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>the ˌother way aˈround/round</b></td><td>反过来；恰恰相反</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I think it should g0 on the other way round.<br>我想这应该反过来弄。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>out of the ˈway</b></td><td>不再碍事；已经处理完</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I moved my legs out of the way so that she could get past.<br>我挪开腿让她过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>out of your ˈway</b></td><td>不顺路；偏离既定路线</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Dropping me home is completely out of your way, I will take the bus.<br>送我回家太绕路了，我坐公交就行。（自拟）</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>ˈway back (informal)</b></td><td>很久以前</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Weve known each other since way back.<br>我们俩很久以前就认识了。 ></td></tr>

<tr><td><b>in ˌmore ways than ˈone</b></td><td>不止一层意思；在好几方面</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>She's a big woman, in more ways than one(= she is big in size, and also important or powerful).<br>她是一个“大”人物，在多个方面都很“大”(不仅体型大，而且权力大)。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌways and ˈmeans</b></td><td>方法和手段；门路</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>There are ways and means of getting tickets if you know the right people.<br>只要认识人，弄到票总有门路。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>fall by the ˈwayside</b></td><td>半途而废；被淘汰</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Half the class started Japanese, but most fell by the wayside by March.<br>班上一半人开始学日语，三月前大都半途而废了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌout/ˌup the waˈzoo (AmE, slang)</b></td><td>大量的；多得很</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>She's got awards up the wazoo.<br>她拿到了许多奖项。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/go ˌweak at the ˈknees (informal)</b></td><td>（因激动、疾病等）两腿发软</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He felt dizay and a bit weak at the knees.<br>他一阵头晕，两腿微微发软。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>wear the ˈtrousers (BrE) (AmE wear the ˈpants) (often disapproving)</b></td><td>（在家中）当家作主</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It's not difficult to see who wears the trousers in their house!<br>他们家里谁说了算，一眼就能看出来!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep a ˈweather eye on sth/open for sth</b></td><td>随时留意；小心提防</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Its difficulty, an ambassador's job to keep a weather eye open for any important political changes.<br>大使的职责就是随时留意重大的政治变革。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>ˈwing your/its way (to...)</b></td><td>快速前往；很快被送往</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>An invitation to the wedding will be winging its way to you very soon.<br>婚礼请柬很快就会到你手里。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(wait, stand, etc.) in the ˈwings</b></td><td>伺机而动；随时准备接替</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>If the party leader should there are plenty of other politicians reslgn, waiting in the wings.<br>如果该党的领袖辞职，很多政客都准备着填补这个空缺。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be onto a ˈwinner (informal)</b></td><td>稳操胜券；找到了赚钱的门路</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He is the sole importer of this product, and he certainly thinks he's onto a winner.<br>作为该产品唯一的进口商，他当然觉得销路一定很好。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wipe the ˈfloor with sb (informal)</b></td><td>彻底击败某人</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>They started arguing about the education reforms, and she wiped the floor with him.<br>他们就教育改革问题展开辩论， 结果她把他驳得哑口无言。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wipe sth off the ˈmap</b></td><td>把……从地球上抹去；彻底摧毁</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>If a meteor hit us, whole cities would be wiped off the face of the earth.<br>如果流星击中我们，整座城市都会毁灭。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wipe the slate ˈclean</b></td><td>既往不咎；一笔勾销</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>We're both to blame. Let's wipe the slate clean and start again.<br>我们俩都有错。让我们捐弃前嫌，重新开始吧。 ⑦</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wipe the/that ˈsmile, ˈgrin, etc. off sb's face</b></td><td>让某人笑不出来</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Wipe that smile off your face or I'll send you out of the classroom.<br>再笑我就把你赶出教室。 2</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go, come, etc. (right) down to the ˈwire</b></td><td>僵持到最后一刻才分胜负</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The election went right down to the wire, decided by a few hundred votes.<br>这场选举一直僵持到最后一刻，只靠几百票定胜负。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>down to the ˈwire (informal)</b></td><td>直到最后一刻；分秒必争</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The match went down to the wire, with a goal in the final minute.<br>这场比赛直到最后一刻才见分晓，终场前一分钟才进球。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>conventional/received ˈwisdom</b></td><td>常人之见；普遍看法</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>Conventional wisdom has it that riots only ever happen in big cities.<br>按</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in your, his, etc. (infinite) ˈwisdom</b></td><td>以其（无限的）智慧（含讽刺）</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>The government in its wisdom has decided to support the ban.<br>政府竟愚蠢到决定支持这项禁令。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be ˌwise after the eˈvent (often disapproving)</b></td><td>事后聪明；马后炮</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>It's easy to be wise after the event and say we should have sold earlier.<br>事后诸葛亮谁都会当，说什么当初该早点卖掉。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's no ˈgood (doing sth)</b></td><td>做……没有用；无济于事</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It's no good complaining now; the tickets are completely sold out.<br>现在抱怨也没用，票已经全卖光了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be/get ˈwise to sb/sth (informal)</b></td><td>识破；察觉；看穿</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>The neighbours finally got wise to his excuses about the missing rent.<br>邻居们终于识破了他关于欠租的种种借口。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put sb ˈwise (to sth) (informal)</b></td><td>告知；使某人明白</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>If Raquel hadn't have put me wise, I would have believed him.<br>假如拉克尔没有告诉我的话，我就相信他了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈwise guy (informal, disapproving, especially AmE)</b></td><td>自以为什么都懂的人</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Don't be a wise guy — just answer the question properly.<br>别自作聪明，好好回答问题。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not be any the ˈwiser</b></td><td>毫不知情；没人察觉</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>If we put the money back tonight, nobody will be any the wiser.<br>只要今晚把钱放回去，就没人会察觉。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(just) as you ˈwish (formal, especially BrE)</b></td><td>悉听尊便；如你所愿</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Just as you wish, sir — we can deliver the order on Friday instead.<br>悉听尊便，先生，我们可以改到周五送货。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I ˈwish! (spoken)</b></td><td>但愿如此（可惜不可能）</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>A week off in Italy? I wish! I'll be here doing paperwork.<br>去意大利休一周假？想得美！我还得在这儿做文书。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>the wish is father to the ˈthought (saying)</b></td><td>愿望是思想之父；一厢情愿</td><td>★<br>★★</td><td>He's sure the team will win, but the wish is father to the thought.<br>他笃定球队会赢，可惜愿望是思想之父，不过一厢情愿。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wish sb/sth ˈwell • wish sb/sth ˈill (formal)</b></td><td>祝某人顺利；希望某人倒霉</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Whatever our differences, I genuinely wish her well in the new job.<br>不管我们有什么分歧，我真心祝她新工作顺利。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wouldn't wish sth on my, your, etc. worst ˈenemy</b></td><td>连仇人也不希望遭此罪</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>That kind of back pain is something I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy.<br>那种背痛，我连最恨的人都不希望他遭这个罪。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>your wish is my comˈmand (humorous)</b></td><td>悉听阁下吩咐</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Coffee with two sugars? Your wish is my command, madam.<br>加两块糖的咖啡？遵命，悉听吩咐，夫人。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>if wishes were ˌhorses, beggars would ˈride (saying)</b></td><td>空想无用；愿望不等于现实</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>Dreaming of a yacht won't help — if wishes were horses, beggars would ride.<br>空想游艇没用，要是愿望能当马，乞丐早骑上了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌwishful ˈthinking</b></td><td>一厢情愿的想法</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Prices seem to have stopped rising in the shops, or is that just wishful thinking on my part?<br>商店里东西的价格好像不再上涨了，要不然就是我的一厢情愿？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>to ˈwit (old-fashioned, formal)</b></td><td>即；也就是说</td><td>★★<br>★</td><td>I told him I only spoke one foreign language, to wit French.<br>我告诉他我只会说一门外语，那就是法语。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be ˈwith sb (informal)</b></td><td>支持某人；与某人站在一起</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>We're with you all the way on this, whatever the committee decides.<br>不管委员会怎么决定，我们都全力支持你。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get ˈwith it (informal)</b></td><td>跟上时势；顺应潮流</td><td>★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>You never seem to know what's happening in the world around you. Time you got with it, Paul.<br>你好像从不关心身边的事。保罗，是该关注一下这</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>with ˈthat (written)</b></td><td>说完便；随即；紧接着</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>He muttered a few words of apology and with that he left.<br>他低声叽咕了几句道歉的话，然后就走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌwither on the ˈvine (formal)</b></td><td>逐渐消亡；无疾而终</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>He used to be so ambitious, but his ambition seems to have withered on the vine.<br>他曾经雄心勃勃，现在却心灰意冷。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be scared/bored ˈwitless (informal)</b></td><td>吓得魂不附体；无聊透顶</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Despite his reputation as a tough guy, he admits that he was scared witless' when he first arrived in New York.<br>他承认自己虽号称硬汉，但是刚到纽约时，几乎被 “吓破了胆” 。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be (a) ˈwitness to sth</b></td><td>目击；亲眼看见（某事发生）</td><td>★★★<br>★★</td><td>He has been witness to a terrible murder.<br>他目击了一起残忍的凶杀案。 2 (</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>bear/give ˈwitness (to sth)</b></td><td>为……作证；证明</td><td>★★<br>★★</td><td>The huge crowd bore witness to the popularity of this man.<br>蜂拥的人群证明这个人广受欢迎。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be at your ˈwits' end</b></td><td>束手无策；全然不知所措</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Ican't pay the bills, the bank won't lend me any money, and I don't know what to do -I'm at my wits' end.<br>我没法付账，银行也不肯贷款给我。我不知如何是好，有点无计可施。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>collect/gather your ˈwits</b></td><td>定下神来；保持镇静</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>After such a shock Ifound it difficult to gather my wits.<br>经此打击，我很难保持冷静。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>frighten/scare sb out of their ˈwits</b></td><td>把某人吓得魂飞魄散</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Iwas scared out of my wits when I looked out of the window and saw the aircraft's engine on fire.<br>当我看到窗外飞机的引擎失火时，吓得慌了神。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have/keep your ˈwits about you</b></td><td>保持机警；随机应变</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Mountanneering i dangerous, so you need to keep your wits about you.<br>登山是一项危险的运动，你必须时刻头脑清醒。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌwoe beˈtide sb (formal or humorous)</b></td><td>某人可要倒霉了</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Woe betide anyone who arrives late!<br>迟到的人将会遭殃!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep the ˈwolf from the door (informal)</b></td><td>勉强糊口；免于挨饿</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Their wages are just enough to keep the wolf from the door.<br>他们的工资仅够糊口。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a wolf in sheep's ˈclothing</b></td><td>披着羊皮的狼</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>That charming landlord turned out to be a wolf in sheep's clothing.<br>那个和气的房东原来是披着羊皮的狼。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>throw sb to the ˈwolves/ˈlions</b></td><td>置某人于险境而不顾</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>When he became politically unpopular the rest of his party just threw him to the wolves.<br>当他在政治上不再得势时，党内同僚便任其处于困境而不顾。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>I ˌshouldn't ˈwonder (if...) (informal)</b></td><td>我一点也不觉得奇怪；很可能</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It's paid for with stolen money, 1 shouldn't wonder.<br>这是用偷来的钱买的，对此我并不觉得奇怪。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's no/small/little ˈwonder (that)...</b></td><td>难怪；不足为奇</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>It's little wonder that she's tired, working twelve hours every single day.<br>她每天工作十二小时，累也不奇怪。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>it's a ˈwonder (that)... (especially spoken)</b></td><td>令人惊奇的是；真是奇迹</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Did you see the car after the crash? It's a wonder that they survived!<br>你看到那辆车碰撞后的样子了吗？神奇的是他们竟然活下来了!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>wonders will ˌnever ˈcease (spoken, usually ironic)</b></td><td>真是无奇不有；怪事年年有</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>He washed the dishes without being asked — wonders will never cease.<br>他没人催就把碗洗了，真是无奇不有。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>ˌno ˈwonder (that)...</b></td><td>难怪；怪不得</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>No wonder you're cold — you're standing there in a thin T-shirt.<br>怪不得你冷，就穿件薄T恤站在那儿。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>work/do ˈwonders/ˈmiracles (for/on/with sb/sth) (informal)</b></td><td>创造奇迹；产生奇效</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Getting the job did wonders for her self-confidence.<br>得到这份工作后，她自信心大增。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>a ˈmiracle-worker noun</b></td><td>能创造奇迹的人</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Sorry, I need more time — I'm a doctor, not a miracle-worker.<br>抱歉，我需要更多时间，我是医生，不是神仙。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not out of the ˈwood(s) (informal)</b></td><td>尚未摆脱困境；尚未渡过难关</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Our sales figures look much better this month, but we're not out of the woods yet.<br>我们这个月的销售额大有好转，但是我们仍未波过难关。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not see the ˌforest for the ˈtrees (informal)</b></td><td>见树不见林；只见细节不见全局</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The situation is so complex that many people are unable to see the wood for the trees.<br>情况如此复杂，许多人都是见树不见林，看不清大局。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>don't take any wooden ˈnickels (AmE)</b></td><td>请多保重；好好照顾自己</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>Well, see you around Tom. Don't take any wooden nickels.<br>好啦，汤姆，再见吧，请多保重。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>get, win, take, etc. the ˌwooden ˈspoon (BrE, informal)</b></td><td>获得最后一名；成为末名</td><td>★<br>★★★</td><td>England must win this match if they are to avoid taking the wooden spoon.<br>如果英格兰队不想垫底，就必须赢得这场比赛。 ②</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>blend/fade into the ˈwoodwork</b></td><td>销声匿迹；隐没不见</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>I decided the best thing to do would be to try and fade into the woodwork and hope that no one noticed me.<br>我认为最好的办法就是尽量销声匿迹，希望没人注意我。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>come/crawl out of the ˈwoodwork (informal, disapproving)</b></td><td>突然纷纷冒出来</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>As soon as he won the lottery, distant cousins came out of the woodwork.<br>他一中彩票，远房表亲就纷纷冒了出来。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be as ˌgood as your ˈword</b></td><td>守信用；说话算数</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>You'll find that she's as good as her word - she always comes if she says she will.<br>你会发现她很守信用；如果她说要来，一定会来。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>be a man/woman of his/her ˈword</b></td><td>守信用的人；说话算数的人</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>Ifhe said he'd help you, he willhe's a man of his word.<br>如果他说过要帮你，他一定会做到。因为他是一个守信之人。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>by ˌword of ˈmouth</b></td><td>口头上；口口相传</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>The news spread by word of mouth.<br>这消息是口头传开的。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(right) from the word ˈgo (informal)</b></td><td>从一开始</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I knew from the word go that it would be difficult.<br>我从一开始就知道这事难做。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(not) get a word in ˈedgeways (BrE) (AmE (not) get a word in ˈedgewise) (informal)</b></td><td>插不上嘴</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>I tried to tell him what I thought, but I couldn't get a word in edgeways.<br>我想跟他谈谈我的想法，但是根本插不上嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>give sb your ˈword (that...) • have sb's ˈword (that...)</b></td><td>向某人许诺；得到某人的保证</td><td>★★★<br>★★★</td><td>I give you my wora that Tll pay you tomorrow.<br>我保证，明天一定付钱给你。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>go ˌback on your ˈword</b></td><td>失约；食言</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>He said he wouldn't charge more than €150, but he went back on his word and gave me an invoice for €200.<br>他说费用不会超过 150 欧元，但是却出尔反尔，给我开了张 200欧元的发票。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a ˈword (with sb) (about sth)</b></td><td>（与某人）简短谈谈</td><td>★★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Can I have a word, Marie? It's about Jane.<br>玛丽，我能和你私下谈谈吗？是有关简的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>have a word in sb's ˈear (BrE)</b></td><td>与某人私下说几句</td><td>★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Can I have a word in your ear, John?<br>约翰，我能跟你单独谈谈吗？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>in a ˈword (spoken)</b></td><td>简言之；一句话；总之</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>In a word, the whole evening was an absolute disaster.<br>一句话，整个晚上糟透了。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>keep/break your ˈword</b></td><td>遵守诺言；食言</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Do you think shell break her word and tell everyone?<br>你觉得她会不会食言，把这事说出去？</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>your/the last/final ˈword (on/about sth)</b></td><td>最终的说法；最后决定</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★</td><td>That's my final word on the subject — we are not moving house.<br>这事我最后表个态：我们不搬家。（自拟）</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>leave ˈword (with sb)</b></td><td>（给某人）留言</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>He left word with his secretary about where to contact him if necessary.<br>他向秘书交代了一下必要时如何同他联系。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>(upon) my ˈword! (old-fashioned)</b></td><td>哎呀（表示惊奇）</td><td>★<br>★★★★</td><td>My word!That was quick!<br>天哪!真快!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not be the ˈword for it</b></td><td>用这个词形容还不够</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>Unkind isn't the word for it! I've never seen anyone treat an animal so cruelly!<br>用不友善来形容都不够!我从未见过有人如此残酷地对待动物!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not/never have a good word to ˈsay about/for sb/sth</b></td><td>从不说……的好话</td><td>★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>She rarely has a good word to say about her neighbours.<br>她极少说邻居的好话。</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>not a ˈword (to sb) (about sth)</b></td><td>只字不提；别透露半个字</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★★</td><td>Not a word to Jean about the party —it's a surprise!<br>别对琼提聚会的事，给她一个惊喜!</td></tr>
<tr><td><b>put in a (good) ˈword (for sb)</b></td><td>为某人说好话；替某人美言</td><td>★★★★<br>★★★★</td><td>If you put in a good word for me, I might get the job.<br>要是你为我美言几句，也许我就能得到这份工作。</td></tr>

<tr><td><b>your, his, etc. word is your, his, etc. ˈbond</b></td><td>一诺千金；言而有信</td><td>★★<br>★★★</td><td>Don't worry, you can trust my brother. His word's as good as his bond.<br>别担心，你完全可以相信我哥哥。他言出必行。</td></tr>
